identity.title: Entitlement qualification → grant, deny or pending
identity.purpose: Establish whether a right actually exists, as a state distinct from being eligible for one or having paid toward one.

requires: an authoritative basis for a right: a completed purchase, an activated plan, an assigned role, an earned benefit, an effective contract, or a satisfied policy condition
insufficientAlone: a payment authorised but not settled
eligibility for a plan nobody has bought
a marketing promise, which describes what we offer rather than what has been granted

nodes.headline: Entitlement basis evaluated or changed
Evaluate the authoritative basis - the record that establishes the right, not the process that led toward it. What matters is whether the business state confirms the grant, not how close it came
Does an entitlement already exist for this right at this scope?
Reconcile scope and validity against the existing grant rather than issuing a second one. Two grants for one right produce two expiries, two revocations and a state nobody can read
existing entitlement reconciled; no duplicate grant issued
nodes.detail: a further change to the basis re-opens this against the reconciled grant

nodes.headline: Are the requirements for this right satisfied?
PENDING_REQUIREMENT; the right is reachable and not yet held
nodes.detail: satisfying the named requirement re-opens this. Pending and denied are kept apart because the route back differs - one needs a step completed, the other needs the rules to change

nodes.headline: DENIED; the right is not available on this basis
nodes.detail: a different basis - a purchase, a role, a contract - is evaluated on its own terms

nodes.headline: Record GRANTED with the basis that established it, the scope it covers and its validity. Granting is idempotent - the same basis arriving twice grants once
Entitlement grant → provision → verify availability
nodes.detail: a right being established

edges.label: Already held
edges.when: a prior grant covers the same right and scope

edges.label: New
edges.when: no existing grant covers it

edges.label: Satisfied
edges.when: the authoritative basis establishes the right

edges.label: A named requirement is outstanding
edges.when: the right is available in principle and something specific has not been met yet

edges.label: Not available
edges.when: the requirements cannot be met for this account - a structural exclusion rather than a missing step
a right being established

distinctFrom.because: Eligibility asks whether the rules would permit this. Entitlement asks whether it has been granted. ACQ-06's own guardrail names the difference; this journey is the state on the other side of it.

guardrails: Eligibility is not entitlement. Being permitted to have something is not having it.
A payment attempt is not an entitlement. Authorised is not settled, and settled is what establishes the right.
A marketing promise is not a granted right unless an authoritative business state confirms it.
An existing entitlement is reconciled, never duplicated.

Qualified but capacity-blocked is pending rather than denied. Somebody who met every requirement and arrived when the allocation was full has not been refused, and recording it as a denial closes a case that policy may reopen with a waitlist or a later grant.
governance.reusableRule: Entitlement represents an established right to a defined capability or benefit, not merely eligibility to receive it.
governance.entityScope: the person or account plus the specific entitlement, at its own scope and validity
governance.entityNote: One entitlement per right per scope. A second grant for the same right produces two expiries and two revocations, which is why an existing one is reconciled rather than duplicated.

identity.title: Entitlement grant → provision → verify availability
identity.purpose: Hold the distance between a right being granted and the thing behind it actually working.

requires: an entitlement recorded as GRANTED with a scope that implies a resource

nodes.headline: Entitlement granted

Create the provisioning action and record the state as PROVISIONING, keyed so that a redelivered event provisions once. A granted entitlement in PROVISIONING is not yet usable, and nothing downstream may present it as though it were
until provisioning succeeds, or provisioning fails
nodes.detail: timeout after the provisioning SLA

nodes.headline: How did provisioning end?
Does actual availability need to be verified?

Check that the capability is genuinely reachable by its holder. A provisioning API returning success is a statement about the API - whether anyone can use the thing is a separate question with its own answer
Is it actually available?
ACTIVE; the right is granted, provisioned and usable
nodes.detail: a scope change re-opens provisioning for the delta rather than for the whole entitlement

nodes.headline: external:access-recovery
nodes.detail: a provisioned resource the holder cannot reach

nodes.headline: What class of failure is this?
Retry against a budget fixed at the first failure. The budget does not renew - that is the difference between a retry policy and a loop that provisions forever
Responsibility escalation → higher authority → resolution or return
nodes.detail: provisioning that cannot be completed automatically

edges.label: on event
edges.when: provisioning succeeds, provisioning fails

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a provisioning run that has neither succeeded nor failed within its SLA is a failure that has not reported itself, and treating silence as success is how a customer finds the gap first

edges.label: Succeeded
edges.when: the provisioning system reports success

edges.label: Failed
edges.when: the provisioning system reports failure

edges.label: Verification matters
edges.when: the holder's ability to reach the capability is what the entitlement is for, and a reported success is not proof of it

edges.label: The provisioning record is authoritative
edges.when: the provisioning system is itself the source of truth for availability

edges.label: Available
edges.when: the capability is reachable

edges.label: Provisioned but unreachable
edges.when: the resource exists and the holder still cannot use it
a provisioned resource the holder cannot reach

edges.label: Transient and retry-safe
edges.when: the failure is expected to clear and the retry budget has room

edges.label: Permanent, or the budget is spent
edges.when: retrying will not help, or has already been tried as often as the budget allows
provisioning that cannot be completed automatically

guardrails: A granted entitlement is not a provisioned one. The grant is a business record; provisioning is a distributed operation that can fail on its own.
Provisioning success is not availability. Where the difference matters, availability is checked rather than assumed.
Provisioning is idempotent. Redelivery provisions once.
Retries are bounded by a budget fixed at the first failure.
governance.reusableRule: A granted right becomes usable only after the required resource or capability is successfully provisioned and available.
governance.entityScope: the entitlement plus the resource or capability being provisioned for it
governance.entityNote: One provisioning run per entitlement, keyed idempotently. Retries and redeliveries are expected, and none of them may provision a second copy.

identity.title: Entitlement change → recalculate scope → expand, reduce or preserve
identity.purpose: Apply only the difference between the old and new rights, rather than re-applying a whole scope over a working one.

requires: an authoritative change to the basis of an existing entitlement: a plan change, a role change, a contract amendment, a benefit or quantity or coverage change

nodes.headline: Entitlement basis changed
Compare the previous scope, the new scope and the effective time, and derive the delta. What gets applied is the difference - a capability present in both scopes is not touched at all
Which way did the scope move?
Provision the newly granted capabilities, idempotently, and leave everything already working untouched

Apply any expansion, and identify precisely which capabilities are no longer covered. Historical data and resources created under the previous scope are not destroyed by a scope change - a reduction removes a right, not a record
Do existing commitments or in-flight usage depend on what is being removed?
Entitlement loss → revoke future capability → reconcile existing obligations
nodes.detail: a scope reduction with live commitments underneath it

nodes.headline: Apply the reduction to future access only, idempotently. Future access loss and cancelling an existing obligation are two different decisions, and this one makes only the first
delta applied; unchanged capabilities untouched
nodes.detail: a further basis change is compared against the new scope

edges.label: Expanded only
edges.when: capabilities were added and none removed

edges.label: Reduced, or mixed
edges.when: at least one capability is no longer covered, whether or not others were added

edges.label: Something depends on it
edges.when: a confirmed reservation, an in-progress service, a purchased benefit or an open transaction rests on the capability being removed

edges.label: Nothing depends on it
edges.when: the reduction affects only future use
a scope reduction with live commitments underneath it

guardrails: A reduction in entitlement does not destroy historical data or resources created while the right was held.
Future access loss and cancelling an existing obligation are separate decisions made by separate journeys.
The delta is applied idempotently, so a redelivered change does not reprovision or re-revoke.
governance.reusableRule: Entitlement changes should apply the difference between old and new rights without rewriting the history of what was previously valid.
governance.entityScope: the entitlement whose basis changed, and the delta between its previous and new scope
governance.entityNote: The delta is the unit of work. Re-applying the full new scope reprovisions what already worked and revokes what should have survived, and the holder sees both as an outage.

identity.title: Entitlement loss → revoke future capability → reconcile existing obligations
identity.purpose: Stop future use of a right that has ended without cancelling what was validly created while it was held.

requires: an authoritative end to a right: a plan downgrade, a contract termination, a role removal, a benefit expiry, an eligibility-linked revocation, or a policy decision

nodes.headline: Entitlement no longer valid

Determine when the loss actually takes effect - immediately, at period end, or on a future date. Assuming immediate is how someone loses what they have already paid for, and everything downstream depends on getting this right
Identify the capabilities affected, scoped to this entitlement alone. A lost role does not revoke rights the same person holds on a different basis

Prevent future use of the affected capabilities from the effective time, idempotently. The record that the entitlement existed and what was done under it is untouched - losing a right does not mean it was never held
Do valid commitments exist that were created while the right was held?
external:commitment-reconciliation
nodes.detail: an entitlement ending with commitments still live under it

nodes.headline: Does a provisioned resource need removing?
Deprovision request → dependency check → remove, retain or escalate
nodes.detail: a provisioned resource whose entitlement has ended

nodes.headline: future use revoked; history and commitments intact
nodes.detail: the right may be granted again on a new basis, which is a new entitlement rather than a revival of this one

edges.label: Commitments outstanding
edges.when: a confirmed reservation, an in-progress service, an already purchased benefit or an open transaction exists

edges.label: Nothing outstanding
edges.when: the right governed only future use
an entitlement ending with commitments still live under it

edges.label: Resource provisioned
edges.when: something was provisioned for this entitlement and is no longer authorised

edges.label: Nothing provisioned
edges.when: the right had no provisioned resource behind it
a provisioned resource whose entitlement has ended

distinctFrom.because: Suspension restricts a right that still exists and is designed to come back. This is the right ending, which is why it reconciles obligations rather than holding them.

guardrails: Losing an entitlement does not mean the entitlement never existed. The historical record stands.
Existing commitments are reconciled separately and are never cancelled automatically by the loss.
Revocation stays scoped to the affected entitlement.
Stopping future use is idempotent.
governance.reusableRule: Losing a right prevents future unauthorized use but does not automatically erase commitments created while the right was valid.
governance.entityScope: the entitlement that ended, plus the resources and commitments that depended on it
governance.entityNote: Revocation stays scoped to this entitlement. A right held on another basis is untouched, and the record that this one existed remains.

identity.title: Access request → authorization check → allow, deny or step up
identity.purpose: Decide at the moment of the attempt whether this actor may take this action on this resource.

requires: an actor attempting a protected action on an identified resource
insufficientAlone: a successful authentication, which establishes who is asking and nothing about what they may do
holding an entitlement to the product the resource belongs to

nodes.headline: Protected action attempted

Evaluate at execution time: the identity, the entitlement, the role and permission, the resource's own scope, the current security state, and the policy requirements for this specific action. A cached decision is re-checked against critical state, because the states that matter most are the ones that change fastest
What does the current state permit?
ALLOW; this action on this resource, now
nodes.detail: the next attempt is decided again. Allowing one action never authorises the following one, however similar it looks

nodes.headline: Step-up requirement → stronger authentication → resume or deny
nodes.detail: an action requiring an assurance level the current session does not hold

nodes.headline: Record the denial with its reason category - entitlement missing, permission missing, resource out of scope, security state blocking, or policy prohibition. A bare denial cannot be appealed, debugged, or distinguished from an outage
DENY, with a recorded reason category
nodes.detail: a change to any of the evaluated states makes the next attempt a new decision

edges.label: Fully authorized
edges.when: every required condition is satisfied for this actor, action and resource

edges.label: Authorized subject to stronger verification
edges.when: the conditions are met except for an assurance level this action requires

edges.label: Not authorized
edges.when: at least one required condition fails
an action requiring an assurance level the current session does not hold

distinctFrom.because: Approval is a business decision taken in advance about a subject. Authorization is a runtime decision taken at the moment of the attempt, and being approved for something does not authorise every action within it.

guardrails: Entitlement to a product is not permission for every action within it.
Authentication success is not authorization. The two answer different questions.
A cached authorization respects current critical state changes rather than the state at the time it was cached.
Every denial carries a reason category.
governance.reusableRule: Access should be granted only when the current actor, resource and action satisfy the required authorization conditions at execution time.
governance.entityScope: the individual access request - one actor, one action, one resource
governance.entityNote: The decision belongs to the request. Allowing one action says nothing about the next, and a cached decision is re-checked against critical state that may have moved since.

identity.title: Credential issued → activate → use, expire or revoke
identity.purpose: Run an access artifact through its own validity lifecycle, separately from the right it represents.

requires: a credential issued with an owner, a scope and a validity

nodes.headline: Credential issued
Store the credential id, owner, scope, issue time, validity, whether activation is required, and its status as ISSUED. Issued is not active, and nothing may present it as usable until it is
Does this credential require activation before use?
until the credential is activated, or the credential is revoked before activation
nodes.detail: timeout after the activation window

nodes.headline: What happened during the activation window?
Expire the credential unactivated, recording that it was never claimed. An expired-unactivated credential and an expired-active one are different facts about how the artifact was used
EXPIRED, never activated
nodes.detail: a replacement credential is issued as a new artifact with its own id and lifecycle

nodes.headline: Record the credential as ACTIVE for its scope and validity
until a revocation event, or a replacement credential is issued
nodes.detail: timeout after the credential's validity end

nodes.headline: What ended the credential's active life?
REPLACED; this artifact is no longer usable
nodes.detail: the replacement runs its own lifecycle. This one is never reactivated, whatever happens to the replacement

nodes.headline: Credential compromise or revocation → disable → replace or re-authenticate
nodes.detail: a credential being revoked

nodes.headline: Re-read the credential's current version before expiring it. An extension or a replacement may have moved its validity since this timer was written, and expiring on the remembered value would undo a later decision
Does the current version still expire now?
Record the credential as EXPIRED. Expired is not revoked - the artifact reached the end of its validity rather than being withdrawn, and the two mean different things to anyone investigating later
EXPIRED after active use
nodes.detail: the entitlement behind it may still be perfectly valid; a new credential is issued for it rather than this one being revived

nodes.headline: expiry superseded by an extension or replacement
nodes.detail: the current validity governs, and its own end executes when it arrives

edges.label: Activation required
edges.when: policy requires the holder to activate it

edges.label: Active on issue
edges.when: policy makes it usable as issued

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the credential is activated, the credential is revoked before activation

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: an unactivated credential does not become active by waiting, and leaving it ISSUED indefinitely keeps a usable artifact alive that nobody ever claimed

edges.label: Activated
edges.when: the holder activated it

edges.label: Revoked first
edges.when: a revocation arrived before activation

edges.label: on event
edges.when: a revocation event, a replacement credential is issued

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: validity ending is the ordinary path; the wait is watching for the two things that can end it sooner

edges.label: Revoked
edges.when: an authoritative revocation arrived

edges.label: Replaced
edges.when: a replacement credential was issued for the same purpose
a credential being revoked

edges.label: Still expiring
edges.when: the current validity ends at this moment

edges.label: Validity moved
edges.when: an extension or replacement changed it

distinctFrom.because: The entitlement is the right. The credential is an artifact that presents it. Treating the artifact as the right means revoking a token looks like removing a benefit.

guardrails: A credential issued is not a credential active.
Credential validity is not entitlement validity. Either can end while the other holds.
A revoked credential is never restored by a stale activation or refresh event.
Expiry re-reads the current version before applying, so an extension is not undone by an older timer.
governance.reusableRule: Credentials are access artifacts with their own validity lifecycle and should not be treated as the entitlement they represent.
governance.entityScope: the individual credential - its id, owner, scope and validity
governance.entityNote: A credential's validity is its own. It can be valid while the entitlement behind it has lapsed, and revoked while that entitlement is perfectly live.

identity.title: Credential compromise or revocation → disable → replace or re-authenticate
identity.purpose: Take a credential out of use immediately, and let any replacement come through its own authorised path.

requires: a requirement to revoke: suspected or confirmed compromise, a manual revoke, a password or security reset, a device removed, access terminated, or a token invalidation

nodes.headline: Authoritative revocation requirement

Determine which credentials are actually affected. One compromised artifact does not revoke unrelated ones unless policy says the compromise implies them - over-revoking on a suspicion locks people out of things that were never at risk, and the lockout becomes the incident

Revoke the affected credentials immediately, ahead of everything else in this journey. Security revocation takes precedence over queued access actions - an artifact invalidated at ten o'clock must not still authorise a request queued at one minute to
Invalidate the refresh and activation operations tied to the revoked credentials, so nothing in flight can bring one back after it has been withdrawn
Is a replacement allowed?
revoked; no replacement issued
nodes.detail: a new credential requires the entitlement and the authorisation to be established again, which is a different journey and not a continuation of this one

nodes.headline: Does issuing a replacement require verification first?
Authentication challenge → authenticate, step up or deny
nodes.detail: a replacement requiring identity or control to be re-established

nodes.headline: Issue a replacement as a new credential with its own id and its own lifecycle. The revoked artifact is never reactivated - a replacement replaces, and reusing the old identifier would make the revocation unverifiable
Credential issued → activate → use, expire or revoke
nodes.detail: a replacement credential being issued

edges.label: Replacement permitted
edges.when: the owner remains entitled and policy allows re-issuing

edges.label: No replacement
edges.when: access is being removed, or the owner is no longer entitled

edges.label: Verification required
edges.when: the revocation reason means the requester's identity or control has to be re-established

edges.label: No verification needed
edges.when: the revocation was routine and the owner's identity is not in question
a replacement requiring identity or control to be re-established
a replacement credential being issued

guardrails: One credential compromise does not automatically revoke unrelated credentials unless policy requires it.
A replacement never reactivates the revoked credential. It is a new artifact.
Security revocation takes precedence over queued access actions, including refresh and activation already in flight.
governance.reusableRule: Credential revocation should immediately invalidate the affected access artifact while replacement follows an independently authorized path.
governance.entityScope: the specific credentials affected, and their owner
governance.entityNote: Scope is the whole question. One compromised artifact does not implicate unrelated ones unless policy says the compromise reaches them.

identity.title: Access suspension → restricted state → restore or terminate
identity.purpose: Restrict defined capabilities for a reason, in the smallest scope that addresses it, while keeping restoration genuinely possible.

requires: a decision to suspend for a stated reason: a payment state, a security review, a policy review, a temporary operational restriction, or an administrative hold
insufficientAlone: an outage, which removes access without anyone deciding to

nodes.headline: Authoritative suspension decision

Record the reason, the scope, when it takes effect, which capabilities are blocked, which continue, and what would end it. The scope is the smallest that addresses the reason - a payment problem does not justify blocking a security setting, and over-broad restriction makes the restriction itself the incident
Does anything remain accessible?
Leave the unaffected capabilities working, so the state is legible as a suspension rather than as an outage - and so the holder can still do the thing that would resolve it
Record a full suspension within the affected scope, with the same review condition. Full is still not terminal, and the record says so
until the suspension reason is resolved, or a terminal decision is made
nodes.detail: timeout after the review point or the recorded expiry

nodes.headline: How was it resolved?
At the review point with nothing resolved, what now?

Record the extension as its own suspension instance with a new review point, so the number of times someone has been suspended without a decision stays countable rather than hidden inside one long record
suspension extended; a new instance carries the new review point
nodes.detail: the extension runs as its own instance with its own end

nodes.headline: Capability restoration → revalidate → restore safely
nodes.detail: a suspension ending without a terminal decision

nodes.headline: Entitlement loss → revoke future capability → reconcile existing obligations
nodes.detail: a review concluding that the right should end

nodes.headline: Responsibility escalation → higher authority → resolution or return
nodes.detail: a suspension review point reached with no decision

edges.label: Partial
edges.when: capabilities outside the reason's scope are unaffected

edges.label: Full
edges.when: the reason justifies blocking everything in scope

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the suspension reason is resolved, a terminal decision is made

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a suspension with no review is a termination that nobody had to authorise, and the review is what keeps the two apart

edges.label: Reason resolved
edges.when: what justified the suspension has been dealt with

edges.label: Terminal decision
edges.when: the review concluded that the right should end rather than resume

edges.label: Extend with a new end
edges.when: the reason still holds and policy allows a further period

edges.label: Lift it
edges.when: the reason has lapsed even though nothing formally resolved it

edges.label: Nobody decided
edges.when: the review point arrived with no decision made at all
a suspension ending without a terminal decision
a review concluding that the right should end
a suspension review point reached with no decision

distinctFrom.because: Grace continues a right whose validity has ended. Suspension restricts a right that is still valid. One is continuity after an ending; the other is a hold before one.

guardrails: Suspended is not terminated. Suspension is designed to be reversible and its record says so.
The suspension uses the smallest scope that addresses its reason.
Restoration does not blindly return every previous capability - it hands to a journey whose job is revalidating first.
A suspension without a review point is a termination nobody authorised.
governance.reusableRule: Suspension temporarily restricts defined capabilities while preserving the possibility of restoration after current eligibility and authority are revalidated.
governance.entityScope: the account or person plus the specific capability scope being restricted
governance.entityNote: The scope is recorded rather than implied. Anything reading the account has to be able to tell which capabilities are blocked and which still work.

identity.title: Capability restoration → revalidate → restore safely
identity.purpose: Rebuild access from what is currently valid, rather than replaying the capability set someone used to have.

requires: the condition that removed or restricted access appearing to be resolved
insufficientAlone: time passing on a restriction whose reason was never addressed

nodes.headline: Restoration condition satisfied

Re-evaluate every current requirement independently: the entitlement, the authorization, the security state, the policy state, the credential's own validity, and whether the resource still exists. Each is read now rather than taken from the snapshot captured when access was removed
How much of the previous capability set is currently valid?
Restore the affected capabilities and invalidate the restriction actions that are now obsolete

Restore only the subset that is currently valid, and invalidate the obsolete restriction actions for it. Expired credentials, withdrawn permissions, lapsed entitlements, deleted resources and roles that no longer exist are not resurrected - each ended for its own reason, and restoring access never addressed any of them. What is not restored is named, so the holder can ask about it rather than discover it
capabilities restored against current valid state
nodes.detail: a further restriction and restoration is its own cycle

nodes.headline: partially restored; what did not return is named
nodes.detail: each capability not restored re-enters when its own requirement is met - the subset that is missing is a list rather than a vague sense that something is wrong

nodes.headline: still restricted; nothing currently qualifies for restoration
nodes.detail: previous access is not a current access right, and regaining it means meeting the requirements now rather than having met them before

edges.label: All of it
edges.when: every requirement for every affected capability is satisfied now

edges.label: Some of it
edges.when: part of the set is currently valid and part is not

edges.label: None of it
edges.when: no affected capability meets its current requirements

distinctFrom.because: TIM-68 reverses a transition within a window and asks what side effects can be undone. This rebuilds a capability set from scratch against current conditions, with no assumption that the previous set is the target.

guardrails: Previous access is not a current access right.
Restoration never resurrects expired credentials, withdrawn permissions, expired entitlements, deleted resources or obsolete roles.
Obsolete restriction actions are invalidated as part of restoring, not left to fire afterwards.
A partial restoration names what did not come back.
governance.reusableRule: Capability restoration should reconstruct access from current valid state rather than rewind the system to a historical snapshot.
governance.entityScope: the person or account plus each capability being considered for restoration
governance.entityNote: Each capability is judged on its own current requirements. Restoration is not one decision but as many as there are capabilities.

identity.title: Deprovision request → dependency check → remove, retain or escalate
identity.purpose: Remove a capability that is no longer authorised, after establishing that nothing still depends on the thing being removed.

requires: a valid requirement to deprovision: an entitlement ended, an account closed, a role removed, a contract terminated, or a resource explicitly removed
insufficientAlone: a period of non-use, which is not an authorisation to remove anything

nodes.headline: Deprovisioning requirement
Identify the provisioned resources affected, and which of them are shared with anything still entitled
What still depends on these resources?
retained; another entitlement still depends on it
nodes.detail: when the last entitlement to the shared resource ends, removal is evaluated again. Removing it now would take it from everyone else who is still entitled

nodes.headline: until the dependent commitment completes
nodes.detail: timeout after the horizon appropriate to the dependent commitment

nodes.headline: external:data-transfer-or-termination
nodes.detail: removal requiring an export, handover or defined termination process first

nodes.headline: Deprovision idempotently. This removes the capability, not the record of it - historical and audit data is governed by its own retention and deletion lifecycle, and a deprovision that deletes it has performed an irreversible action nobody authorised
until deprovisioning succeeds, or deprovisioning fails
nodes.detail: timeout after the deprovisioning SLA

nodes.headline: How did it end?
Does the access consequence matter enough to verify?
Confirm the capability is genuinely no longer available. A deprovisioning API returning success is a statement about the API, and the question here is whether anyone can still get in
capability removed; records and audit data untouched
nodes.detail: re-provisioning follows a new entitlement rather than an undo. Deleting the retained data is a separate lifecycle with its own authorisation

nodes.headline: Is this failure retry-safe within the budget?
Retry against the budget fixed at the first failure, idempotently, so a partially completed removal is completed rather than restarted
Responsibility escalation → higher authority → resolution or return
nodes.detail: a capability that could not be removed

edges.label: Shared with a live entitlement
edges.when: another holder is still entitled to the same resource

edges.label: A commitment must complete first
edges.when: an in-progress service or open transaction needs the resource until it finishes

edges.label: Data transfer or a special process applies
edges.when: an export, a handover or a defined termination process has to run before removal

edges.label: Nothing depends on it
edges.when: the resource serves only the entitlement that ended

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the dependent commitment completes

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a dependency that never clears leaves an unauthorised capability alive indefinitely, which is the failure deprovisioning exists to prevent
removal requiring an export, handover or defined termination process first

edges.label: on event
edges.when: deprovisioning succeeds, deprovisioning fails

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: silence is not success, and an unauthorised capability that may still be live is worth escalating rather than assuming away

edges.label: Succeeded
edges.when: the system reports the resource removed

edges.label: Failed
edges.when: the system reports a failure

edges.label: Verify it
edges.when: continued access would be a real problem, which is the usual case for anything security-relevant

edges.label: The removal record is sufficient
edges.when: the deprovisioning system is authoritative for whether the capability exists

edges.label: Retry
edges.when: the failure is transient and the budget fixed at the first attempt has room

edges.label: Escalate
edges.when: the failure is permanent, or the budget is spent
a capability that could not be removed

distinctFrom.because: ACC-74 ends a right and stops future use. This removes the technical resource behind it, which is a separate operation with its own failure modes and its own reasons to wait.

guardrails: An entitlement ending is not an authorisation for destructive deletion.
Deprovisioning does not delete historical or audit data. That is a separate lifecycle with separate authorisation.
Shared resource dependencies are checked before removal.
Where the access consequence matters, technical success is verified rather than assumed.
Deprovisioning is idempotent, so a retry completes a partial removal rather than restarting it.
governance.reusableRule: Deprovisioning removes no-longer-authorized capability only after active dependencies and retention obligations have been reconciled.
governance.entityScope: the provisioned resource or capability, and the entitlement whose end triggered its removal
governance.entityNote: The resource is the entity, not the entitlement. A shared resource outlives any single right to it, which is why dependency is checked before anything is removed.

identity.title: Anonymous intent → known identity → qualified entry
identity.purpose: Carry a meaningful but anonymous intent signal through identity resolution without inventing an identity, and decide lifecycle entry as a question separate from having resolved one.

requires: repeated visits to high-intent pages
interaction with pricing
product or configuration exploration
a meaningful return after a first session
insufficientAlone: a single page view
one session with no return
an ad click that landed and bounced

identity.title: First value milestone → recognition → next meaningful action

insufficientAlone: a login
a page view
a completed onboarding checklist
an opened or clicked message

nodes.headline: Authoritative first value event

Acknowledge what was actually produced, in the terms of the thing itself. Recognition that names nothing real is the failure mode here - it reads as manufactured, and it devalues the milestones that follow
Does a natural next action follow from what they just did?
Surface one relevant next action, drawn from what they produced rather than from the product's feature list
Early adoption → usage depth → habit or stable use
nodes.detail: first value produced

edges.label: Yes

edges.label: No
edges.when: nothing genuinely follows, and inventing a next step would turn recognition into a pitch
first value produced

distinctFrom.because: The same event can drive both, and they do opposite work. ACT-16 stops what onboarding still had queued; this one speaks to the person about what they just did.

guardrails: A login is not first value. A page view is not first value. The product has to have produced something.
Recognition names the real thing or is not sent. Celebration with nothing behind it costs more than silence.
The milestone has to matter to the person, not only to our funnel. A step that is significant only internally is not a milestone to congratulate anyone for.
governance.reusableRule: The first-value milestone marks the transition from learning how to use something to receiving value from it.
governance.entityScope: person or account plus the product or service context the value was produced in
governance.entityNote: First value is per context. A first report in one workspace is not first value in another the same account also holds.

identity.title: Activation achieved → stop onboarding → adoption handoff

requires: the product's own record that core value was produced
insufficientAlone: a click on an onboarding email
a completed setup checklist
a login
a feature opened but not used to any end

nodes.headline: Authoritative core activation event
Did this come from the product's record of value produced?
no activation recorded; onboarding continues untouched
nodes.detail: the real event, when it happens, arrives from the product and opens a proper instance

nodes.headline: Mark the onboarding objective complete, recording which event satisfied it - so a later question about when this account activated has one answer rather than an inference

Invalidate what onboarding still has outstanding: remaining setup reminders, onboarding calls to action, incomplete-step messages that are no longer true, and assistance prompts whose purpose has just disappeared - including everything already queued

nodes.headline: Authoritative business event

Evaluate the event type, the recipient, whether a communication requirement actually exists for it, the purpose, the urgency, the entity's current state, any equivalent communication already outstanding, and the applicable communication rules
Does a communication requirement exist for this event and this recipient?
Record that no obligation was created, and why. Every event generating a message is how people learn to ignore all of them, and then the one that mattered arrives in a stream nobody opens
no communication obligation; the event stands on its own
nodes.detail: a later event may create an obligation on its own terms. This one creating none is a decision recorded rather than a gap

nodes.headline: Is an equivalent communication already outstanding for this recipient?

Update the existing obligation rather than creating a second. A duplicate event producing a duplicate message means the recipient is told twice about one thing, and the second telling makes them doubt the first
folded into the outstanding obligation; no second message was created
nodes.detail: if that obligation closes with this event still uncommunicated, the requirement is assessed again on its own terms

nodes.headline: Create the communication obligation with its purpose, its recipient, the outcome it requires and the window in which it stays relevant. The obligation is a separate entity from the event - communication rules describe what happened and never redefine it
Communication obligation → resolve recipient → ready, hold or fail
nodes.detail: a communication obligation created

edges.label: It exists
edges.when: a rule, a contract or a defined expectation says this recipient is owed a message about this

edges.label: None
edges.when: nothing requires telling this recipient about this event

edges.label: One exists and can absorb this
edges.when: an unresolved obligation covers the same subject and the semantics permit updating it

edges.label: None, or it cannot be merged
edges.when: nothing outstanding covers it, or the two are genuinely different messages
a communication obligation created

distinctFrom.because: FBK-41 decides whether it is appropriate to ask somebody for something. This decides whether a business event creates an obligation to tell somebody something - the requirement comes from the event and the rules, not from the recipient's receptiveness.

guardrails: An event occurring is not a message being required.
Communication rules never redefine business truth.
Duplicate events do not create duplicate communication obligations.

A repeated attempt at the same obligation is bounded by the distinct approaches actually available to it. When those are exhausted, sustained non-engagement is a permission question rather than a reason for one more send.

Delivery and engagement patterns may suggest different diagnostic hypotheses about why an attempt did not land - the envelope, the message, or the friction after it. They are hypotheses rather than facts: the rule they support is not to repeat the same intervention blindly, and communication telemetry is never treated as causal proof of any of them.
governance.reusableRule: Business events create communication only when an explicit communication requirement exists for the current recipient and state.
governance.entityScope: the business event, the recipient it concerns, and the communication obligation it may create
governance.entityNote: The obligation is a separate entity from the event. It carries its own purpose, its own required outcome and its own relevance window.

identity.title: Communication obligation → resolve recipient → ready, hold or fail
identity.purpose: Establish who is actually owed this, and where they can currently be reached.

requires: a communication obligation with a stated purpose and required outcome

nodes.headline: Communication obligation awaiting recipient

Resolve the authoritative recipient identity. The account owner is not always the intended recipient - a workspace notice may be owed to an administrator, a policy notice to a legal contact, and a security alert to the person whose credential it concerns rather than to whoever pays the bill
Is the intended recipient resolvable?

Record RECIPIENT_UNRESOLVED and send nothing. Falling back to whoever is on the account because nobody else could be found delivers a private matter to the wrong person, and that cannot be undone by a correction
RECIPIENT_UNRESOLVED; the obligation stands unmet and nothing was sent
nodes.detail: the recipient becoming resolvable reopens the routing. The obligation has not lapsed and has not been met

nodes.headline: Does this recipient resolve through a role rather than a named person?

Resolve the current holder of the role rather than whoever held it when the record was written. A notice sent to last year's administrator is a notice nobody received, and on a shared or team entity that is the normal case rather than the edge one
Resolve the named party as the obligation identifies them

Resolve the currently valid destination candidates - email, phone, device, in-app account, workspace or any other supported destination. Currently valid means the destination's own health, not merely its presence: an address in the record that has been hard-bouncing for six months is not a route
Is at least one valid destination available?
Record CONTACT_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE for this recipient. This is a routing fact rather than a statement that the recipient is unreachable in general, and it is scoped to what was actually tried
CONTACT_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE; the obligation stands unmet
nodes.detail: a newly valid destination reopens the routing for this obligation while it is still relevant

nodes.headline: Does reaching this recipient at these destinations require further verification or authorization?

Record HOLD naming what is required, and raise the verification through the mechanism that owns it. A notice containing something sensitive is not sent to an unverified destination merely because the destination exists
until the required verification or authorization completes, or it is refused or cannot be completed
nodes.detail: timeout after the window in which the communication stays relevant

nodes.headline: How did the authorization resolve?
Record READY_FOR_CHANNEL_SELECTION with the resolved recipient and the destinations that are currently valid for them
Communication purpose → permission and preference check → allow, suppress or alternate
nodes.detail: a resolved recipient with usable destinations

edges.label: Resolved
edges.when: the party the obligation is owed to is authoritatively identified

edges.label: Unresolved
edges.when: who this is owed to cannot be established

edges.label: Through a role
edges.when: the obligation is owed to whoever holds a position - an administrator, an approver, a compliance contact

edges.label: A named party
edges.when: the obligation is owed to a specific person or entity

edges.label: Available
edges.when: one or more destinations are currently usable

edges.label: None
edges.when: no destination for this recipient is currently valid

edges.label: It does
edges.when: the content is sensitive enough that the destination must be verified first

edges.label: It does not
edges.when: the destinations are already adequate for this content

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the required verification or authorization completes, it is refused or cannot be completed

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a message held past its own relevance is worse than one never sent - it arrives about something that has already resolved

edges.label: Completed
edges.when: the destination is now adequate for this content

edges.label: Refused or impossible
edges.when: the destination cannot be made adequate
a resolved recipient with usable destinations

guardrails: An account owner is not always the intended recipient.
A destination is never used merely because it exists historically.
Shared and team entities resolve recipients by current role rather than by stored name.

Where policy marks the data sensitive, a channel that renders externally - a lock screen, a notification preview, a shared device - carries a generic notification and no concrete detail. The specifics live behind the authenticated experience instead.
A destination that is internal work rather than a route to the person - a queue, a task, a sales assignment - is never counted as a way of reaching them.
governance.reusableRule: Communication should proceed only after the intended recipient and a currently valid destination have been authoritatively resolved.
governance.entityScope: the communication obligation and the recipient with their candidate destinations
governance.entityNote: Two resolutions, in order: who, then where. A destination found without establishing who it belongs to sends a private matter to whoever is on file.

identity.title: Communication purpose → permission and preference check → allow, suppress or alternate
identity.purpose: Decide whether a working destination may carry this particular message, given what it is for.

requires: a resolved recipient with candidate destinations and an obligation with a purpose

nodes.headline: Recipient and destinations resolved

Classify the communication's purpose - transactional, security, service, a mandatory notice, operational, marketing, or another defined purpose. The purpose decides which permission rules apply, and misclassifying it is what suppresses a security alert under a marketing preference

Evaluate the applicable permission, consent, channel preference, mandatory-delivery rules and suppression state against that purpose. What is read is the authoritative permission state - this journey evaluates it for one message and never sets it
Are the permission rules for this purpose and these channels defined?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a communication purpose with no defined permission rules

nodes.headline: What does the evaluation leave available?

Evaluate the alternate routes the mandatory-delivery rules actually permit. Mandatory does not mean any channel will do - it means the rules define which ones survive a preference, and those are the only ones
Does a permitted alternate exist?
Record the channels permitted for this purpose, each with the rule that permits it. Recording the rule is what makes the send defensible and the suppression explainable
Channel selection → choose route → prepare message
nodes.detail: at least one channel permitted for this purpose

nodes.headline: Record UNDELIVERABLE_BY_POLICY with the purpose and the rule that closed each route. This is a policy outcome rather than a delivery failure, and recording it as a failure sends it into a retry loop against a rule that will not change
Does this obligation require escalation when no route is permitted?
Communication outcome → close obligation or escalate unreachable
nodes.detail: a mandatory communication with no permitted route

nodes.headline: UNDELIVERABLE_BY_POLICY; no permitted route for this purpose
nodes.detail: a permission change or a new permitted destination reopens routing while the obligation is still relevant

edges.label: Defined
edges.when: rules state which channels may carry this purpose, and whether any delivery is mandatory

edges.label: Not defined
edges.when: nothing states whether this purpose may use these channels
a communication purpose with no defined permission rules

edges.label: At least one channel is permitted
edges.when: a channel may carry this purpose to this recipient

edges.label: The preferred channel is not permitted and the communication is mandatory
edges.when: the recipient's preference closes the usual route and a rule requires delivery anyway

edges.label: No permissible route
edges.when: every channel is closed for this purpose

edges.label: One exists
edges.when: the mandatory-delivery rules keep a route open

edges.label: None
edges.when: the rules leave no route for this purpose
at least one channel permitted for this purpose

edges.label: It does
edges.when: the communication is mandatory or critical and cannot simply be dropped

edges.label: It does not
edges.when: an unroutable optional message closes without further action
a mandatory communication with no permitted route

distinctFrom.because: CON-35 owns consent and permission as authoritative state, and propagates changes to it. This evaluates that state for one message's actual purpose - it can suppress a channel the recipient has permitted, and permit one they have not, where mandatory-delivery rules say so.

guardrails: Contactable is not consented for every purpose.
Marketing consent does not control mandatory security notices unless governing rules say so.
Consent requirements are never invented, in either direction.
This journey reads permission state and never writes it.
A requirement to evaluate content-handling policy is not a permission flag. It governs what the message may say and on which surface; it neither grants nor withholds the right to send.
governance.reusableRule: Channel eligibility depends on both technical contactability and whether that channel may be used for the communication's actual purpose.
governance.entityScope: the obligation, the recipient's destinations, and the purpose being evaluated against them
governance.entityNote: This reads permission state and never writes it. Whether somebody has consented is owned elsewhere; whether this purpose may use this channel is decided here.

identity.title: Channel selection → choose route → prepare message
identity.purpose: Pick the smallest set of channels that actually satisfies the obligation, and build the message for them.

requires: one or more channels permitted for this obligation's purpose

nodes.headline: Permitted channels available

Evaluate the purpose, the urgency, the recipient's preferences, each channel's capability, the content's requirements, delivery reliability, the fallback policy, and cost or priority where those are defined

Select the primary route - the smallest valid set capable of satisfying the obligation. Sending on every available channel is not thoroughness; it is one event arriving four times, and the recipient reads the repetition as a fault in the system
Does the obligation genuinely require more than one channel?

Create explicitly coordinated deliveries, each aware of the others, so the obligation closes once rather than once per channel. Uncoordinated parallel sends produce an obligation that closes three times and a recipient who is told three times
Record the single primary route and the fallback that would be tried if it fails. The fallback is held in reserve - it is a route for later rather than a second message now

Prepare the channel-compatible message instance, referencing the business facts rather than restating them independently. Channel selection never alters the facts - a truncated message says less than the full one, and it must not say something different
Message prepared → revalidate state → send or suppress
nodes.detail: a prepared message instance on a selected route

edges.label: Explicitly, yes
edges.when: a rule or the obligation's own requirement calls for delivery on more than one channel

edges.label: One route, with a fallback held
edges.when: a single channel satisfies the obligation
a prepared message instance on a selected route

guardrails: Channel selection never alters business facts.
Multi-channel delivery is intentional rather than incidental.
A fallback channel is not an automatic duplicate send.
A candidate channel has to be inside its own volume cap as well as permitted. A fallback that ignores the cap because the primary failed burns the one route that was still working.
An exemption from a contact-pressure limit exists only where a governing rule defines one for that purpose and channel. Urgency does not create an exemption, and no class is exempt by default.
Internal work destinations are not delivery channels and are skipped when choosing a route to the recipient.
governance.reusableRule: Communication routing selects the smallest valid set of channels capable of satisfying the communication obligation.
governance.entityScope: the obligation and the permitted channels available to it
governance.entityNote: A fallback is a route held in reserve rather than a second send. Multi-channel delivery is a decision somebody makes, never a side effect of several channels being available.

identity.title: Message prepared → revalidate state → send or suppress
identity.purpose: Check the message is still true immediately before it goes, and stop it if it is not.

requires: a prepared message instance about to be submitted for delivery

nodes.headline: Message reaches send ready

Re-read the authoritative state the message describes. Between preparation and send the appointment may have been cancelled, the payment may have succeeded and the approval may have been reversed - and each of those turns a helpful message into a damaging one
Is the communication still valid?

Suppress the stale message and record why. A reminder for a cancelled appointment brings somebody somewhere for nothing; a payment-failure notice sent after the payment succeeded produces a support contact and costs the credibility of every later notice
stale message suppressed; nothing was sent
nodes.detail: the obligation closes as superseded rather than as met. A new event about the same subject creates its own obligation

nodes.headline: Communication obligation → resolve recipient → ready, hold or fail
nodes.detail: a message whose recipient or destination stopped being valid before send

nodes.headline: Does the content depend on data that has changed since preparation?
Regenerate the content from current data before sending. Sending a stale amount, date or status is worse than sending nothing, because the recipient acts on it and then has to be told it was wrong

Record the message as validated at send time, with what was checked and against what version. Historical sent messages are never mutated afterwards - what was sent is what was sent, and rewriting it removes the evidence that a wrong thing went out
Send attempt → accepted, failed or unknown
nodes.detail: a message validated immediately before delivery

edges.label: Still valid
edges.when: the reason for the message and its subject both still stand

edges.label: Superseded or resolved
edges.when: the event the message is about has been undone, cancelled or resolved

edges.label: The recipient or channel is no longer valid
edges.when: the destination failed or the recipient changed since routing
a message whose recipient or destination stopped being valid before send

edges.label: It changed
edges.when: an amount, a date, a status or a name in the message is no longer current

edges.label: Unchanged
edges.when: everything the message states is still current
a message validated immediately before delivery

guardrails: A queued message is not a permanently valid message.
A reminder for a cancelled appointment does not send.
A resolved payment failure does not send as unresolved.
Historical sent messages are never mutated.
governance.reusableRule: Messages should be revalidated immediately before delivery whenever delayed execution could make their content or purpose stale.
governance.entityScope: the prepared message instance and the business entity it describes
governance.entityNote: The message is a claim about the world made at the moment it was written. This is the only point at which that claim is checked against the world as it now is.

identity.title: Send attempt → accepted, failed or unknown
identity.purpose: Record what happened when the message was handed to a provider, which is not what happened to the recipient.

requires: a validated message submitted to a delivery mechanism or provider

nodes.headline: Message submitted to provider

Persist the message id, the attempt id, the channel, the provider and its reference, the submission time and the content version reference. The attempt is written before its outcome is known, so an outcome arriving hours later has something to attach to
until the provider accepts the submission, or the provider reports an immediate authoritative failure
nodes.detail: timeout after the submission timeout for this channel

nodes.headline: What did the provider do with it?
Record SENT and DELIVERY_PENDING. The provider taking the message is a fact about the provider's queue - it can be accepted, held, bounced and discarded without anything reaching anybody
SENT and DELIVERY_PENDING; submitted and accepted, delivery not established
nodes.detail: the channel's delivery outcome arrives on its own schedule and correlates to this attempt. Nothing here concludes the obligation

nodes.headline: Record DELIVERY_FAILED with exactly what the provider reported, unclassified. The classification belongs to the recovery journey, which needs the raw reason rather than a summary of it
Delivery failure → classify → retry, fallback or stop
nodes.detail: a submission the provider refused, or an unknown outcome where duplicates are harmless

nodes.headline: Record DELIVERY_UNKNOWN and hold any resend. A timeout is not a failure - the message may well have gone, and resending blindly delivers the same notice twice, which for some notices reads as a different message than once
Would a duplicate matter for this communication?
external:external-status-reconciliation
nodes.detail: an unknown submission outcome where a duplicate would matter

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the provider accepts the submission, the provider reports an immediate authoritative failure

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a provider that neither accepts nor refuses leaves the message in an unknown state, and the question of whether to resend depends on knowing that rather than assuming either answer

edges.label: Accepted
edges.when: the provider took the message for delivery

edges.label: Refused immediately
edges.when: the provider authoritatively rejected the submission
a submission the provider refused, or an unknown outcome where duplicates are harmless

edges.label: It would
edges.when: the message carries a code, a link, a payment instruction or anything a second copy makes ambiguous

edges.label: It would not
edges.when: a repeat is harmless and the message is worth resending on that basis
an unknown submission outcome where a duplicate would matter

distinctFrom.because: This is the handover to a provider - accepted, refused or unanswered. CMS-207 is what the channel later reports about whether it reached anyone. A message can be accepted and never delivered, and the two states must be separately visible.

guardrails: Provider accepted is not delivered.
A timeout is not a send failure.
A blind resend may create duplicate communication.
governance.reusableRule: Submitting a message establishes a delivery attempt, not proof that the recipient received it.
governance.entityScope: the individual delivery attempt, with its provider reference
governance.entityNote: One attempt per submission. Outcomes arriving later correlate to a specific attempt, which is why the attempt is written before its outcome is known.

identity.title: Delivery outcome → delivered, failed or unknown → update communication
identity.purpose: Derive the real delivery state from what the channel reports, attached to the exact attempt it concerns.

requires: a delivery event or status reported by the channel

nodes.headline: Delivery status received

Correlate the outcome to the exact delivery attempt it concerns. A status with no attempt to attach to is a status about nothing, and attaching it to the wrong attempt marks a different message delivered
Did it correlate to a known attempt?
external:external-status-reconciliation
nodes.detail: a delivery outcome that could not be correlated or that remains ambiguous

nodes.headline: Is this outcome new, repeated, or older than what is already recorded?
duplicate delivery event ignored; recorded state unchanged
nodes.detail: a genuinely new outcome for this attempt is processed on its own terms. Channels repeat webhooks, and repeating the state change with them double-counts every delivery

nodes.headline: Record the late event without overwriting stronger evidence. A bounce arriving after a confirmed delivery does not undo the delivery - unless the channel's semantics explicitly say it does, in which case they say so and the rule is applied rather than assumed
late outcome recorded; stronger delivery evidence preserved
nodes.detail: channel semantics that genuinely make a late failure authoritative are applied as a rule rather than by arrival order

nodes.headline: What does the channel report?

Record DELIVERED against this attempt. Delivered is not read, and read is not understood - a delivery receipt says the message reached a destination and nothing about anybody having seen it, let alone acted on it
Communication outcome → close obligation or escalate unreachable
nodes.detail: a confirmed delivery

nodes.headline: Record DELIVERY_FAILED with the reason exactly as the channel reported it. The reason is what the recovery journey classifies on, and summarising it here loses the distinction between a full mailbox and a dead address
Delivery failure → classify → retry, fallback or stop
nodes.detail: an authoritative delivery failure

nodes.headline: Record DELIVERY_UNKNOWN. Neither delivered nor failed is a real state, and resolving it to whichever is more convenient produces either a closed obligation nobody met or a duplicate nobody needed

edges.label: Correlated
edges.when: the outcome names an attempt we hold

edges.label: Uncorrelated
edges.when: the outcome names nothing we recognise
a delivery outcome that could not be correlated or that remains ambiguous

edges.label: New and current
edges.when: this outcome advances what is known about the attempt

edges.label: Already processed
edges.when: the same outcome has already been applied to this attempt

edges.label: Late and weaker
edges.when: it arrives after, and reports less than, what is already established

edges.label: Delivered
edges.when: the channel authoritatively reports it reached the destination

edges.label: Definitive failure
edges.when: the channel authoritatively reports it did not and will not arrive

edges.label: Ambiguous
edges.when: the report establishes neither
a confirmed delivery
an authoritative delivery failure

guardrails: Sent is not delivered.
Delivered is not read.
A late failure does not overwrite stronger authoritative delivery evidence without valid channel semantics.
Repeated delivery events are processed idempotently.
An open or a read can be produced by a privacy proxy or a scanner rather than by a person. It is evidence about the message and never authoritative evidence of intent or outcome.
governance.reusableRule: Communication delivery state should be derived from authoritative channel evidence and correlated to the exact delivery attempt.
governance.entityScope: the delivery attempt and the outcomes reported against it
governance.entityNote: Outcomes arrive out of order, twice, and late. Each is processed against the attempt it names and against what is already recorded.

identity.title: Delivery failure → classify → retry, fallback or stop
identity.purpose: Respond to the failure that actually happened, without spreading it wider than the destination it belongs to.

requires: a delivery failure reported authoritatively by the channel or provider
insufficientAlone: an unknown outcome, which is not a failure and needs reconciling rather than recovering

nodes.headline: Authoritative delivery failure

Classify the failure by what the channel actually reported, into an explicit class - TEMPORARY, PROVIDER_FAILURE, RATE_LIMITED, PERMANENT, INVALID_DESTINATION, CHANNEL_RESTRICTED or UNKNOWN. The class decides everything downstream, which is why it is established before anything is retried, and treating them all as transient produces a retry loop against an address that will never exist
Is the communication still relevant?
Suppress the recovery. Recovering delivery of a message whose reason for existing has passed spends effort arriving at a stale notice, which is the worst of both outcomes
recovery abandoned; the message was overtaken by events
nodes.detail: the obligation closes as superseded rather than as failed. Its subject producing a new event creates a new obligation

nodes.headline: What does the failure class call for?

Treat an unclassifiable failure as temporary but on a smaller budget, and record that the class was unknown. Guessing permanent discards a destination that may work; guessing temporary on the full budget is how an unknown failure becomes an unbounded retry

Retry on the same channel through the canonical retry mechanism, with backoff, against a budget fixed at the first failure. The budget is set once and does not renew - that is the difference between a retry policy and a loop, and a schedule with no end looks like a working system from inside and like harassment from the recipient's inbox
Does retry budget remain?
retrying within budget on the same channel
nodes.detail: each retry is a new send attempt with its own outcome, and a failure on it returns here with the budget one lower

nodes.headline: Stop futile retries against this destination and raise the contactability evidence. One invalid address invalidates that address and nothing else - the recipient's phone, device and in-app account are untouched by an email that bounced
Channel contactability change → recalculate reachability → route or suppress
nodes.detail: a failure that is a property of the contact point rather than of the attempt

nodes.headline: Is an alternate channel available?
Communication purpose → permission and preference check → allow, suppress or alternate
nodes.detail: a failed channel with an alternate destination available

nodes.headline: Communication outcome → close obligation or escalate unreachable
nodes.detail: a failure with no remaining channel to try

edges.label: Still relevant
edges.when: the reason for the message still stands and its window is open

edges.label: No longer relevant
edges.when: the event it concerns has resolved, or its relevance window has closed

edges.label: Temporary, rate-limited or provider-side
edges.when: the destination is fine and the failure is expected to clear

edges.label: Permanent for this destination
edges.when: a hard bounce, an invalid address or a dead token

edges.label: Restricted on this channel
edges.when: this channel will not carry this content, for a reason a retry does not address

edges.label: Unclassifiable
edges.when: the provider gave no class that can be relied on

edges.label: Budget remains
edges.when: the attempt count and window still permit another try

edges.label: The destination's contactability changed underneath the retry
edges.when: the contact point's own state moved while the budget was being spent

edges.label: Exhausted
edges.when: the budget fixed at the first failure has been spent
a failure that is a property of the contact point rather than of the attempt

edges.label: One is available
edges.when: the recipient has another destination on another channel

edges.label: None
edges.when: no other channel remains for this recipient
a failed channel with an alternate destination available
a failure with no remaining channel to try

distinctFrom.because: OPS-124 is the generic retryable-failure and backoff mechanism. This decides what a communication failure means - whether the address is dead, whether another channel may carry this purpose, and whether the message is even still worth delivering. It uses that retry machinery rather than being it.

guardrails: A delivery failure does not mean the user is unreachable everywhere.
Retry is bounded rather than infinite.
A fallback must independently pass the purpose and permission checks.
One invalid address does not invalidate unrelated destinations.
The retry budget is fixed at the first failure and does not renew.
A permanent bounce is a deliverability fact rather than an engagement problem, and is never fed into an engagement or churn model as one.
A failure on one channel says nothing about the permission or the contactability of any other.
A permitted alternative channel allows a move; it does not require one.
governance.reusableRule: Communication recovery should respond to the actual delivery failure while preserving channel-specific contactability and message relevance.
governance.entityScope: the failed delivery, its channel and the destination it was aimed at
governance.entityNote: The failure belongs to a destination on a channel. It says nothing about the recipient's other destinations, and recording it against the person loses them.

identity.title: Communication outcome → close obligation or escalate unreachable
identity.purpose: Close the obligation against what it actually required, and escalate the ones that could not be met.

requires: an obligation whose deliveries have reached a state that could close it

nodes.headline: Delivery attempts reach meaningful outcome
Did the communication become obsolete before it was delivered?
Close as SUPERSEDED or SUPPRESSED, recording that the obligation ended because its reason did rather than because it was met. The two look identical in a completion count and mean opposite things
closed as superseded; the obligation ended unmet and unneeded
nodes.detail: a new event about the same subject creates its own obligation rather than reviving this one

nodes.headline: What does this obligation require to be satisfied?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: an obligation with no defined completion semantics

nodes.headline: Is delivery confirmed?
Is a documented send attempt on record?
Record COMMUNICATION_COMPLETED against the requirement it actually satisfied, naming which one. Unread is not undelivered, and an obligation met by delivery is met whether or not anybody opened it
COMMUNICATION_COMPLETED against its stated requirement
nodes.detail: a further event about the same subject creates its own obligation. Whether the recipient understood is not something this state claims

nodes.headline: Are all permissible delivery routes exhausted?
obligation open; permitted routes remain untried
nodes.detail: the remaining routes are attempted and report their own outcomes back here

nodes.headline: Record UNREACHABLE_FOR_PURPOSE. This is scoped to the purpose - every route permitted for this kind of message failed, and the same recipient may be perfectly reachable for something else
Is this communication mandatory or critical?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a mandatory communication that could not be delivered by any permitted route

nodes.headline: UNREACHABLE_FOR_PURPOSE; the obligation closes unmet and recorded as such
nodes.detail: a new valid destination for this purpose makes the recipient reachable again, and a later obligation routes normally

edges.label: It did
edges.when: the event it concerns resolved or was undone while delivery was still in progress

edges.label: It stands
edges.when: the reason for the message is still real

edges.label: Confirmed delivery
edges.when: the requirement is that the message actually reached the recipient

edges.label: A documented send attempt
edges.when: the requirement is that a message was properly sent, with the record to show it

edges.label: Not defined
edges.when: nothing states whether an attempt or a delivery satisfies this notice
an obligation with no defined completion semantics

edges.label: Confirmed
edges.when: authoritative channel evidence establishes it arrived

edges.label: Not confirmed
edges.when: no delivery has been established on any route

edges.label: On record
edges.when: a properly validated message was submitted and the attempt is recorded

edges.label: None succeeded in being made
edges.when: no attempt was ever submitted on any permitted route

edges.label: Routes remain
edges.when: a permitted channel or destination has not yet been tried

edges.label: Exhausted
edges.when: every route permitted for this purpose has been tried and none worked

edges.label: It is
edges.when: a rule, a contract or a regulation requires this recipient to be told

edges.label: It is not
edges.when: the message was useful rather than required
a mandatory communication that could not be delivered by any permitted route

guardrails: Whether a send or a delivery is sufficient is never invented.
Unread is not undelivered.
A critical communication failure escalates rather than retrying endlessly.
An obligation does not close merely because a message object exists.
governance.reusableRule: A communication obligation closes according to its required outcome - attempt, delivery or explicit escalation - not merely because a message object exists.
governance.entityScope: the communication obligation and every delivery made against it
governance.entityNote: The obligation defines its own required outcome. Some are met by a documented attempt and some only by confirmed delivery, and which applies is not this journey's to decide.

identity.title: Permission capture → validate scope → activate or reject
identity.purpose: Turn a permission decision into an auditable record of what exactly was authorised, rather than a flag that says yes.

requires: a deliberate act of granting or refusing permission, identifying what is being permitted
insufficientAlone: creating an account
providing an email address or phone number
accepting terms of service where consent was not separately given
a pre-ticked box

nodes.headline: Explicit permission decision received

Capture the permission type, the purpose, the channel, the scope, the source, the time, and the evidence or consent-text version where one is required - the version matters, because what someone agreed to is the wording in front of them at the time
Is this a valid permission, and is its scope unambiguous?

Record only the narrowest defensible reading, and flag the ambiguity so it can be resolved by asking rather than by assuming. Reading an unclear scope broadly is how one newsletter signup becomes a permission to send anything
not recorded as permission
nodes.detail: a genuine permission decision later creates one normally; nothing partial is stored that a later process could mistake for consent

nodes.headline: Does a permission already exist for this purpose, channel and scope?

Reconcile against the prior record using the authoritative rules for this permission type, appending rather than replacing - the previous grant, its source and its version stay readable, because a permission history is the only defence of what was sent under it
Activate the permission for exactly the purpose, channel and scope captured, and nothing adjacent to them
permission active for the captured purpose, channel and scope
nodes.detail: any later decision on the same combination opens a new instance; changes to an active permission are CON-35's, not this journey's

edges.label: Valid and clear
edges.when: the act was deliberate, the purpose and channel are identified, and the scope is unambiguous

edges.label: Valid but ambiguous scope
edges.when: permission was clearly given, but what it covers can be read more than one way

edges.label: Not a permission
edges.when: the act does not constitute authorisation - an implied opt-in, a pre-ticked box, or a signup mistaken for consent

edges.label: Exists
edges.when: a prior record covers the same combination

edges.label: New
edges.when: no prior record covers it

distinctFrom.because: This creates authorisation. CON-32 records how someone would like authorised communication done, which is a different fact and must never be able to create this one.

guardrails: Creating an account is not consent. Nor is providing contact details, which is how someone reaches a service rather than an invitation to be marketed to.
