Permission on one channel never transfers to another. Email consent is not SMS consent.
An ambiguous scope is read narrowly. The broad reading is the one that has to be asked for.
A refusal is recorded as a decision, not as an absence - so that nothing later reads the silence as room to assume.
governance.reusableRule: Permission must represent an explicit, auditable authorization for a defined purpose and scope.
governance.entityScope: person plus the permission record, keyed by purpose, channel and scope
governance.entityNote: One record per purpose x channel x scope. Consent to product notices by email is a different record from consent to marketing by email, and neither is a record about SMS.

identity.title: Preference capture → persist → personalise eligible communication
identity.purpose: Record how someone would like permitted communication done, in a store that structurally cannot become permission.

requires: the person deliberately setting or changing a preference: frequency, topic, category, language, preferred channel, content type
insufficientAlone: behaviour that suggests a preference
the channel someone happened to reply on
a topic they clicked once

nodes.headline: Preference explicitly set or changed

Persist the value with its source and the time it changed, into the store that holds declared answers only. Inference is written elsewhere - once the two share a field, nothing can tell what the person actually said
Is the communication this preference would shape actually permitted?
preference stored, shaping nothing
nodes.detail: if permission is granted later the stored preference applies from that moment; the preference waited rather than authorised anything

nodes.headline: Apply the preference to communication that is already permitted - which is the only thing a preference can do
Preference change → recalculate active journeys → suppress or adapt
nodes.detail: a preference that will change what already-running journeys should do

edges.label: Permitted
edges.when: an active permission covers the purpose and channel the preference applies to

edges.label: Not permitted
edges.when: no permission covers it - including the common case where someone states a channel preference without ever authorising that channel
a preference that will change what already-running journeys should do

guardrails: A preference is not consent. Preferring email says nothing about wanting marketing.
Inferred behaviour and declared preference stay in separate stores. The confidence attached to them is different and the merge cannot be undone.
A preference set where no permission exists is stored and applied to nothing.
governance.reusableRule: Preferences shape permitted experiences; they do not create permission to communicate.
governance.entityScope: person plus the declared-preference profile
governance.entityNote: Declared preferences live in their own store. Inferred interests live in another, and the two are never written to the same field.

identity.title: Preference change → recalculate active journeys → suppress or adapt
identity.purpose: Make a preference change reach the messages already sitting in a queue, not just the profile field.

requires: a recorded preference change with its previous value

nodes.headline: Authoritative preference changed

Persist the new value keeping the change history - what it was, what it became, and when. Messages already delivered under the old preference are not rewritten and not apologised for; they were correct when they went
Identify the active journey instances and queued actions this preference touches. The queue is the point: a preference that only affects what has not been scheduled yet changes nothing anyone notices
How does each pending action stand against the new preference?
Suppress the conflicting actions before they execute. A queued action written under the old preference must not be allowed to overwrite the new one simply by arriving first
Adapt the pending actions to the new preference before execution rather than after - adapting afterwards is called an apology
future orchestration aligned to the new preference; permission unchanged
nodes.detail: the next preference change re-opens this

edges.label: Now unwanted
edges.when: the new preference means this action should not happen at all - a topic removed, a category switched off

edges.label: Reshaped, not forbidden
edges.when: the action still happens but differently - a changed language, a changed format, a changed level of detail

edges.label: Unaffected
edges.when: nothing pending conflicts

guardrails: A preference change does not rewrite what has already been sent.
A stale queued action never overrides a newer preference. Execution re-validates; scheduling is not a decision.
A preference change is not a permission change, however much it reduces what gets sent.
governance.reusableRule: Preference changes should affect future eligible orchestration, including actions already queued but not yet executed.
governance.entityScope: person plus the preference plus every active journey instance and queued action it touches
governance.entityNote: The scope is deliberately wide on the forward side and closed on the backward one: everything not yet executed, nothing already delivered.

identity.title: Communication frequency change → recalculate cadence → apply prospectively
identity.purpose: Recalculate how often optional communication may go out, without letting that quietly reach the messages someone has to receive.

requires: a deliberate change to how often communication should arrive - weekly to monthly, everything to important only, a reduction to a stated minimum
insufficientAlone: a decline in engagement, which is a signal rather than an instruction

nodes.headline: Frequency preference changed
Determine which communication classes this preference governs. By default that is optional communication only, and the default is the one that holds unless a policy explicitly says otherwise
Does the governing policy extend this preference to required or transactional communication?
Include the required classes the policy names, and only those, recording which policy authorised it
Leave required and transactional communication governed by its own rules. Someone asking for fewer marketing emails has not asked to stop hearing that their service is being suspended
Recalculate the future cadence for the governed classes. Messages already delivered are untouched - a cadence change is prospective by definition
Does what is already queued exceed the new cadence?
Suppress or reschedule the optional communication that now exceeds the cadence, choosing between the two by whether the message keeps its meaning later
cadence recalculated prospectively; permission untouched
nodes.detail: the next frequency change re-opens this

edges.label: Policy extends it
edges.when: a specific policy says this preference covers required communication too, naming which

edges.label: Optional only
edges.when: no such policy - the ordinary case

edges.label: Exceeds
edges.when: more optional communication is scheduled than the new preference allows

edges.label: Within it
edges.when: the queue already fits

distinctFrom.because: A frequency preference changes how much rather than what, which means recalculating a cadence across classes rather than adapting individual queued actions.

guardrails: A frequency reduction is not a global opt-out. Fewer is not none, and treating it as none loses the relationship the person was trying to keep.
A marketing frequency preference does not close critical transactional communication.
A cadence change never retroactively alters messages already delivered.
governance.reusableRule: Frequency preferences modify future optional communication cadence without silently changing unrelated permission states.
governance.entityScope: person plus the communication classes the frequency preference actually governs
governance.entityNote: The governed set is the whole question. A frequency preference that silently covers required communication is an opt-out nobody chose.

identity.title: Consent or permission change → immediate enforcement → propagate
identity.purpose: Stop affected communication the moment permission changes, and let the distributed systems catch up afterwards.

requires: a recorded transition on an existing permission: opted in to opted out, allowed to restricted, or a scope reduced or widened

nodes.headline: Authoritative permission change

Record the old state, the new state, the source, the time, and the scope, purpose and channel it applies to - appended, because the question later is always what we were authorised to do at a particular moment
Does this reduce permission or extend it?

Suppress the affected outbound communication now, including everything queued, without waiting for any downstream system to acknowledge anything. The asymmetry is deliberate: a grant applied late costs a message that could have been sent, a withdrawal applied late costs one that should not have been
Propagate the new state to the dependent systems, carrying origin and version so that an out-of-order echo cannot revert it and a redelivery cannot restart the exchange
until the required propagation confirmations arrive
nodes.detail: timeout after the synchronisation SLA for this permission type

nodes.headline: Do the dependent systems now agree?
Permission conflict → fail-safe state → reconcile → restore
nodes.detail: systems failing to converge on the new permission state

nodes.headline: permission change enforced and consistent across dependent systems
nodes.detail: the next change on this permission opens a new instance

edges.label: Withdrawal or restriction
edges.when: permission is removed, narrowed or restricted

edges.label: Grant or extension
edges.when: permission is given or widened

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the required propagation confirmations arrive

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: convergence that has not happened by its deadline is a conflict, and calling it one is what gets it looked at - enforcement is already in force either way

edges.label: Consistent
edges.when: every required system confirms the new state at the expected version

edges.label: Divergent
edges.when: at least one system reports a different state
systems failing to converge on the new permission state

distinctFrom.because: CON-31 creates a permission. This changes one that exists, and the difference that matters is that a change can be a withdrawal, which has to be enforced before it has been agreed anywhere else.

guardrails: Withdrawal never waits for a campaign schedule, a batch window, or a downstream acknowledgement.
Communication already queued is invalidated wherever that is technically possible, and where it is not, that limitation is recorded rather than assumed away.
Permission history is preserved. The current value alone cannot answer what we were allowed to do last month.
Enforcement is scoped to the purpose, channel and scope that changed - a withdrawal is not an excuse to stop everything.
governance.reusableRule: Permission withdrawal should be enforced immediately and propagated asynchronously rather than waiting for distributed systems to converge.
governance.entityScope: person plus the permission record that changed, at its purpose, channel and scope
governance.entityNote: Enforcement is scoped to what actually changed. A withdrawal of marketing email consent does not suspend service notices, and treating it as though it did is its own failure.

identity.title: Channel contactability change → recalculate reachability → route or suppress
identity.purpose: Track whether a channel can reach someone, as a state entirely separate from whether it may, and keep each destination's route health separately so future sending routes around what is broken.

requires: a change in whether a contact point can technically be reached: an address becoming undeliverable, a number found invalid, a push token expired or refreshed, an address corrected, a channel restored, or a new destination verified and added
insufficientAlone: a single soft failure that resolved on retry
silence from the recipient, which says nothing about deliverability

nodes.headline: Channel contactability materially changed

Update the contactability state to CONTACTABLE, TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE, UNDELIVERABLE, INVALID or RESTORED, leaving permission untouched - a channel that cannot reach someone has expressed no opinion about whether it may
What does the evidence establish about this contact point?

Make the new destination available for future eligible communication. Available is not consented - a verified address is a route, and whether it may carry a given purpose is a separate question decided separately

Allow future eligible communication on this contact point again, recorded from the current evidence rather than by clearing the history of why it was suppressed. The prior failures stay readable, because a route that keeps breaking and being restored is worth being able to see. What was missed while it was unreachable is not replayed - the queue described a state that has since moved
Is any pending communication waiting on this contact point?
Communication obligation → resolve recipient → ready, hold or fail
nodes.detail: pending communication affected by a change in this destination's health

nodes.headline: contact point reachable again; nothing replayed
nodes.detail: the next contactability change re-opens this

nodes.headline: Suppress future attempts on this contact point according to the failure class - a temporary failure and a permanently invalid destination are not held the same way and must not be recorded as though they were. Historical delivery records are untouched: a message delivered to this address last year was delivered, and rewriting that to match today's state destroys the record of what the person was actually told
Is any pending communication aimed at this contact point?
What can reach this person instead?
unreachable here, reachable elsewhere with permission
nodes.detail: the sending journey decides whether to use the alternative; this journey establishes that it is allowed to, which is not the same as recommending it

nodes.headline: until the contact point becomes reachable again
nodes.detail: timeout after the horizon for this failure class

nodes.headline: external:human-in-the-loop-lifecycle
nodes.detail: an important communication with no permitted way to deliver it

nodes.headline: no permitted, working channel; permission unchanged
nodes.detail: a corrected contact point or a new permission re-opens this - the person has not opted out, and nothing here may be recorded as though they had

edges.label: Restored or contactable
edges.when: the contact point works again

edges.label: A newly added or verified destination
edges.when: a route has been added or verified for the first time

edges.label: Unavailable
edges.when: temporarily unavailable, undeliverable or invalid

edges.label: Some is waiting
edges.when: obligations were held for this destination, or were routed away from it while it was unusable

edges.label: None
edges.when: nothing outstanding depends on this contact point
pending communication affected by a change in this destination's health

edges.label: Some is aimed at it
edges.when: obligations are queued against a destination that has just become unusable

edges.label: None
edges.when: nothing outstanding is routed here

edges.label: A permitted, appropriate alternative
edges.when: another channel is both covered by permission for this purpose and appropriate to what the journey is doing

edges.label: Nothing yet, but the failure is temporary
edges.when: the contact point may come back and the communication can wait for it

edges.label: Nothing, and it matters
edges.when: no permitted alternative exists and the communication is important enough that a person should know

edges.label: Nothing, and it can wait
edges.when: no permitted alternative exists and nothing needs escalating

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the contact point becomes reachable again

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a temporary failure that lasts long enough stops being temporary, and holding it in that state indefinitely hides a contact point that needs correcting
an important communication with no permitted way to deliver it

distinctFrom.because: One is about capability and the other about authorisation. They are stored separately precisely so that a bounce can never look like an opt-out.

guardrails: Undeliverable is not opted out. A full mailbox is not a decision.
Opted out is not undeliverable. The channel still works; we are simply not allowed to use it.
An available alternative channel is not permission to use it. Availability is the easiest thing to check and the least meaningful.
Consent is never inferred from contactability. A newly verified destination is a route, not a permission.
One destination failing does not make the person globally unreachable; state is held per destination.
Historical delivery records remain unchanged when a destination's health changes.

A request to repair a broken contact point goes out on a different verified channel, or it does not go out at all. Asking somebody to fix an address by sending to that address is the failure repeating itself.

Repair attempts are bounded per cycle. A contact point that fails re-verification stays suppressed rather than being retried blind, and a corrected value is verified before the destination is treated as usable.
governance.reusableRule: Contactability describes whether a channel can technically reach the user; permission determines whether it may be used.
governance.entityScope: person plus the specific contact point - this address, this number, this device token
governance.entityNote: Contactability belongs to the contact point, not the person and not the channel class. One dead device token does not make push unreachable, and there is deliberately no person-level reachable flag - one would erase every route the failing one is not.

identity.title: Communication suppression → reason → release or persist
identity.purpose: Make every reason something is not being sent an explicit, scoped, releasable state rather than an absence.

requires: a condition that stops communication: permission withdrawn, a frequency policy, a contactability failure, a higher-priority journey taking ownership, a legal or policy restriction, a cooldown, a duplicate, an existing human resolution, or a temporary incident

nodes.headline: Suppression condition became active

Record the reason, the scope, the source, the start time, and the release condition where one exists. Scope carries as much weight as reason: without it nothing downstream can tell what is still allowed
Does this suppression have a definable release condition?
suppressed until the underlying state changes
nodes.detail: a change to the state that caused it opens a new evaluation. Nothing was deleted here - the person, their history and their record are intact, and only sending is stopped

nodes.headline: until the recorded release condition is met
nodes.detail: timeout after a review horizon appropriate to the reason

nodes.headline: At review, does the reason still hold?

Re-evaluate what the affected journeys should do now, and act on that. What was held during the suppression is not replayed - those messages described a state that has since moved, and delivering a week of them at once is how a release becomes worse than the suppression
suppression released; current state re-evaluated, backlog discarded
nodes.detail: any new suppression condition opens its own instance with its own reason and scope

edges.label: Temporary
edges.when: a condition or a time will end it - a cooldown, an incident, a frequency window, a case being closed

edges.label: Persistent
edges.when: it stands until an authoritative state changes - a withdrawal, a legal restriction, an invalid contact point

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the recorded release condition is met

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a temporary suppression whose release condition never arrives has quietly become permanent, and the review is what forces that to be said out loud

edges.label: Still valid
edges.when: the condition that caused it has not gone away

edges.label: No longer valid
edges.when: the reason has lapsed even though no release event fired

distinctFrom.because: A cooldown is one reason among the nine this journey holds. It has its own journey because its release is time-based and its scope is deliberately partial, which the general mechanism does not assume.

guardrails: Suppression is not deletion. Nothing is removed; sending is stopped.
Release is not replay. What was held is discarded and current eligibility is recalculated.
Different reasons carry different scopes, and a suppression without its scope cannot be released correctly.

Suppression we impose on ourselves is a separate state from permission the person gave us. A sender-side hold is not an unsubscribe, it is recorded against our own sending rather than against their consent, and nobody may read it as a decision they made.
Releasing a sender-side suppression asks for permission again rather than switching sending back on. Silence long enough to suppress for is not consent that survived it.
governance.reusableRule: Suppression should be explicit, scoped and reversible only when its underlying reason is no longer valid.
governance.entityScope: the person, message or journey instance the suppression applies to, at the scope recorded with it
governance.entityNote: The scope is part of the record. A cooldown on one channel and a legal restriction across all of them are both suppressions and share nothing else.

identity.title: Communication cooldown → hold optional messaging → re-evaluate
identity.purpose: Reduce optional communication pressure for a while, without touching permission and without covering more than it needs to.

requires: an event that justifies a quiet period: a recent service recovery, a critical external alert, an explicit decline, unusually dense recent communication, a sensitive interaction, or a recent retention attempt

nodes.headline: Cooldown triggering event
Create the cooldown scoped to what its reason actually justifies, recording the reason, the scope, the start, and either an expiry or the condition that would end it early
Does this reason justify holding required or safety communication as well?
Extend the cooldown only to the required communication the policy names, recording which policy did it - so the extension is attributable rather than inherited
until an authoritative change to the condition that created the cooldown
nodes.detail: timeout after the cooldown period

nodes.headline: How did the underlying condition change?
Communication suppression → reason → release or persist
nodes.detail: a cooldown outgrown by its own cause

nodes.headline: Re-evaluate what is eligible now and act on that. Anything queued when the cooldown began is discarded rather than released - a cooldown that ends by flushing a backlog has achieved nothing except a delay
cooldown ended; current eligibility recalculated, backlog discarded
nodes.detail: a new cooldown-triggering event creates a new one with its own reason and scope

edges.label: Optional only
edges.when: the ordinary case - the reason concerns pressure, not safety

edges.label: Policy extends it
edges.when: a specific policy names required communication that should also be held, and says why

edges.label: on event
edges.when: an authoritative change to the condition that created the cooldown

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the ordinary end of a cooldown is that it expires, so the timeout is the normal path rather than the exception

edges.label: Reason has gone
edges.when: what justified the quiet period has been resolved earlier than expected

edges.label: Reason has hardened
edges.when: the situation has become one that warrants an explicit, reasoned suppression rather than a timed hold
a cooldown outgrown by its own cause

guardrails: A cooldown is not a global opt-out. Permission is untouched throughout.
A cooldown need not cover every channel, and covering all of them by default is how a quiet period becomes an unsearchable opt-out.
Expiry does not restart a stale campaign queue. What was held is discarded and eligibility is recalculated from the current state.
Required and safety communication is evaluated separately and is only held where a named policy says so.
governance.reusableRule: Cooldown temporarily reduces optional communication pressure without changing the underlying permission relationship.
governance.entityScope: person or account plus the communication context the cooldown was created for
governance.entityNote: A cooldown covers what its reason justifies. One that reaches every channel by default is an opt-out that nobody chose and nobody can find.

identity.title: Permission conflict → fail-safe state → reconcile → restore
identity.purpose: Hold optional communication closed while two systems disagree about permission, and reconcile on evidence rather than on whichever value allows more.

requires: two or more systems reporting different states for the same person, permission type, channel and purpose
insufficientAlone: a system that has not yet received a change that is still propagating within its SLA

nodes.headline: Conflicting permission states detected

Suppress the affected optional outbound communication immediately, before anything is collected or decided. This runs first on purpose: investigating while still sending resolves the uncertainty in favour of sending, which is the one outcome the journey exists to prevent

Collect from each participating system its state, source, timestamp, version and the provenance of the change. A timestamp alone is not authority - clocks disagree, and write order is not the order things were decided
Determine exactly which purpose, channel and scope combination is in dispute. Everything outside it is not in conflict and is not suppressed
Is a safe authoritative state immediately determinable from the evidence?
Record PERMISSION_CONFLICT and leave the fail-safe suppression in force. Being unresolved is a state worth naming rather than a gap between two states
until authoritative reconciliation completes, or a manual resolution is recorded
nodes.detail: timeout after the reconciliation horizon for this permission type

nodes.headline: Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a conflict that automated reconciliation could not settle

nodes.headline: Apply the established state and propagate the correction with origin and version, so a redelivered or out-of-order echo is discarded rather than treated as a new change - which is what turns a reconciliation into a synchronisation loop
Verify convergence across the systems that are required to agree, using idempotent versioned writes so verification cannot itself become another round of the exchange
Do all required systems now hold the resolved state?
Release the conflict state and re-evaluate what is eligible now. Communication withheld during the conflict is not replayed, whichever way the conflict resolved
conflict resolved, state converged, eligibility recalculated
nodes.detail: a fresh divergence on the same combination opens a new instance, and the log of this one is part of what the next is judged against

edges.label: Determinable
edges.when: provenance and version identify which record reflects the person's actual decision

edges.label: Not determinable
edges.when: the evidence does not establish which state is right - including the case where the more permissive one is newer, which is not the same as being correct

edges.label: on event
edges.when: authoritative reconciliation completes, a manual resolution is recorded

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: an unresolved conflict is safe but not free - it silently withholds communication someone may have wanted, so it is escalated rather than left to sit
a conflict that automated reconciliation could not settle

edges.label: Converged
edges.when: every required system reports the resolved state at the resolved version

edges.label: Still divergent
edges.when: at least one system has not converged after the correction

distinctFrom.because: CON-35 propagates a state it knows to be right. This one runs when nobody knows which state is right, which is why it starts by closing rather than by deciding.

guardrails: The more permissive state is never chosen because it is more permissive. Permissiveness is not evidence.
A system timestamp alone is not authority. Provenance and version are what identify the record that reflects a real decision.
The correction is propagated with origin and version and applied idempotently, so reconciliation cannot become a loop between two systems each correcting the other.
The fail-safe is scoped to the disputed combination. A conflict about one permission does not close everything.
governance.reusableRule: Distributed permission conflicts should fail safe until an authoritative state is established and verified across dependent systems.
governance.entityScope: person plus the specific permission type, channel and purpose that disagrees
governance.entityNote: Only the disputed combination is suppressed. A conflict about marketing email does not close service notices, and widening it would make the fail-safe worse than the failure.

identity.title: Ownership assignment → validate authority → assign or reject
identity.purpose: Establish an accountable controller for an entity, by an explicit act rather than by inference.

requires: a request to assign ownership of an identified entity to an identified party
insufficientAlone: somebody holding the highest access role, which is a permission level and not an assignment
somebody having created the entity, which is a fact about history rather than a standing accountability

nodes.headline: Ownership assignment requested

Validate that the entity supports ownership at all, that the assigning party holds the authority to assign it, the proposed owner's identity, their eligibility, the existing ownership state, and whether acceptance is required
Does this entity support an ownership relationship?
Record that this entity has no ownership relationship to assign. Not everything has an owner, and inventing one creates an accountability nobody granted and nobody can be held to
entity does not support ownership; nothing assigned
nodes.detail: the entity's model gaining an ownership concept makes assignment possible. Access and administration continue to be governed on their own terms

nodes.headline: Does the assigning party hold the authority to assign this?

Record the assignment rejected, naming what failed. Access permission is not ownership, and the highest access role is not the owner - an administrator can do everything an owner can do and is still not the party accountable for the entity
assignment rejected; existing ownership state unchanged
nodes.detail: an assignment by an authorized party, or by an eligible proposed owner, is assessed on its own terms

nodes.headline: Is the proposed owner eligible to hold this?
Would this assignment create a prohibited ownership configuration?
Block the assignment and record the configuration it would have produced. A prohibited ownership arrangement created by accident is usually discovered by an audit rather than by the people it affects
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: an assignment that would create a prohibited ownership configuration

nodes.headline: Must the proposed owner accept?
Record the assignment as awaiting acceptance. Nobody owns the entity on the strength of an unanswered invitation, and any existing ownership continues unchanged meanwhile
until the proposed owner accepts, or the proposed owner declines
nodes.detail: timeout after the acceptance window the assignment allows

nodes.headline: What did the proposed owner do?
Record the assignment declined. The entity's existing ownership state is untouched, and the decline is a fact worth keeping rather than a failure to retry
assignment declined; existing ownership unchanged
nodes.detail: a different proposed owner is a new assignment. Re-offering the same one changes nothing they have already answered

nodes.headline: Record the assignment as lapsed unanswered. Nothing was assigned, and this is not a decline - the proposed owner said nothing
assignment lapsed unanswered; existing ownership unchanged
nodes.detail: a renewed assignment to the same party is a new offer against the entity as it stands then

nodes.headline: Create the ownership relationship explicitly, recording who assigned it, on what authority, when, and what the owner is accountable for. Ownership is never inferred - it is a record somebody made, and that record is what any later dispute is resolved against
ownership assigned and recorded with its authority
nodes.detail: a change of owner runs through the transfer lifecycle rather than through a second assignment over the top of this one

edges.label: It does
edges.when: the entity type has an accountable controller as part of its model

edges.label: It does not
edges.when: the entity has access and administration but no ownership concept

edges.label: They do
edges.when: an existing owner, a governance rule or a defined authority permits it

edges.label: They do not
edges.when: nothing establishes their right to assign ownership of this entity

edges.label: Eligible
edges.when: the party meets whatever the entity requires of an owner

edges.label: Not eligible
edges.when: the party cannot hold ownership of this entity

edges.label: It would not
edges.when: the resulting ownership state is one the entity's rules permit

edges.label: It would
edges.when: the result would breach a separation, a limit or a governance constraint
an assignment that would create a prohibited ownership configuration

edges.label: They must
edges.when: ownership carries obligations the party has to take on knowingly

edges.label: They need not
edges.when: the assignment is within what the assigning authority may do unilaterally

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the proposed owner accepts, the proposed owner declines

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: an unanswered assignment left open indefinitely leaves an entity in a state where two parties each believe the other is accountable for it

edges.label: Accepted
edges.when: they took on the ownership

edges.label: Declined
edges.when: they refused it

distinctFrom.because: ACC-71 qualifies an entitlement - what somebody may do. This establishes who is accountable for the entity itself. An administrator can hold every entitlement the owner holds and still not be the party answerable for it.

guardrails: Access permission is not ownership.
An owner is never inferred from the highest access role.
Ownership assignment is explicit and auditable.
governance.reusableRule: Ownership exists only after an authorized assignment establishes an eligible party as the accountable controller of the entity.
governance.entityScope: the ownable entity and the ownership relationship being created on it
governance.entityNote: Ownership is a relationship somebody created. It is never derived from a role, a permission level or being the first account to touch the entity.

identity.title: Ownership transfer request → validate → pending acceptance or reject
identity.purpose: Propose a future controller without disturbing the one the entity currently has.

requires: a request to move ownership of an identified entity to an identified party

nodes.headline: Ownership transfer requested
Capture the entity, the current owner, the proposed owner, the requester, the request time, the transfer scope and any conditions attached to it

Record explicitly that the current owner remains authoritative. Nothing about their control changes because a request exists - revoking them on the invitation leaves the entity ownerless for the length of an unanswered email, and unanswered is the most common outcome
Does the requester hold the authority to transfer this entity?
Is the proposed owner eligible to hold this entity?
Is the entity transferable, and are the transfer's conditions satisfiable?
Record TRANSFER_REJECTED with what failed - authority, eligibility or transferability. The current owner is unaffected in every case
TRANSFER_REJECTED; the current owner remains the owner
nodes.detail: a transfer becoming possible - a different recipient, a cleared obligation, a proper authority - is a new request

nodes.headline: Is acceptance by the proposed owner required?

Record PENDING_ACCEPTANCE with the request version. The current owner is still the owner, still accountable, and still able to act - and the request can be withdrawn by them at any point before it completes
PENDING_ACCEPTANCE; ownership unchanged and the request outstanding
nodes.detail: acceptance runs through its own revalidation. A request pending for weeks is a claim about an entity as it was, and is checked against the entity as it is

nodes.headline: Ownership cutover → assign new owner → reconcile old owner
nodes.detail: a transfer authorized to proceed without recipient acceptance

edges.label: They do
edges.when: the current owner, or a governance rule, permits them to initiate this

edges.label: They do not
edges.when: nothing establishes their right to move this entity

edges.label: Eligible
edges.when: they meet what the entity requires of an owner

edges.label: Not eligible
edges.when: they cannot hold ownership of this entity

edges.label: Transferable
edges.when: nothing about the entity's state, obligations or governance prevents a transfer

edges.label: Not transferable
edges.when: an obligation, a hold or a rule prevents ownership moving now

edges.label: It is required
edges.when: ownership carries obligations the recipient must take on knowingly

edges.label: It is not
edges.when: policy permits the transfer to proceed on the requester's authority alone
a transfer authorized to proceed without recipient acceptance

distinctFrom.because: This validates that a transfer may be proposed at all. CTL-233 validates that it is still valid when somebody finally accepts it, which is a different question asked against a different state of the world.

guardrails: A transfer requested is not a transfer completed.
The current owner remains authoritative until the transfer is effective.
The current owner is never revoked merely because a request or invitation exists.
governance.reusableRule: An ownership transfer request proposes a future controller while preserving existing ownership until all transfer conditions are satisfied.
governance.entityScope: the entity, its current owner, the proposed owner and the transfer request between them
governance.entityNote: The request is a proposal. The current owner is unaffected by its existence, and remains the answer to who controls the entity.

identity.title: Ownership transfer acceptance → revalidate → execute or expire
identity.purpose: Check that a transfer accepted today is still the transfer that was proposed.

requires: an acceptance by the proposed owner against an identified transfer request

nodes.headline: Proposed owner accepts transfer
Has the acceptance deadline passed?
Record TRANSFER_EXPIRED. The acceptance arrived and the window had closed - nobody refused anything, and telling the recipient they were rejected misstates what happened
TRANSFER_EXPIRED; the current owner remains the owner
nodes.detail: a fresh transfer request against the entity as it now stands can be raised. This acceptance does not carry to it

nodes.headline: Re-read everything the request assumed - whether it is still active, whether the current owner is still the party it named, whether the recipient is still eligible, whether the entity is still transferable, whether its conditions still hold, and whether the request has been superseded
Does the transfer still hold against current state?

Record the acceptance as made against a stale request. A transfer invitation sent in March and accepted in June transfers an entity that may since have been sold, renamed, restructured or transferred to somebody else entirely
Record the acceptance refused on the recipient's current eligibility. They were eligible when invited and are not now, which is a fact about them rather than about the invitation
acceptance refused against current state; ownership unchanged
nodes.detail: a new transfer request against the entity as it now is can be raised and accepted on its own terms

nodes.headline: Record the acceptance bound to the exact request version, and authorize execution. Acceptance is not completion - nothing has moved, and the cutover is where control actually changes hands
Ownership cutover → assign new owner → reconcile old owner
nodes.detail: an acceptance revalidated against current state

edges.label: Still open
edges.when: the acceptance arrived inside the window the request allowed

edges.label: Passed
edges.when: the window closed before this acceptance arrived

edges.label: It holds
edges.when: the request is active, unsuperseded, and every assumption it made is still true

edges.label: The request was superseded or the entity changed
edges.when: ownership already moved, the entity was restructured, or a later request replaced this one

edges.label: The recipient is no longer eligible
edges.when: the proposed owner no longer meets what the entity requires
an acceptance revalidated against current state

guardrails: Acceptance is not transfer completion.
A stale invitation never transfers an entity that has since changed.
Acceptance binds to the exact transfer request version.
governance.reusableRule: Transfer acceptance authorizes ownership change only when the original transfer remains valid against the entity's current state.
governance.entityScope: the transfer request and the acceptance made against its specific version
governance.entityNote: Acceptance binds to a request version. The entity, the current owner and the recipient's eligibility can all have moved since the invitation went out.

identity.title: Ownership cutover → assign new owner → reconcile old owner
identity.purpose: Move control from one party to another without the entity being uncontrolled in between.

requires: a transfer revalidated and authorized against the entity's current state

nodes.headline: Ownership transfer authorized for execution

Establish the new owner relationship first, and only then touch the old one. The ordering is the whole point - removing the old owner before a valid new one exists leaves an entity nobody controls, and for entities requiring continuous ownership that gap is itself the failure

Verify the new ownership is actually authoritative - the relationship exists, it resolves, and the new owner can exercise control through it. Created is not effective, and a relationship written but not resolving leaves both parties unable to act on an entity they both believe somebody owns
Is the new ownership authoritative?

Abort the cutover, leaving the old owner in place entirely unchanged. A failed cutover that has already downgraded the old owner produces exactly the ownerless state this journey exists to prevent, and the recovery from that is far harder than a retried transfer
cutover aborted; the previous owner remains in place unchanged
nodes.detail: the transfer can be executed again once the new relationship can be established. Nothing about the current ownership was disturbed by the attempt

nodes.headline: Reconcile the previous owner's relationship according to policy - removed, converted to an administrator or member role, retained as a defined secondary relationship, or access removed entirely. Which one applies comes from policy rather than from a default of stripping them, and for a founder handing over a workspace the difference matters a great deal
Update the owner-dependent references and workflows to point at the current owner

Leave every historical action attributed to whoever performed it. The previous owner did what they did, and reattributing it to the new owner produces a record in which somebody appears to have taken actions before they had any relationship with the entity at all
Ownership change → transfer obligations → continue
nodes.detail: an ownership cutover completed

edges.label: It is
edges.when: the new owner resolves and can exercise control

edges.label: It is not
edges.when: the new relationship did not establish, or does not resolve
an ownership cutover completed

distinctFrom.because: TRM-104 transfers a primary relationship and its dependencies during account consolidation. This is the ownership control boundary specifically - establishing an accountable controller before removing the previous one, which is a sequencing requirement rather than a dependency migration.

guardrails: The old owner is never removed before a valid new owner exists, where continuous ownership is required.
Ownership transfer is atomic where the architecture permits it.
The previous owner's historical actions remain attributed to them.
governance.reusableRule: Ownership cutover establishes the new accountable controller before removing or downgrading the previous owner's current control.
governance.entityScope: the entity and both ownership relationships during the change
governance.entityNote: Both relationships exist briefly and deliberately. The order in which they are created and reconciled is the safety property.

identity.title: Delegation request → define scope → grant or reject
identity.purpose: Let somebody act on an owner's behalf, inside a boundary, without moving anything.

requires: a request to delegate defined authority over an identified entity to an identified party

nodes.headline: Delegation requested
Define the delegated scope, the actions it permits, its duration, the target entity, the delegator's authority, the delegate's eligibility, and the redelegation semantics where any are defined
May the delegator delegate this scope?

Reject the delegation, naming the part of the scope that exceeds the delegator's own. Delegated authority can never exceed the delegator's - a delegation broader than what they hold manufactures authority out of a form, and it will be exercised before anybody notices
delegation rejected; no authority granted
nodes.detail: a narrower delegation within the delegator's own authority, or one from a party who holds the scope, is assessed on its own terms

nodes.headline: Is the delegate eligible to receive this?
Reject the delegation on the delegate's eligibility, recorded separately from a scope rejection because the two lead somewhere different
Does the delegation include the right to redelegate?
Record the redelegation right as granted, with its own bound - a right to pass authority on that is itself unbounded produces a chain nobody can enumerate

Record that redelegation is not included. It is never assumed from silence - a delegate who may pass the authority on turns one bounded grant into a chain nobody can enumerate and nobody can revoke in one act

Record DELEGATED with the scope, the duration and the authority behind it. Delegation is not a transfer - the owner is still the owner, still accountable for the entity, and can revoke this at any point

Raise the actual capabilities through the access and entitlement mechanism, bounded to exactly the delegated scope. What the delegate can do is owned there; what they have been authorized to do is owned here, and implementing both in one place produces two sources of truth for one door
Is the delegation time-bounded?
Temporary delegation → expire → revoke, extend or restore
nodes.detail: a time-bounded delegation

nodes.headline: DELEGATED; bounded authority granted and ownership unchanged
nodes.detail: revocation runs through its own lifecycle and removes only what this delegation gave. A wider scope is a new delegation rather than an edit to this one

edges.label: They may
edges.when: the requested scope sits inside what the delegator holds and may pass on

edges.label: They may not
edges.when: the requested scope exceeds what the delegator holds, or is not theirs to delegate

edges.label: Eligible
edges.when: the party may hold delegated authority of this kind over this entity

edges.label: Not eligible
edges.when: the party cannot hold this authority

edges.label: Explicitly granted
edges.when: the delegator states that the delegate may pass this on

edges.label: Not stated
edges.when: the delegation says nothing about passing it on

edges.label: It is
edges.when: the delegation carries a validity period or an ending condition

edges.label: It is not
edges.when: the delegation stands until it is revoked
a time-bounded delegation

distinctFrom.because: A transfer moves accountability permanently to somebody else. A delegation lends bounded authority while the owner stays the owner, stays accountable, and can revoke it. Treating one as the other moves control nobody moved.

guardrails: Delegation is not ownership transfer.
A delegate never gains broader authority than the delegated scope.
Redelegation rights are never assumed from silence.
governance.reusableRule: Delegation grants bounded authority to act on behalf of an existing controller without changing the underlying ownership relationship.
governance.entityScope: the delegation, the delegator, the delegate and the target entity
governance.entityNote: Ownership does not change. The delegate acts with borrowed authority that the delegator still holds and can withdraw.

identity.title: Temporary delegation → expire → revoke, extend or restore
identity.purpose: End borrowed authority at its boundary, checking first that the boundary still belongs to a delegation that exists.

requires: a delegation with an explicit validity period or ending condition

nodes.headline: Delegation has validity boundary
Record the boundary as the delegation defines it, together with the delegation version this expiry is scheduled against
until the delegation is revoked early, or the delegation is replaced by a new authorization
nodes.detail: timeout after the delegation's own boundary

nodes.headline: What happened before the boundary?
Record this version as superseded and stand down its scheduled expiry. The new authorization carries its own boundary, and leaving this expiry live would end the successor at the predecessor's date
this delegation version superseded; its expiry stood down
nodes.detail: the successor version carries its own boundary and its own expiry, scheduled against itself

nodes.headline: At the boundary, re-read the current delegation version before doing anything. The scheduled job carries the version it was created against, and the delegation may have been extended, narrowed or replaced since - expiring the version in the job's hand ends a delegation that no longer exists in that form
Is this still the current delegation version?
Suppress the stale expiry. A job expiring last month's delegation cancels this month's, and the delegate loses authority they were explicitly granted days earlier
stale expiry suppressed; the current delegation version stands
nodes.detail: the current version's own boundary has its own expiry, scheduled against it

nodes.headline: Has an authorized extension been granted?

Record the extension as a new authorization referencing the original, rather than editing the original's dates. Rewriting the original makes it look as though it always ran to the new date, and the record of who extended it, when and why disappears entirely
extended by a new authorization; the original's history preserved
nodes.detail: the extension carries its own boundary and its own expiry, scheduled against the extended version

nodes.headline: Record the delegation expired at its boundary. An expired delegation is not an ownership change - the owner never moved, and the delegate simply stops acting for them
Delegation revoked → remove delegated authority → preserve independent access
nodes.detail: a delegation reaching its boundary without extension

nodes.headline: Delegation revoked → remove delegated authority → preserve independent access
nodes.detail: a delegation revoked before its boundary

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the delegation is revoked early, the delegation is replaced by a new authorization

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: reaching the boundary is what the wait exists for. It is the normal outcome, and the point at which the current delegation version is checked before anything is ended

edges.label: Revoked early
edges.when: an authority withdrew the delegation before its boundary

edges.label: Replaced by a new authorization
edges.when: a new delegation supersedes this one

edges.label: Still current
edges.when: no newer version of this delegation exists

edges.label: A newer version supersedes it
edges.when: the delegation was extended, narrowed or replaced after this expiry was scheduled

edges.label: It has
edges.when: an authority has extended the delegation before its boundary

edges.label: It has not
edges.when: the boundary arrives with no extension
a delegation reaching its boundary without extension
a delegation revoked before its boundary

guardrails: An expired delegation is not an ownership change.
A scheduled expiry is version-aware.
An extension never silently rewrites the original authorization's history.
governance.reusableRule: Temporary delegated authority ends automatically at its defined boundary unless a new authorized state explicitly extends it.
governance.entityScope: the time-bounded delegation and the version this expiry was scheduled against
governance.entityNote: The scheduled expiry carries a version. A delegation extended, narrowed or replaced since is a different delegation, and expiring the old one ends the wrong thing.

identity.title: Delegation revoked → remove delegated authority → preserve independent access
identity.purpose: Take back exactly what was lent, and nothing the delegate had of their own.

requires: an authorized revocation of a delegation, or a delegation reaching its boundary unextended

nodes.headline: Delegation revocation authorized
Mark the delegation REVOKED with the authority behind it and the moment it took effect

Determine which capabilities the delegate holds specifically because of this delegation, as against those they hold in their own right. This is the whole difficulty of the journey - a delegate who was already an administrator keeps being one, and removing everything is how a revocation locks somebody out of an account they independently run

Recalculate the delegate's authority from what remains, through the access mechanism, rather than by subtracting a remembered set. Subtraction from a snapshot taken at delegation time removes rights that were granted independently while the delegation was live
Does the delegate hold independent access or roles on this entity?

Preserve the independent rights explicitly, and record that they were preserved and why. An explicit record is what stops the next revocation, or the next audit, from concluding they were left behind by mistake
Is active work assigned to the delegate under this delegation?
Ownership change → transfer obligations → continue
nodes.detail: active work assigned under a revoked delegation

nodes.headline: Leave the delegated actions attributed as they were performed - by the delegate, on behalf of the delegator, under this delegation. Revocation ends future authority and rewrites no history, which is what makes the delegation record worth having at all
delegation-derived authority removed; independent rights preserved and history intact
nodes.detail: a fresh delegation to the same party is a new grant with its own scope. Nothing about this one is reactivated by it

edges.label: They do
edges.when: rights exist that were granted to them directly rather than through this delegation

edges.label: They do not
edges.when: everything they held here came from this delegation

edges.label: There is
edges.when: tasks, approvals or responsibilities were assigned to them as delegate

edges.label: There is not
edges.when: nothing is outstanding under the delegation
active work assigned under a revoked delegation

distinctFrom.because: ACC-74 handles entitlement loss for a party losing rights. This decides which of a party's rights were borrowed and which were their own - and its whole difficulty is that removing the wrong set locks somebody out of an account they independently administer.

guardrails: Revoking a delegation is not removing all of a user's access.
Independently granted roles are never removed.
Historical delegated actions remain auditable and attributed as performed.
governance.reusableRule: Delegation revocation removes only authority derived from that delegation while preserving unrelated rights held by the same actor.
governance.entityScope: the delegation and the capabilities that exist because of it
governance.entityNote: The delegate may hold rights from several sources. Only the ones derived from this delegation are in scope.

identity.title: Owner unavailable or invalid → protect entity → recover ownership
identity.purpose: Hold an entity safely when its owner cannot act, without handing it to whoever is nearest.

requires: authoritative evidence that the current owner cannot exercise valid control - departure, invalidity, incapacity, or a governance determination
insufficientAlone: an owner not logging in, which is inactivity rather than invalidity - an owner who has not appeared for a year is still the owner
somebody else asking for control on the grounds that the owner is gone

nodes.headline: Owner becomes unavailable or invalid

Determine whether the owner can still exercise valid control. Inactive is not invalid - a system that reassigns on inactivity takes an entity from somebody who never lost the right to it, and the first they hear of it is when they come back
What kind of condition is this?

Protect the entity and preserve the ownership where the governing rules permit. What is needed is a recovery path back to the owner rather than a replacement for them, and the entity is held rather than reassigned meanwhile
Account recovery request → prove control → restore secure access
nodes.detail: an owner temporarily unable to exercise control

nodes.headline: What governance applies to replacing this owner?

Initiate the authorized succession or transfer process. No new owner is selected here - arbitrarily promoting the highest-privileged administrator gives an entity to whoever happened to have the most access, which is a security model standing in for a governance decision
Ownership transfer request → validate → pending acceptance or reject
nodes.detail: a succession process nominating a new owner

nodes.headline: Apply only the governance mechanism that is actually defined, with its own scope and its own review point. An emergency control that has no defined end becomes a permanent reassignment nobody decided, and it is discovered years later as an administrator who turns out to own everything
May this entity remain ownerless?

Record OWNERLESS_PENDING explicitly. A named ownerless state is something somebody can find and act on; an entity whose owner field still points at an invalid party is a bug that surfaces at the worst possible moment
OWNERLESS_PENDING; the entity is protected and visibly without an owner
nodes.detail: an authorized assignment or succession gives it an owner. The state is deliberately visible rather than papered over with a nominal one

nodes.headline: Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: an entity whose ownership recovery has no defined governance path

edges.label: Temporary
edges.when: the owner is locked out, unreachable or incapacitated in a way that can resolve

edges.label: The owner is permanently invalid or gone
edges.when: authoritative evidence establishes they cannot return to control

edges.label: Not determinable
edges.when: whether this is temporary or permanent cannot be established
an owner temporarily unable to exercise control

edges.label: A defined succession or transfer process
edges.when: a contract, policy or governance rule states who may become owner and how

edges.label: A defined emergency controller mechanism
edges.when: a governance mechanism exists for interim control, with its own scope and review point

edges.label: Neither is defined
edges.when: nothing states who may replace this owner
a succession process nominating a new owner

edges.label: It may
edges.when: the entity's model and its obligations tolerate having no accountable controller for a period

edges.label: It may not
edges.when: the entity requires continuous ownership and no process exists to supply one
an entity whose ownership recovery has no defined governance path

guardrails: An inactive owner is not an automatically invalid owner.
A new owner is never arbitrarily selected.
Ownership recovery follows defined authority and governance rules.
governance.reusableRule: Loss of a valid owner should place the entity into a controlled ownership-recovery state rather than silently assigning control to another actor.
governance.entityScope: the entity and its ownership state while the owner cannot exercise control
governance.entityNote: The owner remains the owner throughout unless a defined governance process says otherwise. Unavailability is a condition, not a forfeiture.

identity.categoryTitle: Data change, import, migration & state transformation
identity.title: Data intake → identify format → parse or reject
identity.purpose: Get an incoming dataset into a stable readable form, without touching anything real while doing it.

requires: a dataset, file or import payload submitted or made available for a target context
insufficientAlone: a file appearing in a location, which may be a partial upload still being written

nodes.headline: Dataset submitted for intake

Capture the intake id, the source, the submitting actor or system, the receipt time, the declared data type, the expected schema or version where it is known, and the target context this is intended for
Is the representation readable and supported?
Record PARSE_REJECTED with what was expected and what actually arrived. Nothing has been read into the system, so nothing needs undoing - which is exactly why this check comes before anything else
PARSE_REJECTED; nothing was read and no state was touched
nodes.detail: a resubmission in a supported format is a new intake, assessed on its own terms

nodes.headline: Parse into a staging representation held apart from production. Parsing never partially mutates production state - a parse that fails halfway must leave nothing behind, and one that writes as it reads cannot make that promise
Did structural parsing succeed?

Record PARSE_FAILED with actionable diagnostics - which row, which field, what was expected and what was found. A parse error reported as an invalid file makes the submitter guess, and they will guess wrong several times before asking
PARSE_FAILED; staging discarded and production untouched
nodes.detail: a corrected payload is a new intake. The diagnostics from this one are what make correcting it possible

nodes.headline: Record PARSED against the staging representation. Structural parsing succeeding says the bytes made sense and says nothing whatever about whether the data does
Parsed data → validate schema and semantics → accept, reject or quarantine
nodes.detail: a payload parsed into a stable staging representation

edges.label: Supported
edges.when: the format is one the target can read, at a version it understands

edges.label: Not supported
edges.when: the format, encoding or version cannot be read

edges.label: Parsed
edges.when: the whole payload resolved into the staging representation

edges.label: Failed
edges.when: the structure broke down at some point in the payload
a payload parsed into a stable staging representation

guardrails: A file received is not valid data.
Successful parsing is not semantic validity.
Production state is never partially mutated during parsing.
governance.reusableRule: Data intake should first establish a stable parsed representation before any business validation or production mutation occurs.
governance.entityScope: the intake and the source artifact or dataset it carries
governance.entityNote: The intake is the submission. Nothing about it is in the system until a later stage puts it there.

identity.categoryTitle: Data change, import, migration & state transformation
identity.title: Parsed data → validate schema and semantics → accept, reject or quarantine
identity.purpose: Establish that the data is valid for the target it is going into, record by record where that is meaningful.

requires: a parsed staging representation against an identified target

nodes.headline: Input successfully parsed

Validate the required fields, the types, the identifiers, the references, the allowed values, the business invariants, the scope, the version compatibility and the duplicate semantics. Schema-valid is not business-valid - a well-formed row can reference an entity that does not exist, duplicate an identifier that must be unique, or carry a value the target has no meaning for

Classify each record VALID, INVALID or AMBIGUOUS where per-record classification is meaningful. Ambiguous is a real third answer rather than a soft invalid - it means the data could be read two ways, and the parser should not be the thing that chooses
Does any record carry an ambiguous mapping or value?

Halt on the ambiguous scope rather than coercing it. A value that could mean two things silently becomes whichever one the parser prefers, and the wrong one is discovered by whoever relies on it, months later, with no record of a choice having been made
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: ambiguous records requiring resolution before any mutation

nodes.headline: What are this import's acceptance semantics?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a dataset with undefined partial-acceptance semantics

nodes.headline: Under atomic semantics, is every record valid?

Reject the whole dataset under its atomic semantics, naming every record that failed and why. The submitter needs the full list rather than the first failure, because they will otherwise fix one and resubmit into the second
dataset rejected at validation; nothing applied
nodes.detail: a corrected dataset is a new intake and validates fresh against the target as it is then

nodes.headline: Is any record valid?

Quarantine the invalid records with their individual reasons, and carry forward only the valid scope. The quarantined records are held rather than dropped - they are the submitter's data, they need to come back, and a dropped row is indistinguishable from one that was never sent
Record the validated change scope, bound to this intake and this validation as a versioned change set. What follows applies this version and not whatever the staging area holds later
Valid data → preview and impact analysis → confirm or hold
nodes.detail: a validated change set ready to be assessed for impact

edges.label: Some are ambiguous
edges.when: a value, identifier or mapping could resolve more than one way

edges.label: None
edges.when: every record resolves unambiguously as valid or invalid
ambiguous records requiring resolution before any mutation

edges.label: Atomic
edges.when: the dataset is defined as all-or-nothing

edges.label: Partial acceptance is explicitly supported
edges.when: the import is defined to apply its valid scope and hold the rest

edges.label: Not defined
edges.when: nothing states whether part of this dataset may be applied
a dataset with undefined partial-acceptance semantics

edges.label: All valid
edges.when: no record fails validation

edges.label: At least one invalid
edges.when: any record fails

edges.label: Some are valid
edges.when: at least one record passes and can be applied on its own

edges.label: None
edges.when: every record fails validation
a validated change set ready to be assessed for impact

guardrails: Schema-valid is not business-valid.
Ambiguous values are never silently coerced.
Partial acceptance semantics are explicit rather than assumed.
Quarantined records are held with reasons rather than dropped.
governance.reusableRule: Parsed data becomes importable only after both structural and business-level validity have been established for the scope that will be applied.
governance.entityScope: the parsed dataset and the target's schema and business rules
governance.entityNote: Validation produces a scope that will be applied, which is not necessarily the whole dataset. What is excluded is held rather than dropped.

identity.categoryTitle: Data change, import, migration & state transformation
identity.title: Valid data → preview and impact analysis → confirm or hold
identity.purpose: Show what the mutation would actually do, so an approval attaches to that rather than to a filename.

entry.trigger: Validated change set ready to mutate
requires: a validated change set with an identified target scope

nodes.headline: Validated change set ready to mutate

Calculate the proposed delta - the creates, the updates, the deletes or deactivations, the conflicts, the records that would not change at all, the relationship changes, and the downstream entities affected

Surface the destructive changes explicitly rather than inside an aggregate count. Four thousand records processed hides the three hundred deactivations inside it, and the person confirming reads the total and approves the deletion without ever seeing it
Does this change set require confirmation or approval?
Does the impact cross a risk or approval threshold?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a change set crossing a risk or approval threshold

nodes.headline: Present the impact summary bound to this exact change-set version. A confirmation that binds to the intake rather than the version approves whatever the change set later becomes, including a regenerated one nobody looked at
until the change set is confirmed, or the change set is rejected
nodes.detail: timeout after the window this change set remains valid against the target

nodes.headline: What was decided?
Record the change set as rejected with the reason, and apply nothing
change set rejected; nothing applied
nodes.detail: a revised change set is a new validation and a new preview rather than a resubmission of this one

nodes.headline: Check the change set still describes the same mutation against the target as it now is. Target state moves while somebody reads a summary, and applying a delta computed against a state that has since changed applies edits nobody previewed
Does the delta still describe the same mutation?

Regenerate the delta against current state and present it again. The previous confirmation was for a different mutation and does not carry - a confirmation reused across a regenerated delta is an approval of something nobody saw
Record the change set as expired unconfirmed. Nothing was applied, and the validated data is still held - what lapsed is the authorization window rather than the data
change set expired unconfirmed; nothing applied
nodes.detail: the same data can be re-previewed against the target as it is then, which is a new delta and a new confirmation

nodes.headline: Import execution → apply idempotently → complete, partial or fail
nodes.detail: a change set authorized to mutate the target

edges.label: It does not
edges.when: the change is routine and within what the import is authorized to do unattended

edges.label: It does
edges.when: the scope, the destructiveness or the policy calls for somebody to confirm

edges.label: It crosses
edges.when: the delta's size, destructiveness or reach exceeds what a simple confirmation covers

edges.label: Within threshold
edges.when: a confirmation from the requesting party is sufficient
a change set crossing a risk or approval threshold

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the change set is confirmed, the change set is rejected

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a delta computed against a target that has since moved describes a mutation that no longer exists, and confirming it applies edits nobody previewed

edges.label: Confirmed
edges.when: somebody with the authority approved the presented delta

edges.label: Rejected
edges.when: the change set was refused

edges.label: Unchanged
edges.when: the target has not moved in any way the delta depends on

edges.label: Changed
edges.when: the target has moved and the delta would now do something different
a change set authorized to mutate the target

guardrails: The preview represents the mutation that would actually occur.
Destructive changes are never hidden inside aggregate counts.
Confirmation binds to the specific change-set version.
governance.reusableRule: High-impact data changes should expose their proposed delta before execution so authorization applies to the mutation that will actually occur.
governance.entityScope: the validated change set and the target state it would mutate
governance.entityNote: The preview is computed against the target as it is now. Target state moves while somebody reads a summary, and the confirmation binds to the version that was shown.

identity.categoryTitle: Data change, import, migration & state transformation
identity.title: Import execution → apply idempotently → complete, partial or fail
identity.purpose: Apply a fixed validated change set to production state, keeping every record's outcome.

requires: a confirmed change set with authorization bound to its version

nodes.headline: Import authorized for execution

Freeze and reference the exact input and change-set version being applied. What is applied is a fixed set - a change set still reading from a moving source applies something other than what was approved, and nobody can say afterwards what that was

Give each record operation a stable identity derived from the change set and the record, so a retry re-applies the same operation rather than performing a second one. Without it, the second run of a partly-failed import creates duplicates of everything that succeeded the first time, and those duplicates look exactly like real data

Apply the changes, recording each record's outcome - created, updated, unchanged, skipped, failed or unknown. Unchanged and skipped are distinct and both worth keeping: one means the data already matched, the other means we chose not to touch it, and only the second needs explaining
How did the execution end?

Record IMPORT_APPLIED with the change-set version and the per-record execution history. The history identifies which records changed - an import that reports a count and not a list cannot be audited, corrected or partially undone
IMPORT_APPLIED; every record outcome recorded against the change-set version
nodes.detail: an error discovered in what was applied is a transformation error with its own correction path rather than a re-run of this import

nodes.headline: Record PARTIALLY_APPLIED with the per-record outcomes intact. The successful scope is a real result and stays that way - classifying the whole import as failed because part of it was discards work that is already correct in production
Partial import → isolate failed scope → correct → resume
nodes.detail: an import completing with mixed outcomes

nodes.headline: Roll back or compensate to the boundary the atomic semantics define. What is undone is this operation's own mutations and nothing else - anything that happened to those records from another source in the meantime is not this import's to revert
Did the rollback complete cleanly?
atomic import failed and fully reverted; target state as it was
nodes.detail: a corrected dataset is a new import. The failed attempt stays in the record because it explains any transient effect anybody observed

nodes.headline: external:external-status-reconciliation
nodes.detail: a rollback that could not be completed or verified

an import completing with mixed outcomes

edges.when: every mutation this import made has been reverted

edges.label: Incomplete or uncertain
edges.when: some mutations could not be reverted, or their state is unknown
a rollback that could not be completed or verified

distinctFrom.because: OPS-121 runs a unit of async work and reports whether it finished. This mutates production data from a validated set, so its outcomes are per-record rather than per-job and its defining requirement is that re-running it does not create a second copy of everything that already worked.

guardrails: A retry never duplicates created records.
An import with confirmed successful scope is not classified as wholly failed.
Execution history identifies which records changed.

identity.categoryTitle: Data change, import, migration & state transformation
identity.title: Partial import → isolate failed scope → correct → resume
identity.purpose: Fix only what did not land, without touching the records that already did.

requires: an import with per-record outcomes including at least one unresolved record

nodes.headline: Import completed with mixed outcomes

Partition the outcomes into successful, retryable failures, data failures, unknowns and skipped. Each needs a different response, and treating them as one bucket either re-runs what already worked or abandons what could still be fixed

Mark the confirmed successful records as not to be re-applied. A partial import is not a total failure - re-running the whole dataset to fix forty rows re-touches thousands that were already right, and any of those re-touches is a fresh opportunity to break something that worked
Are any record outcomes unknown?

Hold the unknown scope out of any replay until it is reconciled. Replaying a record that may have been created produces two of it, and in an import that duplicate is indistinguishable from a legitimate row and will be found by whoever runs a report
external:external-status-reconciliation
nodes.detail: records whose import outcome could not be established

nodes.headline: What do the unresolved records need?

Retry only the unresolved scope, using the same stable operation identity so a record that actually succeeded is not created a second time. The successful scope is not part of the retry at all - it is not re-read, re-validated or re-applied
Does retry budget remain?
retrying the unresolved scope only; successful records untouched
nodes.detail: each retry reports its own per-record outcomes and returns here with the unresolved set smaller and the budget one lower

nodes.headline: Create a corrected change set covering only the unresolved records, linked to the original import. The correction does not touch the already-successful records - silently changing them turns a fix into a second incident, and one nobody is looking for
Parsed data → validate schema and semantics → accept, reject or quarantine
nodes.detail: a corrected change set covering the unresolved scope

nodes.headline: Record the unresolved scope as unrecovered, with the reason for each record. The submitter needs to know exactly what did not land - an import reported as done with a silent shortfall is worse than one reported as failed
successful scope applied and preserved; unresolved scope recorded as unrecovered
nodes.detail: a fresh submission covering the unrecovered records is a new intake, linked to this one so the shortfall is traceable
