Record ISSUED and nothing more. Issuance is the artifact existing in fixed, identifiable form - whether it has any effect is a separate question with its own conditions, and a contract can exist in final form and bind nobody
ISSUED and immutable; effect not established
nodes.detail: any later change creates a new version through the amendment lifecycle. This version is never reopened, edited or reissued under the same identifier

nodes.headline: Record the effective semantics exactly as the document states them, without inventing any. A document type that takes effect at issue says so; assuming it on behalf of one that does not brings terms into force early
Signed document → validate completion → effective or pending condition
nodes.detail: an issued document whose own terms make it effective without signature

edges.label: Not by itself
edges.when: effect depends on signature, a date, a condition or another dependency

edges.label: Effective on issue, by its own terms
edges.when: the document type takes effect at issuance without further conditions
an issued document whose own terms make it effective without signature

guardrails: A draft is not an issued document.
An issued document never silently changes.
Issuance does not automatically make a document effective.
governance.reusableRule: Issuance freezes an auditable version of a document so later changes create new versions rather than rewriting what was previously issued.
governance.entityScope: the document and the specific version being issued
governance.entityNote: This is the boundary between an editable draft and an authoritative record. After it, change means a successor.

identity.title: Document distribution → send or provide access → confirm or fail
identity.purpose: Get a specific issued version to the party who should have it, without either fact touching the other.

requires: an issued document version with a party who is to receive it

nodes.headline: Issued document requires distribution

Resolve the intended recipient and the route permitted for a document of this type. A document reaching the wrong party is worse than one not sent - the second can be retried and the first cannot be recalled

Bind the distribution to the exact issued version. Sending an outdated version is the failure this step exists to prevent: the recipient then holds, relies on, and may sign terms that nobody currently offers

Raise the actual delivery through the canonical communication mechanism, which owns channels, permissions, retries and delivery evidence. Document distribution does not build its own delivery path - a parallel one will disagree with the canonical delivery record about whether the contract was ever sent
until the distribution is confirmed to the level the requirement demands, or the distribution authoritatively fails
nodes.detail: timeout after the distribution window the requirement allows

nodes.headline: How did the distribution resolve?

Record DELIVERED or AVAILABLE against the exact version distributed. Delivery state describes the distribution and never the document - an undelivered contract is a valid contract nobody has, and treating delivery as validity turns a mail failure into a legal one
the identified version reached the intended recipient; the document's validity is unchanged by this
nodes.detail: a superseding version requires its own distribution. Nothing about this one is retracted by that - the recipient was correctly given what was current then

nodes.headline: Record the distribution outcome as unknown and do not treat it as delivered. The document's validity is untouched either way - what is unknown is whether anybody has it
external:external-status-reconciliation
nodes.detail: a distribution whose outcome could not be established

nodes.headline: Delivery failure → classify → retry, fallback or stop
nodes.detail: a failed document distribution

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the distribution is confirmed to the level the requirement demands, the distribution authoritatively fails

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a distribution neither confirmed nor failed leaves nobody able to say whether the recipient has the document, which is the one thing distribution exists to establish

edges.label: Confirmed
edges.when: delivery or availability is established to the level the requirement demands

edges.label: Failed
edges.when: the channel authoritatively reports it did not arrive
a distribution whose outcome could not be established
a failed document distribution

guardrails: A document being issued is not the recipient having received it.
Sending a wrong or outdated version is prevented by binding distribution to a version.
Distribution reuses the canonical communication mechanics rather than duplicating them.
governance.reusableRule: Document distribution delivers a specific issued version to an intended recipient without changing the document's underlying validity or status.
governance.entityScope: the issued version, the intended recipient, and the distribution of one to the other
governance.entityNote: The distribution is bound to a version. Delivery state describes the distribution and never the document.

identity.title: Signature request → await signatures → signed, declined or expired
identity.purpose: Collect the required signatures against one exact version, and know when they are actually all there.

requires: an issued or prepared document version requiring signature by identified parties

nodes.headline: Document requires signature
Define the required signers, the signing authority each of them needs, the signing order where one applies, the scope of what is being signed, and the validity window where one is defined
Is a signature validity window defined?
Record the window as defined, so the request's own terms decide when it lapses
Record that no expiry was set rather than assigning one. An invented signature deadline voids a request nobody withdrew, and the signer discovers it at the moment their signature is refused

Record AWAITING_SIGNATURE and issue the request to each required signer, bound to the exact document version. A signature request that does not name a version collects marks against nothing anybody can identify afterwards
until a required signer signs, or a signer declines, or the document version is superseded
nodes.detail: timeout after the validity window where one is defined, and the process's own review point where none is

nodes.headline: What happened?
Record the signature evidence - who signed, when, which version, and under what authority. The version is part of the evidence rather than context around it
Are all required signatures now complete?

Record FULLY_SIGNED against this version. One signature is not a signed document when several are required, and a process that proceeds on the first one proceeds on an agreement that does not exist yet
Signed document → validate completion → effective or pending condition
nodes.detail: a document with all required signatures complete

nodes.headline: Record DECLINED with the signer and the reason where one was given. A decline is a business outcome rather than a failure, and the process that required the document decides what follows from it
external:operational-resolution
nodes.detail: a required signer declining

nodes.headline: End the signature process because the version it was against no longer stands, and suppress the outstanding requests. Signatures already collected are not carried to the successor - the successor is a different document, and signing it is a new request
signature process ended; its version was superseded before completion
nodes.detail: the successor version raises its own signature process. The signatures collected here remain evidence about the version they were made against

nodes.headline: Record SIGNATURE_EXPIRED. The request lapsed - nobody declined and nothing was decided, and reporting it as a refusal misstates what the signer did
SIGNATURE_EXPIRED; signatures collected so far remain evidence, the set is incomplete
nodes.detail: a fresh request against the same version is a new process. Whether the partial signatures still count is governed by the document's own rules rather than assumed

edges.label: Defined
edges.when: the process or the document states how long the request stands

edges.label: Not defined
edges.when: nothing states an expiry for the request

edges.label: on event
edges.when: a required signer signs, a signer declines, the document version is superseded

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a signature request open indefinitely leaves a process waiting on an agreement that will not arrive, with nobody having decided to abandon it

edges.label: A required signer signed the correct version
edges.when: the signature is against the version this process governs, by a signer with the required authority

edges.label: A signer declined
edges.when: a required signer refused

edges.label: The version was superseded
edges.when: the document this process is bound to is no longer the current one

edges.label: All complete
edges.when: every required signer has signed the governed version

edges.label: Some remain
edges.when: at least one required signature is outstanding
a document with all required signatures complete
a required signer declining

distinctFrom.because: DEC-183 is somebody exercising judgment against criteria. This is collecting authorized marks against a fixed artifact - nobody is deciding anything on the merits, and its failure modes are version binding, incomplete sets and expiry rather than authority to conclude.

guardrails: A signature requested is not a signature made.
One signature is not a fully signed document when several are required.
A signature binds to the exact document version.
A signature expiry is never invented.
governance.reusableRule: A signature process completes only when the required authorized parties have signed the exact document version governed by that process.
governance.entityScope: the document version, the signature process against it, and each required signer
governance.entityNote: The process is bound to a version. Signatures do not carry to a successor - a changed document is a new request.

identity.title: Signed document → validate completion → effective or pending condition
identity.purpose: Establish when a document actually starts doing something, which is not when it was signed.

requires: all required signatures complete against one version, or an issued document whose own terms make it effective without signature

nodes.headline: Document completion established

Validate that every required signature is present, that each is against the correct version, that each signer held the authority they signed under, which conditions apply, and what the effective date is
Does the completion hold up?

Record the completion as not established, naming exactly what fails. A document that looks signed and is not is the most dangerous state in this category, because everything downstream will treat it as agreement
Document or record conflict → determine authoritative version → reconcile
nodes.detail: signatures that do not bind to the version they are held against

nodes.headline: What governs when this takes effect?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a completed document with no defined effectiveness rules

nodes.headline: Record PENDING_EFFECTIVE_DATE. The document is complete and does nothing yet, which is a real state and not an incomplete one
until the document is superseded or revoked before its date
nodes.detail: timeout after the effective date

nodes.headline: Record PENDING_CONDITION, naming the dependency. A document waiting on an unstated condition is indistinguishable from one that is simply stuck
until the dependency is satisfied, or the dependency becomes unsatisfiable
nodes.detail: timeout after the window the document or its process allows for the condition

nodes.headline: How did the dependency resolve?

Re-read the document's current standing at the effective moment - is this still the authoritative version, has it been superseded or revoked, do the parties still stand. A stale signed version activating a newer business state is exactly the failure the version binding exists to prevent
Does the document still stand at its effective moment?
Record that the document did not take effect, because it was superseded or revoked first. It remains a validly issued and validly signed record of what was agreed - it simply never became operative
Record the condition as unsatisfiable and the document as never effective, naming which dependency failed
complete and never effective; the signed record stands as history
nodes.detail: a successor document runs its own effectiveness. Nothing here is deleted - a signed agreement that never came into force is still evidence of what the parties agreed to

nodes.headline: Record EFFECTIVE with the version, the moment, and what made it so. This is the document's own state - what it then causes elsewhere is a different lifecycle and is not implied by this
Does this document taking effect create or change a business state elsewhere?
external:operational-resolution
nodes.detail: an effective document that starts something elsewhere

nodes.headline: EFFECTIVE; the document is in force from the recorded moment
nodes.detail: expiry, revocation or supersession each end future reliance on it through their own lifecycles, and none of them changes that it was effective while it was

edges.label: It holds
edges.when: signatures, versions and authorities all check out

edges.label: It does not
edges.when: a signature is against the wrong version, or a signer lacked the authority
signatures that do not bind to the version they are held against

edges.label: Effective on valid signature
edges.when: the document's terms make completion sufficient

edges.label: A future effective date
edges.when: the document names a date after completion

edges.label: A further dependency
edges.when: effect waits on a condition, an approval or an external event

edges.label: The rules do not define effectiveness
edges.when: nothing states when or whether this document takes effect
a completed document with no defined effectiveness rules

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the document is superseded or revoked before its date

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: reaching the effective date is what this wait exists for. It is the normal outcome, and the point at which the document's current standing is checked again

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the dependency is satisfied, the dependency becomes unsatisfiable

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a signed document waiting forever on a condition that will not arrive is an agreement in limbo, and both parties are entitled to know which it is

edges.label: Satisfied
edges.when: the condition governing effect is met

edges.label: Unsatisfiable
edges.when: the condition cannot now be met

edges.label: Still authoritative
edges.when: this version is current, unsuperseded and unrevoked

edges.label: Superseded or revoked
edges.when: something replaced or withdrew it before it took effect

edges.label: It does
edges.when: a relationship, an entitlement, an obligation or an authorization begins from it

edges.label: It does not
edges.when: the document's effect is entirely a matter of the record itself
an effective document that starts something elsewhere

distinctFrom.because: SUB-161 makes a continuing relationship active. This makes a document effective, which may be what triggers that - but a document can be effective without creating a relationship, and a relationship can activate without any document.

guardrails: Signed is not automatically effective.
Legal or business effectiveness rules are never invented.
A stale or superseded signed version never activates newer business state.
Effectiveness is revalidated at the effective moment rather than assumed from completion.
governance.reusableRule: Signing establishes documented agreement or authorization; effectiveness begins only when the conditions governing that document's effect are satisfied.
governance.entityScope: the completed document version and the effect it is to have
governance.entityNote: Effectiveness is the document's own state. What it then causes elsewhere is a different lifecycle with its own entity.

identity.title: Document change → new version or amendment → supersede prospectively
identity.purpose: Change an issued artifact by creating a successor, leaving what it replaces exactly as it was.

requires: an authorized need to change an issued document, with the authority established
insufficientAlone: an error being noticed, which identifies a need rather than authorizing a change

nodes.headline: Authorized document change required
Identify the base version, the changed scope, the authority for the change, its effective semantics and the parties it affects
What form does the successor take?
Create the successor as a new draft version, carrying the base forward with the change incorporated. The base version is not touched
Create an amendment that references the base version rather than restating it. What changed stays legible as a change, which a full reissue makes somebody diff two documents to discover

Record the lineage - this successor, its base, the authority and what changed. Lineage is what makes a document history readable; without it a chain of versions is a set of unrelated files with similar names and nobody can say which one anybody signed
until the successor completes its own validation, approval and signature requirements, or the change is abandoned
nodes.detail: timeout after the window the change process allows

nodes.headline: Did the successor become authoritative?
Record the change as abandoned. The base version stands unchanged and unmarked - a superseded flag set in anticipation of a successor that never arrived leaves the current document looking obsolete
change abandoned; the base version remains current and unmarked
nodes.detail: the change can be attempted again as a new successor against whatever version is current then

nodes.headline: Mark the prior version SUPERSEDED for applicable future use. Superseded is not deleted and not historically invalid - the prior version governed everything that happened while it was current, and that stays true regardless of what replaced it
When do the successor's terms apply?

Apply the new terms only from the successor's own effective conditions. Applying them before it is effective enforces terms nobody has agreed to yet, and applying them backwards makes a compliant history retroactively non-compliant
successor authoritative going forward; the prior version preserved and superseded
nodes.detail: a further change creates its own successor against this one, extending the lineage rather than replacing it

nodes.headline: Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a successor with undefined effective semantics

edges.label: A new version
edges.when: the document is reissued in full with the change incorporated

edges.label: An amendment
edges.when: a separate instrument modifies the base while leaving it standing

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the successor completes its own validation, approval and signature requirements, the change is abandoned

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a successor stuck in progress leaves two versions in play and no clear answer about which governs, which is the exact ambiguity the lineage exists to prevent

edges.label: It did
edges.when: the successor completed validation, approval and any required signatures

edges.label: Abandoned
edges.when: the change was withdrawn or could not complete

edges.label: From its own effective conditions
edges.when: the successor states when it takes effect

edges.label: The effective semantics are not defined
edges.when: nothing states when the new terms begin
a successor with undefined effective semantics

guardrails: A new version does not delete the old version.
Superseded is not historically invalid.
New terms are never applied before the successor's required effective conditions.
Lineage between base and successor is recorded rather than implied.
governance.reusableRule: Document changes create a traceable successor version whose authority begins according to its own approval and effective conditions.
governance.entityScope: the document lineage and the successor version or amendment being created
governance.entityNote: Lineage is the entity. A version without a recorded base and authority is an unrelated file that happens to share a name.

identity.title: Document expiry → revalidate requirement → renew, replace or close
identity.purpose: End future reliance on a time-limited artifact, and stop only what genuinely needs it to be current.

requires: a time-limited document approaching or reaching its defined expiry

nodes.headline: Document validity reaches expiry
Is the expiry defined by the document or its governing rules?

Record that this document carries no expiry, rather than assigning one. Inventing an expiry invalidates something nobody invalidated, and dependent processes then start failing for a reason that does not exist anywhere in the rules
no expiry defined; the document remains valid until something else ends it
nodes.detail: an authority withdrawing it runs through revocation, and a successor replacing it runs through amendment. Neither is expiry

nodes.headline: Determine the active and future processes that depend on this document's current validity. What expires is future reliance - nothing that happened while it was valid changes, and the list is of what needs it now rather than of what ever used it
Record EXPIRED. Expired is not revoked: nobody withdrew it, its time ran out, and everything it authorized while valid remains authorized
Do the governing rules require a replacement or renewal?
Raise a new document requirement, linked to the expired artifact so the successor's purpose is traceable to what it replaces
Document requirement → determine artifact → create, reuse or waive
nodes.detail: an expired document the rules require to be replaced

nodes.headline: May the dependent processes continue after expiry?
Leave the dependent processes running under the rules that permit it, recording that the artifact expired and that they continue by rule rather than by oversight
EXPIRED; dependent processes continue under rules that permit it
nodes.detail: a future action that does require current validity is blocked at its own point rather than by pre-emptively stopping everything

nodes.headline: Block only the future actions that require a currently valid document. Everything not requiring current validity continues - one expired certificate stopping an entire relationship is a suspension nobody decided and nobody can find the authority for
EXPIRED; only the actions requiring current validity are blocked
nodes.detail: a replacement artifact releases the blocked actions. Actions performed while the document was valid remain historical facts

nodes.headline: Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: an expired document whose effect on dependent processes the rules do not define

edges.label: Defined
edges.when: the document or a rule states when its validity ends

edges.label: Not defined
edges.when: no expiry was ever set for this artifact

edges.label: They require one
edges.when: a current artifact must exist for the process to continue

edges.label: They do not
edges.when: no replacement is mandated by the rules
an expired document the rules require to be replaced

edges.label: They may
edges.when: the governing rules permit them to run on without a current artifact

edges.label: Future actions require current validity
edges.when: specific future actions need a valid document and the rest do not

edges.label: The rules do not say
edges.when: nothing states what the dependent processes do after expiry
an expired document whose effect on dependent processes the rules do not define

distinctFrom.because: Expiry is time running out on terms the document itself set. Revocation is an authority withdrawing it. Nobody decided the first, somebody decided the second, and they carry different consequences for what was relied on meanwhile.

guardrails: Expired is not revoked.
Expiration dates are never invented.
Actions performed while the document was valid remain historical facts.
Only processes requiring current validity are affected.
governance.reusableRule: Document expiry ends future reliance on a time-limited artifact according to its governing rules without rewriting actions completed while it was valid.
governance.entityScope: the time-limited document and the processes depending on its current validity
governance.entityNote: What expires is future reliance. Everything done while it was valid was done while it was valid.

identity.title: Document revocation or withdrawal → stop future reliance → reconcile
identity.purpose: Withdraw an artifact by an authority's decision, exactly as far as that decision reaches.

requires: a revocation or withdrawal by an authority entitled to make it
insufficientAlone: a document expiring, which is time rather than a decision
a successor being issued, which supersedes rather than revokes

nodes.headline: Authoritative revocation occurs
Record the revoked version, the authority, the reason and its category, the revocation time, and the revocation's own effective semantics

Record REVOKED, preserving the document and everything about it. A revoked document's history stays available - it is the evidence for everything done while it stood, and deleting it destroys the explanation for actions that were entirely correct at the time
Identify the pending and future processes relying on this document
What does the revocation's effective scope permit going forward?
Block or revalidate the affected processes, which now have no valid artifact behind them

Apply exactly the scope the revocation names, and nothing wider. A revocation applied more broadly than its own terms withdraws things the authority did not withdraw, and there is no record of who decided that because nobody did
What does the revocation say about actions already completed?
Apply the retroactive consequence the revocation actually states, recording the authority for it. What is applied is what was stated - a revocation that reaches backwards has to say so, and how far

Leave completed actions as they stand. Retroactive invalidity is not inferred - assuming it turns every past action taken under a now-revoked certificate into a problem nobody has decided is a problem, and unwinding them is far harder than not unwinding them
Is a replacement artifact required?
Document requirement → determine artifact → create, reuse or waive
nodes.detail: a revoked document that still needs replacing

nodes.headline: REVOKED; future reliance stopped within the revocation's scope, history preserved
nodes.detail: the revocation being itself withdrawn or narrowed is a further authoritative act, recorded on top rather than by clearing this one

edges.label: No future reliance at all
edges.when: the revocation withdraws the document entirely from here on

edges.label: Limited scope, some reliance continues
edges.when: the revocation names a scope narrower than the whole document

edges.label: It explicitly reaches them
edges.when: the revocation states a retroactive consequence and the authority for it

edges.label: It says nothing about them
edges.when: the revocation addresses future reliance only

edges.label: One is required
edges.when: the processes that relied on this still need a valid artifact

edges.label: None
edges.when: nothing further requires an artifact of this kind
a revoked document that still needs replacing

distinctFrom.because: An amendment replaces a document with a successor that carries the same purpose forward. Revocation withdraws it with nothing behind it - there may be no successor, and the reason is a decision rather than a change of terms.

guardrails: Revoked is not expired.
A revoked document's history remains available and auditable.
Retroactive consequences are never inferred without explicit authority.
The revocation applies exactly its own stated scope.
governance.reusableRule: Revocation stops reliance on a document according to the revocation's effective scope while preserving the historical record of the artifact and prior actions.
governance.entityScope: the revoked document version and the revocation acting on it
governance.entityNote: The revocation has its own effective scope. Applying it more widely withdraws things the authority did not withdraw.

identity.title: Document or record conflict → determine authoritative version → reconcile

Record DOCUMENT_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED and change nothing. The newest file is not automatically the authoritative version - recency is a property of a filesystem and authority is a property of an issuance, and picking the newer one is how a superseded draft becomes the contract
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a conflict where the authoritative version cannot be safely determined

nodes.headline: Record which version is authoritative and why, preserving every conflicting record alongside it. Conflicting evidence is not deleted to tidy the state - it is the only proof the conflict happened, and the only way to work out afterwards what anybody actually relied on

Record that the signature does not bind to the authoritative version, without discarding the signature. It is valid evidence for the version it was made against and for no other, however similar the content of the two looks

nodes.headline: Was a non-authoritative version distributed or acted upon?

Preserve what was done and under which version it was done. The action happened - what to do about it is a separate question with its own authority, and rewriting the record to show the right version leaves an effect with no cause
Remedy selection → resolve obligation → financial handoff if needed
nodes.detail: a business action taken on a non-authoritative document version

nodes.headline: authoritative version established; conflicting records preserved and explained
nodes.detail: a further inconsistency in this lineage is assessed with this reconciliation as part of its evidence, which is why none of it was deleted

edges.when: it describes something that does not usually change - a role, an industry, a structural constraint

edges.label: Volatile
edges.when: it describes a current situation - a project, a season, a temporary goal

edges.label: Affected
edges.when: a live journey would make a different decision knowing this

edges.label: Nothing affected
edges.when: nothing running depends on it, whatever it might inform later

distinctFrom.because: CON-32 records how someone wants to be communicated with. This records what they are trying to achieve, which shapes product and journey decisions rather than message delivery.

guardrails: Declared data is never overwritten by behavioural inference.
The attribute is used only where a decision genuinely depends on it. Personalisation that references something for the sake of referencing it reveals the mechanism.
A need or preference signal is not permission to communicate.
governance.reusableRule: Declared relationship context should influence only the decisions that genuinely depend on it.
governance.entityScope: person or account plus the declared attribute, at the scope it was declared for
governance.entityNote: A declared attribute belongs to the context it was given in. A goal stated for one product is not a goal for another.

identity.title: Missing critical data → request or resolve → resume
identity.purpose: Treat a genuinely blocking data gap as a named dependency, and keep it distinct from wanting to know more about someone.

requires: a named business process that cannot safely proceed, and the specific field, document or value it is waiting on
insufficientAlone: a profile field that would be useful to have
data that would improve a future decision while blocking nothing today

nodes.headline: Required data missing and blocking
Identify the exact missing item and the named process it blocks. A request that cannot name what it unblocks is progressive profiling wearing a blocker's clothes, and the two must not be confusable
Can an authoritative source supply this without asking anyone?
Retrieve and reconcile it. Asking someone for what we already hold authoritatively is the fastest way to demonstrate that we do not know our own records
Request it from the actor who can actually provide it - which is often not the customer - stating what it unblocks, so the request is answerable rather than merely received
until the data arrives
nodes.detail: timeout after the SLA of the process being blocked

nodes.headline: Is what we now have valid?
Persist it and re-evaluate the blocked process, which resumes because its dependency is satisfied rather than because it was told to
requirement satisfied; the blocked process is free to continue
nodes.detail: a further missing requirement is its own dependency with its own instance

nodes.headline: Given how critical the blocked process is, what now?
external:human-in-the-loop-lifecycle
nodes.detail: a critical dependency that requesting did not resolve

nodes.headline: blocked process proceeding by a route that does not need this
nodes.detail: if the alternate route later requires it after all, that is a new dependency

nodes.headline: requirement unmet; the blocked process stays blocked and says so
nodes.detail: the item arriving later re-opens this normally; it is not re-requested repeatedly in the meantime

edges.label: We already have it
edges.when: an authoritative system holds it, or it can be derived or reconciled from what we hold

edges.label: It has to be provided
edges.when: no system holds it and someone has to supply it

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the data arrives

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: how long to wait is a property of what is blocked, not of the request - a blocked payment and a blocked report do not deserve the same patience

edges.label: Valid
edges.when: it satisfies the requirement

edges.label: Invalid or incomplete
edges.when: what arrived does not satisfy the requirement

edges.label: Critical enough for a person
edges.when: the process matters enough that someone should own getting this resolved

edges.label: An alternate route exists
edges.when: the process can proceed by a path that does not require this item

edges.label: Not worth pursuing further
edges.when: the blocked process can wait or be abandoned without harm
a critical dependency that requesting did not resolve

distinctFrom.because: ACT-13 is scoped to activation specifically and owns resuming onboarding. This applies to any named process, most of which have nothing to do with onboarding.

guardrails: Nice-to-have profile data is not a critical requirement, and asking for it as though it were teaches people that our requests are negotiable.
Nothing is requested that an authoritative system already holds.
Every request names the process it unblocks. A request that cannot is progressive profiling and belongs elsewhere.
governance.reusableRule: Critical data should be requested only when a named process cannot safely proceed without it.
governance.entityScope: the business entity that is blocked plus the specific missing requirement
governance.entityNote: One instance per missing requirement per blocked process. Two gaps are two dependencies, resolvable by different people at different times.

identity.title: Relationship signal → evidence accumulation → state reassessment
identity.purpose: Accumulate signals as dated evidence, and let a relationship label exist only where a policy defined what it means.

requires: a signal that says something about the relationship: positive or negative feedback, a successful outcome, a repeated contribution, support friction, a declared preference, an engagement change, an advocacy action
insufficientAlone: an open or a click, which describes a message rather than a relationship

nodes.headline: Meaningful relationship signal

Store the signal with its type, source, time, related entity and how reliable it is. It is stored as evidence, never as a conclusion - the difference is whether anything downstream can disagree with it later
Does this signal need immediate operational action?
recorded as evidence; the action is owned elsewhere
nodes.detail: the journey that owns the action is triggered by the same signal independently - this one records, it does not dispatch, and duplicating the dispatch here is how two systems respond to one event

nodes.headline: Does the accumulated evidence justify reassessing a relationship state?
evidence recorded; state unchanged
nodes.detail: the next signal is weighed against a slightly larger set

nodes.headline: Re-evaluate against the whole current evidence set, applying the decay the state being assessed requires. How fast evidence stops counting depends on what is being judged: satisfaction ages quickly, tenure does not
Is the state being assigned one a policy has actually defined?
Assign the state, recording which policy defines it and which evidence satisfied it, so it can be explained, disputed and removed by the same route it was created by
relationship state reassessed against the current evidence set
nodes.detail: further signals may move it again, in either direction

nodes.headline: evidence recorded; no label created
nodes.detail: a policy defining the label makes it assignable later, against this same evidence - a label nobody defined is one nobody can dispute, remove, or explain to the person carrying it

edges.label: Needs action
edges.when: something has to happen now - a complaint, a failure, a request

edges.label: Evidence only
edges.when: it says something about the relationship without requiring anything to be done

edges.label: Worth reassessing
edges.when: enough has changed across the evidence set that the current state may no longer be right

edges.label: State stands
edges.when: one more signal consistent with what is already recorded

edges.label: Governed
edges.when: a policy defines what this label means, what evidence establishes it, and what removes it

edges.label: Undefined
edges.when: the label would be created here for the first time - LOYAL, ADVOCATE, AT_RISK, VIP, DETRACTOR and everything like them

distinctFrom.because: RET-21 recalculates engagement from behaviour on a defined cadence. This accumulates heterogeneous signals - feedback, outcomes, friction, contributions - and only reassesses a state where the evidence justifies it.

guardrails: One signal does not silently create a permanent label. LOYAL, ADVOCATE, AT_RISK, VIP and DETRACTOR exist only where a policy defines what they mean and what removes them.
Evidence decays, and how fast depends on what is being assessed rather than on a single global rule.
Signals stay scoped to the entity they were observed on.
Communication engagement is not relationship evidence and does not enter this store.
governance.reusableRule: Relationship states should emerge from appropriate evidence over time rather than from isolated behavioral or feedback events.
governance.entityScope: person or account plus the relationship context the signal was observed in
governance.entityNote: Signals are scoped and dated. Without scope one bad experience colours everything; without a date, evidence from years ago outvotes evidence from this week.

identity.title: Financial obligation created → due → satisfied or outstanding
identity.purpose: Hold what is owed as its own state, independent of any attempt to pay it and of anything sent about it.

requires: an authoritative record that an amount is owed, by whom, to whom, and arising from what
insufficientAlone: an invoice being emailed, which is a communication about an obligation rather than the obligation
a reminder being scheduled

nodes.headline: Financial obligation created

Record the obligation id, the amount, the currency, the payer, the payee, the due date where one applies, the source, the related business entity and the settlement requirement. Currency is part of the amount - a monetary value without it cannot be reconciled against anything later
Does an existing payment or credit already satisfy this?
Record OUTSTANDING. This is the normal state of a new obligation and not a failure - nothing has gone wrong and nothing has been paid, and the two are different facts
until an authoritative financial event satisfies or partly satisfies it, or an adjustment or cancellation is recorded against it, or it becomes due or overdue
nodes.detail: timeout after the obligation's own horizon - its limitation period, its write-off point, or the end of the relationship it belongs to

nodes.headline: What happened to the obligation?

Version the obligation and reconcile the financial state. An adjustment does not overwrite the original amount - the obligation's history is what any later dispute or reconciliation reads, and a silently edited balance cannot be explained to anyone
obligation adjusted; prior versions preserved
nodes.detail: the adjusted obligation continues its own lifecycle from its new amount

nodes.headline: Financial obligation satisfied → reconcile balance → release dependent state
nodes.detail: an authoritative financial event applying to this obligation

nodes.headline: Due-state change → recalculate priority → resolve or escalate
nodes.detail: the obligation becoming due or overdue

nodes.headline: outstanding past its horizon
nodes.detail: what happens to an aged obligation is an accounting decision - writing it off is a policy act with its own authority, and this journey does not make it

edges.label: Already covered
edges.when: an existing authoritative financial event discharges it, in whole or in part

edges.label: Nothing against it
edges.when: no financial event has been applied to it

edges.label: on event
edges.when: an authoritative financial event satisfies or partly satisfies it, an adjustment or cancellation is recorded against it, it becomes due or overdue

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: an obligation outstanding indefinitely is a balance nobody is collecting and nobody has decided to stop collecting, and which of those it is should be stated

edges.label: A financial event discharged some or all of it
edges.when: a payment, credit or settlement was applied

edges.label: It was adjusted or cancelled
edges.when: the amount, the terms or the obligation's existence changed authoritatively

edges.label: Its due state moved
edges.when: it became due, or passed its due date unsatisfied
an authoritative financial event applying to this obligation
the obligation becoming due or overdue

distinctFrom.because: An attempt is one try at discharging an obligation. It can fail without the obligation changing at all, which is exactly why they are two entities.

guardrails: An invoice issued is not a payment received.
An outstanding obligation is not a payment failure.
Reminder activity does not define financial truth. What is owed is established by financial events, not by what was sent about it.
governance.reusableRule: A financial obligation remains outstanding until authoritative financial events satisfy, adjust or cancel it.
governance.entityScope: the obligation itself - its amount, its currency, its payer and the business entity it arose from
governance.entityNote: The obligation outlives every payment attempt against it. Attempts come and go; what is owed changes only when an authoritative financial event satisfies, adjusts or cancels it.

identity.title: Payment initiated → pending → success, failure or unknown
identity.purpose: Keep initiating a payment and knowing what happened to it as separate states, with a third state for not knowing.

requires: an authoritative payment system accepting an attempt against a specific obligation
insufficientAlone: a payment button clicked, which is an intent until an authoritative system has accepted the attempt
an HTTP success from a payment form, which describes the form rather than the money

nodes.headline: Payment attempt initiated

Persist the attempt id, the amount, the currency, the payment method reference, the obligation it targets, the provider reference, the idempotency key and the initiation time, and record PAYMENT_PENDING. The idempotency key exists before submission because it is the only thing that makes a later retry or reconciliation safe
until an authoritative success, or an authoritative failure
nodes.detail: timeout after the payment outcome window

nodes.headline: What did the authoritative system establish?
Financial obligation satisfied → reconcile balance → release dependent state
nodes.detail: a payment succeeding against an obligation

nodes.headline: Payment authorization → capture → settle or release
nodes.detail: an authorization that still requires capture

nodes.headline: Payment failure → classify → recover, alternate or exit
nodes.detail: an authoritative payment failure

nodes.headline: Payment unknown → reconcile → confirm success or failure
nodes.detail: a payment whose outcome window closed without an authoritative result

edges.label: on event
edges.when: an authoritative success, an authoritative failure

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the window ending means we stopped hearing, which is a fact about our visibility rather than about the money - and in this category the difference between those two is a duplicate charge

edges.label: Funds committed
edges.when: the payment succeeded outright, with no separate capture or settlement step to follow

edges.label: Authorized, capture still required
edges.when: funds are reserved and the movement has not been requested

edges.label: Authoritative failure
edges.when: the payment system states that nothing moved and why
a payment succeeding against an obligation
an authorization that still requires capture
an authoritative payment failure
a payment whose outcome window closed without an authoritative result

distinctFrom.because: INT-114 is the generic shape of an external operation. This carries financial semantics the generic version has no room for: an obligation behind it, an authorization that is not money, and an unknown state whose safe response is to investigate rather than retry.

guardrails: A payment button click is not a payment initiated unless an authoritative system accepted the attempt.
An HTTP success is not a payment success.
A timeout is not a failed payment.
An unknown outcome is never blindly retried.
governance.reusableRule: A payment attempt remains pending until an authoritative outcome establishes success, failure or an explicitly unresolved state.
governance.entityScope: the individual payment attempt, keyed by its own idempotency key and provider reference
governance.entityNote: One attempt, one key, recorded before submission. Without it a later reconciliation cannot ask the provider about anything in particular.

identity.title: Payment authorization → capture → settle or release
identity.purpose: Model the actual commitment of funds, where reserving, taking and receiving are three different things.

requires: an authorization confirmed by the payment system, with its own validity window

nodes.headline: Payment authorization succeeded
Record AUTHORIZED. Authorized means funds are reserved, not moved - granting an irreversible outcome here grants it against money that has not been taken and may never be
Is a separate capture required?
until capture is executed, or the authorization is cancelled
nodes.detail: timeout after the authorization's validity window

nodes.headline: What happened to the authorization?
Record RELEASED - the reservation returned and no funds moved. The obligation behind it is untouched and still outstanding
RELEASED; reservation returned, obligation unchanged
nodes.detail: a further attempt against the same obligation is a new attempt with its own key

nodes.headline: Record EXPIRED - the authorization lapsed before capture and the reservation is gone. Nothing was taken, and the obligation stands exactly as it did
EXPIRED; authorization lapsed uncaptured
nodes.detail: a new authorization is required; this one cannot be captured after expiry

nodes.headline: Record CAPTURED. Captured means the movement was requested and accepted, which is still not the same as the funds having arrived on the other side
Is settlement tracked separately in this system?
Record SETTLEMENT_PENDING. Captured and settled are different, and an outcome that depends on funds having actually arrived waits for the second
until settlement completes, or settlement fails
nodes.detail: timeout after the settlement window

nodes.headline: Did settlement complete?
Financial obligation satisfied → reconcile balance → release dependent state
nodes.detail: funds having completed the movement this system treats as authoritative

nodes.headline: Financial reconciliation → detect mismatch → correct or escalate
nodes.detail: a settlement that failed or never arrived

edges.label: Capture required
edges.when: the authorization reserves funds and a separate act moves them

edges.label: Captured at authorization
edges.when: the payment model takes the funds as it authorises them

edges.label: on event
edges.when: capture is executed, the authorization is cancelled

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: an authorization that expires uncaptured releases the reservation on its own, and the customer's available balance returns without anyone deciding it should

edges.label: Captured
edges.when: the movement was requested and accepted

edges.label: Cancelled
edges.when: the authorization was released deliberately

edges.label: Tracked separately
edges.when: capture and settlement are distinct events with distinct timing

edges.label: Capture is authoritative
edges.when: this payment model treats capture as the completed movement

edges.label: on event
edges.when: settlement completes, settlement fails

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a settlement that never arrived is a mismatch between our state and the provider's, which is a reconciliation problem rather than a payment one

edges.label: Settled
edges.when: the funds completed their movement

edges.label: Settlement failed
edges.when: the movement did not complete
funds having completed the movement this system treats as authoritative
a settlement that failed or never arrived

guardrails: Authorized is not money captured.
Captured is not necessarily settled.
An irreversible outcome that depends on funds is not granted from an authorization where the business requires capture or settlement.
governance.reusableRule: Financial transaction states should reflect the actual movement commitment of funds rather than collapse authorization, capture and settlement into a generic success.
governance.entityScope: the payment transaction across its authorization, capture and settlement states
governance.entityNote: Each state is a different commitment. An outcome that depends on money having moved is not granted against an authorization, which is money that has only been promised.

identity.title: Payment failure → classify → recover, alternate or exit
identity.purpose: Respond to the reason a payment actually failed, and keep the obligation alive while doing it.

requires: a payment system stating that the attempt failed, with whatever reason it gave
insufficientAlone: a timeout, which establishes nothing about whether money moved

nodes.headline: Authoritative payment failure

Classify the failure into the class the provider actually reported: temporary, insufficient funds, invalid method, expired method, authentication required, provider failure, policy decline, or unknown reason. A decline reason is never invented - telling someone their card had insufficient funds when the provider said only 'do not honour' is a checkable falsehood that sends them to fix the wrong thing
What kind of failure was it?
Retry within the bounded policy, using the same idempotency key so that a first attempt which did land can be absorbed rather than repeated

Request the exact corrective action - update the method, complete the authentication, choose another method. Naming what to fix is the whole value of the classification, and a generic notice that payment failed makes the person guess. Provider risk detail and internal decline codes are not exposed
Is an alternative valid payment route available and permitted?
Offer or use the alternative route according to the customer and business rules, as a new attempt with its own identifiers
until the obligation is satisfied, or the customer abandons the attempt
nodes.detail: timeout after the recovery window for this obligation

nodes.headline: How did recovery end?
obligation satisfied through recovery
nodes.detail: a future failure against a future obligation is its own instance

nodes.headline: The obligation is unpaid after the recovery window - what does policy apply?
Grace period entry → temporary continuity → recover or terminate
nodes.detail: an unpaid obligation entering a grace period

nodes.headline: Due-state change → recalculate priority → resolve or escalate
nodes.detail: an unpaid obligation becoming overdue

nodes.headline: Access suspension → restricted state → restore or terminate
nodes.detail: policy restricting capability while an obligation is unpaid

edges.label: Transient, safe to retry
edges.when: a temporary condition or a provider-side failure, with the same idempotency key still valid

edges.label: The customer can fix it
edges.when: insufficient funds, an invalid or expired method, or an authentication that was not completed

edges.label: Declined, or no usable reason given
edges.when: a policy decline, or a decline whose reason cannot be turned into an instruction

edges.label: Alternative available
edges.when: another method or route exists and the customer and business rules allow it

edges.label: Nothing further to offer
edges.when: no alternative route is available or permitted

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the obligation is satisfied, the customer abandons the attempt

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the window bounds how long recovery runs before the obligation's own consequences apply - it does not end the obligation, which continues regardless

edges.label: Satisfied
edges.when: a subsequent attempt discharged the obligation

edges.label: Abandoned
edges.when: the customer stopped trying

edges.label: Grace period
edges.when: policy continues limited service while the obligation remains unresolved

edges.label: Overdue tracking
edges.when: the obligation moves to an overdue operational state without immediate consequence

edges.label: Access restriction
edges.when: policy restricts capability while the obligation is unpaid
an unpaid obligation entering a grace period
an unpaid obligation becoming overdue
policy restricting capability while an obligation is unpaid

distinctFrom.because: OPS-124 is a generic technical retry against a transient fault. This makes a business recovery decision: what to ask the customer for, whether an alternative route exists, and what happens to the obligation if none of it works.

guardrails: A payment failure is not a subscription cancellation.
A decline reason is never invented. What the provider said is what the customer is told, or nothing specific is claimed.
Retries are bounded.
Sensitive provider and internal risk detail is not exposed.
governance.reusableRule: Payment recovery should respond to the actual failure class while preserving the underlying financial obligation until it is resolved.
governance.entityScope: the failed attempt, the obligation behind it and the customer relationship it belongs to
governance.entityNote: Three things, and the failure touches only the first. The obligation stands and the relationship continues while recovery runs.

identity.title: Payment unknown → reconcile → confirm success or failure
identity.purpose: Find out what actually happened to a payment whose outcome we lost sight of, before anything is charged again.

requires: a payment attempt whose outcome could not be authoritatively established - a timeout, an interrupted connection, an incomplete callback

nodes.headline: Payment outcome undeterminable

Preserve the provider reference, the idempotency key, the amount, the target obligation and the last known state, and record PAYMENT_UNKNOWN. Unknown is not failed, and nothing downstream may treat it as such

Suppress any automatic replacement payment. While the original may still have succeeded, initiating another is the single action that converts uncertainty into a duplicate charge - and the customer finds it before we do
Query the authoritative financial source for the operation's true state, using the provider reference and the idempotency key
until the provider confirms the payment succeeded, or the provider confirms the payment failed, or the customer initiates another payment attempt
nodes.detail: timeout after the reconciliation round window

nodes.headline: What was established?

Record PAYMENT_SUCCEEDED and apply it exactly once, reconciled against the obligation's current balance. A late success is applied against what the obligation is now rather than what it was when the attempt started - the balance moved while this was in flight
Financial obligation satisfied → reconcile balance → release dependent state
nodes.detail: a late-confirmed payment success

nodes.headline: Payment failure → classify → recover, alternate or exit
nodes.detail: a reconciliation establishing that the payment failed

nodes.headline: Duplicate work detected → deduplicate → reuse, suppress or reconcile
nodes.detail: a second attempt arriving while the first is unresolved

nodes.headline: Is another reconciliation round available within the bounded policy?
external:finance-ownership
nodes.detail: a payment that remains unknown after bounded reconciliation

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the provider confirms the payment succeeded, the provider confirms the payment failed, the customer initiates another payment attempt

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: each round is bounded so an unresolved payment escalates to someone rather than being retried into by a process that has lost patience

edges.label: It succeeded
edges.when: the provider confirms the funds moved

edges.label: It failed
edges.when: the provider confirms nothing moved

edges.label: The customer tried again
edges.when: another attempt arrived while this one was unresolved
a late-confirmed payment success
a reconciliation establishing that the payment failed
a second attempt arriving while the first is unresolved

edges.label: Round available
edges.when: the policy allows another query and the provider may yet answer

edges.label: Rounds exhausted
edges.when: the attempt remains unresolved after the policy's rounds
a payment that remains unknown after bounded reconciliation

guardrails: Unknown is not failed.
No replacement payment is initiated automatically while the original may still have succeeded.
A customer retry during an unknown state is correlated and deduplicated rather than charged.
A late success is reconciled against the obligation's current balance.
governance.reusableRule: Unknown payment outcomes require reconciliation before replacement attempts because uncertainty itself creates duplicate financial risk.
governance.entityScope: the single payment attempt whose outcome could not be established
governance.entityNote: One attempt. This is not a mismatch between records - it is one operation whose result we do not know, and the answer exists at the provider.

identity.title: Financial obligation satisfied → reconcile balance → release dependent state
identity.purpose: Apply a financial event to an obligation exactly once, and release only what actually depended on that obligation.

requires: an authoritative payment, credit or settlement that discharges some or all of an obligation

nodes.headline: Authoritative financial event against obligation

Apply the amount idempotently against the obligation, keyed so the same financial event arriving twice moves the balance once. Currency compatibility is checked before anything is netted - amounts in different currencies are not offset against each other
Recalculate the remaining balance, the obligation's status, any overpayment, and which dependent restrictions or holds rested on this obligation specifically
What does the recalculated balance show?
Record PARTIALLY_SATISFIED with the remaining balance stated explicitly. Partial is not paid, and a remainder that is implied rather than carried is one nobody can collect and nobody can dispute
PARTIALLY_SATISFIED; the remaining balance is explicit and still outstanding
nodes.detail: further financial events apply against the remaining balance. Restrictions that depended on this obligation stay in force, because it is not discharged

nodes.headline: external:overpayment-or-credit
nodes.detail: an amount applied exceeding what was owed

nodes.headline: Record SATISFIED against the obligation
Does an existing restriction depend solely on this obligation?
Capability restoration → revalidate → restore safely
nodes.detail: an obligation whose payment removes the reason a capability was restricted

nodes.headline: SATISFIED; nothing else depended on it
nodes.detail: a later adjustment or reversal against this obligation is its own financial event, applied to a discharged balance rather than an outstanding one

edges.label: Fully satisfied
edges.when: the balance reaches zero

edges.label: Partially satisfied
edges.when: an amount remains outstanding

edges.label: Overpaid
edges.when: the amount applied exceeds what was owed
an amount applied exceeding what was owed

edges.label: Restriction rested on this
edges.when: a capability was restricted specifically because this obligation was unpaid

edges.label: No restriction depended on it
edges.when: nothing was withheld on account of this obligation
an obligation whose payment removes the reason a capability was restricted

guardrails: A payment success is never applied twice.
Financial satisfaction does not automatically restore unrelated suspended capabilities.
Partial payment is not full payment, and the remainder is carried explicitly.
Amounts are not netted across incompatible currencies.
governance.reusableRule: Successful financial events should update the obligation balance exactly once and release only the states that actually depended on that obligation.
governance.entityScope: the obligation and the financial event being applied to it
governance.entityNote: Applying is idempotent by key. The same event arriving twice moves the balance once, which is the difference between a balance and a running total of deliveries.

identity.title: Refund request → eligibility → approve, reject or review
identity.purpose: Turn a refund request into an authorised decision, without money moving on the request itself.

requires: a refund requested against an identified original transaction
insufficientAlone: dissatisfaction expressed about a purchase, which is feedback until it is made as a request

nodes.headline: Refund requested
Record the request id, the original transaction, the requested amount, the reason, the requester and the submission time. The original payment history is not modified by a request made against it
Is the request valid and within the process scope?
Reject with the actual reason and whatever process does apply. A rejection that does not say why produces the next request rather than closing this one
Is a refund eligibility policy defined for this transaction type?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a refund request with no governing eligibility policy

nodes.headline: What does the policy determine?
Record REJECTED with the reason drawn from the policy that ruled it out
REJECTED; no money moves and the original transaction stands
nodes.detail: a differently grounded request, or new evidence, is assessed on its own. A refund requested is not a refund owed

nodes.headline: Record UNDER_REVIEW and gather whatever the decision requires. Nothing moves while it is under review
until a decision is recorded
nodes.detail: timeout after the decision SLA

nodes.headline: What was decided?
Responsibility escalation → higher authority → resolution or return
nodes.detail: a refund decision outliving its SLA

nodes.headline: Record APPROVED with the authorised amount and the authority that approved it. Approved authorises the movement and performs none of it
Refund approved → execute → confirm or reconcile

edges.when: it identifies a real transaction, from someone entitled to ask, within any applicable window

edges.label: Out of scope
edges.when: it names no valid transaction, comes from someone with no standing, or falls outside the process entirely

edges.label: Defined
edges.when: policy states what qualifies for a refund and on what terms

edges.label: Not defined
edges.when: no policy covers this kind of refund
a refund request with no governing eligibility policy

edges.label: Eligible
edges.when: the policy's conditions are met deterministically

edges.label: Ineligible

edges.label: Requires judgement
edges.when: the policy leaves this case to a decision rather than a rule

edges.label: on event
edges.when: a decision is recorded

edges.when: the reviewer authorised the refund

edges.label: Rejected
edges.when: the reviewer declined it
a refund decision outliving its SLA
a refund authorised for execution

guardrails: A refund requested is not a refund owed.
A refund request does not modify the original payment history.
Eligibility policy is never invented. Where none exists the decision goes to a person.

nodes.headline: Refund authorized for execution

Submit the refund under a stable operation identity and record REFUND_PENDING. The stable identity is what stops a retry or a redelivered response producing a second refund - and a duplicate refund is money that has to be asked for back
until the refund completes, or the refund fails

nodes.headline: Financial dispute opened

Record the dispute id, the transaction, the amount, the reason category, when it opened, the response deadline and the external authority handling it. A dispute being opened is not fraud confirmed and not a loss - it is a claim with a deadline, and most of them are confusion, a forgotten subscription or an unrecognised descriptor
Collect the evidence this dispute category actually requires, which the authority defines rather than we do

Submit before the deadline. A deadline missed is usually decided against us regardless of what the evidence would have shown, which makes the date more important than the argument

nodes.headline: What did the authority decide?

Reconcile the financial balance and the related obligation according to the outcome - won leaves the original transaction standing, lost reverses the funds and reopens what they had discharged, partial does both in proportion, withdrawn leaves everything as it was. In every case the dispute's own history is preserved: the final outcome does not overwrite the record of what was claimed, what was submitted and when

identity.title: Financial reconciliation → detect mismatch → correct or escalate
identity.purpose: Restore financial consistency by explaining the difference and adjusting it, never by editing the record that is inconvenient.

nodes.headline: Material financial mismatch detected
Collect the authoritative records from every relevant system rather than reasoning from the one that raised the alarm

Compare transaction identifiers, amounts, currency, statuses, timestamps, obligation allocations, refunds and credits, and settlement state. Amounts in different currencies are not compared or netted - a mismatch across currencies is a context error rather than a discrepancy, and resolving it as one produces a balance that is confidently wrong
What can be established from the records?
until the provider confirms the authoritative state

nodes.headline: Does an accounting policy cover this correction?

Apply the correction idempotently as an explicit adjustment, preserving the adjustment history. A mismatch is never fixed by deleting the inconvenient transaction - the correction is a new record that explains the difference, and the original stays so the explanation has something to refer to
Verify the final financial state balances according to the defined accounting and business invariants
Does the corrected state balance?
reconciled through an explicit, auditable adjustment
nodes.detail: a further mismatch on the same records is its own reconciliation, with this adjustment in the history

Determine the original commitment, the current estimate, the cause, the affected scope and the impact, and record DELAYED. Delayed is a change to timing and not a failure - the obligation is still owed and nothing downstream may treat it as gone

Update the expected timing, appending to the commitment history. The original commitment is preserved - what was promised and what it became are two facts, and keeping both is the only way a repeated slip becomes visible

Record that no reliable estimate exists rather than issuing one. Repeatedly promising dates that do not hold costs more trust than admitting the date is unknown, and each broken date makes the next one worth less

Does the counterparty have a decision to make?

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the window closing means we stopped hearing, which is a fact about our visibility rather than about the parcel - and a provider timeout is not a delivery failure

edges.label: Delivered
edges.when: the executor authoritatively confirms the recipient has it

edges.label: Attempt failed
edges.when: the executor confirms an attempt was made and delivery did not happen

edges.label: Delayed
edges.when: the executor reports the delivery will be later than the window
a delivery whose outcome could not be established
an authoritative delivery confirmation
a confirmed failed delivery attempt
the executor reporting the delivery will be later

distinctFrom.because: INT-114 is the generic shape of an external operation. This carries delivery semantics that shape has no room for: a recipient who may refuse, an attempt that is not an outcome, and intermediate tracking updates that look like results and are not.

guardrails: Dispatched is not delivered.
A tracking update is not necessarily a final delivery.
A provider timeout is not a delivery failure.
Duplicate delivery events are idempotent.
governance.reusableRule: Handoff transfers execution to a delivery mechanism but the fulfillment remains unresolved until an authoritative delivery outcome exists.
governance.entityScope: the handoff to a delivery executor, and the obligation behind it
governance.entityNote: Handing something to a carrier transfers who is doing the work. It transfers nothing about who owes the outcome.

identity.title: Delivery attempt failed → reason → retry, correct, alternate or return
identity.purpose: Recover a failed delivery according to why it failed, within a bounded number of attempts.

requires: a delivery executor confirming an attempt was made and delivery did not occur
insufficientAlone: a tracking status that has not advanced, which is silence rather than a failure

nodes.headline: Authoritative delivery attempt failure

Classify the failure into the class the executor actually reported. Refused and unavailable are different outcomes - one is a decision by the recipient and the other is an absence, and treating the first as the second keeps redelivering to someone who has already said no
What kind of failure was it?

Request the exact correction - the address, the access instruction, the contact. Naming what is missing is what makes it fixable, and a generic notice that delivery failed sends the recipient to guess
until the correction is provided
nodes.detail: timeout after the correction window

nodes.headline: Is a reattempt available within the bounded policy?
Would an alternative route serve better than another attempt at the same one?
Use the alternative route according to policy or the recipient's choice, recorded as a change of route rather than a new obligation
Schedule the bounded reattempt, against the remaining attempt budget rather than a fresh one
Dispatch or handoff → track → delivered, failed or unknown
nodes.detail: a further delivery attempt being dispatched

nodes.headline: Post-completion issue → validate → remedy route
nodes.detail: a delivery that cannot be completed - refused, uncorrectable, or out of attempts

nodes.headline: Fulfillment exception → diagnose → recover, substitute or fail
nodes.detail: an item that arrived damaged

edges.label: Correctable information needed
edges.when: the destination is wrong, or access to it is blocked in a way information would resolve

edges.label: A reattempt is safe
edges.when: the recipient was unavailable, the time window was missed, or the executor itself failed

edges.label: The recipient refused it
edges.when: someone with authority to refuse did so

edges.label: Damaged
edges.when: what arrived is not what should have been delivered

edges.label: A reattempt is safe
edges.when: the recipient was unavailable, the time window was missed, or the executor itself failed

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the correction is provided

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: an item held indefinitely awaiting information nobody is providing is one that has to go somewhere, and returning it is the honest ending

edges.label: Attempts remain
edges.when: the policy's attempt limit has not been reached

edges.label: Exhausted
edges.when: the attempt limit is reached

edges.label: An alternative is better
edges.when: a collection point, a different window or another executor is more likely to succeed, and policy or the recipient's choice permits it

edges.label: Reattempt the same route
edges.when: the original route remains the best option
a further delivery attempt being dispatched
a delivery that cannot be completed - refused, uncorrectable, or out of attempts
an item that arrived damaged

guardrails: Attempted is not delivered.
Delivery is not retried indefinitely - the budget is bounded and does not reset.
Refused and unavailable are different outcomes with different consequences.
The failure reason is never invented. What the executor reported is what is acted on.
governance.reusableRule: Failed delivery attempts should recover according to the reason delivery failed while preserving the original fulfillment obligation until its terminal outcome is known.
governance.entityScope: the individual delivery attempt and the obligation it was serving
governance.entityNote: The obligation survives every failed attempt. What changes is how many attempts remain and what would make the next one work.

identity.title: Delivery confirmation → acceptance or issue window → finalize
identity.purpose: Separate arriving from being agreed to have arrived correctly, wherever that difference has business meaning.

requires: an authoritative confirmation that the recipient has what was owed

nodes.headline: Authoritative delivery completion
Record DELIVERED with the proof of delivery, which stays attached to the delivery history rather than being superseded by whatever finalisation follows
Does this fulfillment require explicit acceptance?
until the recipient accepts, or the recipient raises an issue
nodes.detail: timeout after the acceptance deadline defined by the contract or policy

nodes.headline: What did the recipient do?
Does policy define a post-delivery issue window?
until an issue is raised
nodes.detail: timeout after the issue window closing

nodes.headline: Post-completion issue → validate → remedy route
nodes.detail: an issue raised within a valid post-delivery window

nodes.headline: Record FINALIZED. This closes the fulfillment relationship and does not erase rights that policy independently provides afterwards - a warranty, a statutory return period or a service guarantee all survive finalisation and are not what this state was measuring
FINALIZED; the obligation is discharged and the remaining scope is zero
nodes.detail: later rights that policy provides independently are exercised on their own terms and do not reopen this state

edges.label: Acceptance required
edges.when: the contract or the nature of the work means the recipient has to agree it is correct

edges.label: No acceptance required
edges.when: delivery itself discharges the obligation

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the recipient accepts, the recipient raises an issue

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: deemed acceptance after a stated period is a policy position; inventing one where none exists closes an obligation the counterparty never agreed was finished

edges.label: Accepted
edges.when: they confirmed it is correct

edges.label: Raised an issue
edges.when: they say something is wrong with it

edges.label: A window exists
edges.when: policy gives the recipient a defined period to raise a problem

edges.label: No window defined
edges.when: policy defines completion at delivery

edges.label: on event
edges.when: an issue is raised

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the window ending without an issue is the ordinary path to completion, and no acceptance window is invented beyond what policy defines
an issue raised within a valid post-delivery window

guardrails: Delivered is not accepted where acceptance is contractually meaningful.
No acceptance window is invented beyond what policy defines.
Proof of delivery remains attached to the delivery history.
Finalisation does not erase later rights that policy independently provides.
governance.reusableRule: Delivery establishes receipt; final fulfillment completion may additionally depend on acceptance or a defined post-delivery resolution window.
governance.entityScope: the delivered fulfillment and the recipient whose acceptance may still be required
governance.entityNote: Proof of delivery stays attached to the delivery record. Finalisation is a later state and does not supersede the evidence that produced it.

identity.title: Fulfillment cancellation → stop future work → release resources → reconcile
identity.purpose: Stop what remains of an obligation while keeping everything that already happened.

requires: an authoritative cancellation that has taken effect on the obligation
insufficientAlone: a cancellation requested, which is an intent until it becomes effective

nodes.headline: Fulfillment cancellation effective

Record the cancellation source, the reason, the effective time, and the three scopes separately - what is completed, what is in progress and what has not started. They are treated differently throughout, and collapsing them either discards delivered work or cancels nothing at all
Stop the future work that can still be stopped, scoped to the unstarted portion and whatever in-progress work can be halted safely

Release the allocations and reservations this obligation no longer needs, scoped strictly to its own. A release that reaches a shared allocation or another obligation's claim takes capacity from work that is still going ahead
Has any scope already been completed?

Preserve the completed scope. Cancellation stops what remains; it does not pretend what was delivered never happened, and a record that erases it cannot be reconciled against what the recipient actually has
Has any of it already been handed to a delivery executor?
