edges.label: It does not
edges.when: nothing held covers it, or what is held has lapsed or was scoped to something else

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the requirement is authoritatively satisfied, the requirement authoritatively fails

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a dependent process blocked on a requirement nobody is completing is stopped without anyone having decided to stop it

edges.label: Satisfied
edges.when: the required evidence was obtained and verified

edges.label: Failed
edges.when: the requirement cannot be met with what is available

edges.label: It defines an outcome
edges.when: policy states what happens to the dependent process when the deadline passes

edges.label: It does not
edges.when: no rule states what an expired compliance deadline does
a compliance requirement satisfied, releasing the process that depended on it

edges.label: Block it
edges.when: the rules stop the dependent process while the requirement is unmet

edges.label: Close it
edges.when: the rules end the dependent process where the requirement cannot be met

edges.label: The rules do not say
edges.when: nothing authoritative states the consequence for the dependent process
a compliance requirement whose failure or deadline consequence the rules do not define

distinctFrom.because: IDN-82 orchestrates collecting a verification and resuming what it blocked. This owns the compliance requirement as a business state - which requirement applies, whether existing evidence already satisfies it, and what happens when it cannot be met. It uses that collection mechanism rather than reimplementing one.

guardrails: A compliance requirement never requests unrelated evidence.
A satisfied requirement is scoped to its defined purpose and validity.
A compliance requirement is not generic customer onboarding.
Only the processes depending on the requirement are blocked.
governance.reusableRule: Compliance requirements should block only the processes that depend on them and release those processes only when the defined requirement is authoritatively satisfied.
governance.entityScope: the compliance requirement and the specific process depending on it
governance.entityNote: Satisfied is scoped to the requirement's purpose and validity. The same evidence does not satisfy a different requirement.

identity.title: Compliance or policy hold → preserve state → resolve → resume or terminate
identity.purpose: Pause what a policy question makes unsafe, and leave everything else running.

requires: an authoritative policy or compliance hold, with an authority behind it

nodes.headline: Policy or compliance hold applied

Record the hold reason, its scope, the authority for it, the effective time, which operations it affects, which remain allowed, and what would resolve it. A hold with no stated resolution condition has no way out and becomes a termination nobody decided

Record ON_HOLD and pause only the future actions the hold is incompatible with. Unrelated capabilities stay available where policy permits - a hold on outbound payments is not a reason to stop someone reading their own records
Do existing commitments require continued handling?

Preserve those commitments and route them according to the governing rules. An order already placed, a refund already due and a regulatory report already owed do not stop existing because the entity is on hold - and some of them the hold specifically requires us to keep doing
Leave existing deadlines where they are unless the governing policy explicitly moves them. A hold that silently resets clocks extends obligations nobody agreed to extend, and it shortens none of them
until the stated resolution requirement is met, or a review decision changes the hold, or a terminal policy outcome is reached
nodes.detail: timeout after the maximum hold duration policy defines

nodes.headline: How did the hold resolve?

Re-read the entity's current state before resuming. What resumes is what is valid now - the hold may have outlasted an entitlement, a term or an eligibility, and lifting it does not restore things that expired underneath it
Record the hold lifted and resume the operations that are currently valid, rebuilt from current state rather than from what was paused
hold lifted; operations resumed at what is currently valid
nodes.detail: a further policy question is a new hold with its own scope and its own resolution condition. This one stays in the record as something that was applied and answered

nodes.headline: Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a hold whose resolution or continuation needs authorized judgment

nodes.headline: external:termination-lifecycle
nodes.detail: a hold resolving into a terminal policy outcome

edges.label: They do
edges.when: orders, refunds, reports or obligations created before the hold are still live

edges.label: None outstanding
edges.when: nothing created before the hold is still owed in either direction

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the stated resolution requirement is met, a review decision changes the hold, a terminal policy outcome is reached

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: an indefinite hold is a termination without a decision, and the entity under it cannot tell which one it is in

edges.label: The requirement was met
edges.when: the stated resolution condition is authoritatively satisfied

edges.label: A terminal policy outcome
edges.when: the policy question resolved against the entity in a way that ends something

edges.label: A review decision is needed
edges.when: resolving it turns on judgment rather than on the stated condition
a hold whose resolution or continuation needs authorized judgment
a hold resolving into a terminal policy outcome

distinctFrom.because: RSK-193 restricts because evidence of risk warrants it, and releases on evidence. A hold pauses because a policy or compliance question is open, and releases when that question is answered - the trigger, the authority and the release condition are all different.

guardrails: A hold is not a rejection.
A hold never resets deadlines unless governing policy explicitly does so.
Unrelated capabilities remain available where permitted.
Every hold states the condition that would resolve it.
governance.reusableRule: A policy or compliance hold temporarily prevents defined actions while preserving the underlying entity and its unresolved obligations.
governance.entityScope: the entity or process on hold, and the hold acting on it
governance.entityNote: The hold pauses future incompatible actions. The entity, its obligations and its deadlines all continue existing underneath it.

identity.title: Exception request → validate authority → approve, reject or review
identity.purpose: Ask for a controlled deviation from a named rule, over a stated scope, from someone entitled to ask.

requires: a request to deviate from an identified policy or rule, for an identified scope
insufficientAlone: a policy block having occurred, which is a rule applying rather than a request to set it aside

nodes.headline: Policy exception requested
Capture the policy or rule concerned, the exception requested, its scope, the reason, the requester, any proposed duration or effective window, and the supporting evidence
Does the policy permit exceptions to this rule?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: an exception sought against a rule whose policy says nothing about exceptions

nodes.headline: Record that this rule admits no exceptions, and close the path. A rule that can be excepted by asking is not a rule, and some of them exist precisely because they cannot be set aside by the person they inconvenience
no exception path exists for this rule; the rule stands
nodes.detail: the policy itself changing is a policy change rather than an exception, and it runs through its own lifecycle with its own effective-time semantics

nodes.headline: May this requester ask for an exception to this rule?
Record the request as invalid on standing, naming who may ask. This is not a refusal of the exception on its merits - nobody assessed it - and reporting it as one is untrue
request invalid on standing; the exception itself was not assessed
nodes.detail: the same exception sought by someone the policy admits is assessed on its merits

nodes.headline: Does a deterministic exception rule cover this case?

Record PENDING_REVIEW. The exception needs an authorized judgment and this journey does not make it - it establishes what is being asked for, over what scope, and hands the decision to the mechanism that owns decisions
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: an exception requiring authorized judgment

nodes.headline: Evaluate the request against the deterministic exception rule that covers it
What did the exception rule determine?
Record the exception REJECTED, naming the condition that was not met. The underlying policy continues to apply exactly as it did
exception rejected; the policy applies unchanged
nodes.detail: the unmet condition being satisfied makes a fresh request assessable. This rejection concerns the request rather than the requester

nodes.headline: Record the exception APPROVED with exactly which rule it displaces, over what scope, for how long and under what conditions. An exception that names no rule and no scope is a general permission, which is what nobody meant to grant and what will be discovered being used somewhere else
Exception granted → apply scoped override → expire or revoke
nodes.detail: an authorized exception ready to be applied

edges.label: It permits them
edges.when: the policy defines an exception path for this rule

edges.label: It forbids them
edges.when: the policy explicitly admits no exceptions to this rule

edges.label: It is silent
edges.when: nothing states whether this rule can be excepted or by whom
an exception sought against a rule whose policy says nothing about exceptions

edges.label: They may
edges.when: the policy's exception path admits requests from this party

edges.label: They may not
edges.when: the requester is not among those the exception path admits

edges.label: It does
edges.when: the policy defines when this exception is granted without judgment

edges.label: It does not
edges.when: granting it turns on an authorized judgment
an exception requiring authorized judgment

edges.label: Granted
edges.when: the rule's conditions for granting are met

edges.label: Refused
edges.when: the rule's conditions are not met
an authorized exception ready to be applied

distinctFrom.because: This defines what a policy exception is and whether one may even be sought - which rule, what scope, whose authority. Where the answer needs judgment it uses the decision engine rather than being one.

guardrails: An exception requested is not an exception granted.
Exception authority is never invented.
An exception identifies exactly which rule and which scope it affects.
An exception is a controlled deviation rather than removal of the rule.
governance.reusableRule: A policy exception is a controlled authorization to deviate from a defined rule within an explicit scope; it is not removal of the rule itself.
governance.entityScope: the exception request and the specific policy, action or entity it concerns
governance.entityNote: An exception names a rule and a scope. One that names neither is a general permission, which is what nobody meant to grant.

identity.title: Exception granted → apply scoped override → expire or revoke
identity.purpose: Let an authorized deviation apply exactly where it was authorized, and stop applying the moment it should.

requires: an authorized exception naming a rule, a scope and its usage semantics

nodes.headline: Exception becomes authorized
Record the exception id, the policy or rule it displaces, its scope, who authorized it, its valid-from, its valid-until where one applies, its conditions and its usage semantics
Does the exception define an expiry?
Record the boundary as granted, so the exception's own terms decide when it stops rather than any assumption made here

Record that no expiry was set, rather than assigning one. Inventing an expiry revokes an authorization nobody revoked; the absence is itself worth surfacing, because an unbounded exception to a live rule is usually something someone should look at again
until the exception is invoked for an action, or the exception is revoked
nodes.detail: timeout after the exception's valid-until, or the review point set for an unbounded exception

nodes.headline: What happened to the exception?
Is the exception currently valid for this specific action?

Apply normal policy and record the attempt. An exception granted for one action or one entity does not travel to another - leakage here is how a single approved deviation becomes a general practice nobody authorized and nobody can date
Refuse the reuse and record the attempt. A single-use exception used twice authorizes one deviation and performs two

Apply the override for this action only, and record the use. The underlying policy is untouched - an exception overrides a decision rather than disabling a rule, and the next action it does not cover gets the normal answer
Is this a single-use exception?
Mark the exception consumed. Its authority is spent, and any later invocation is refused rather than quietly honoured
consumed; the exception can authorize nothing further
nodes.detail: a further deviation needs a further exception, which is a new request rather than a re-reading of this grant

nodes.headline: Record the exception EXPIRED and stop all future override, including in work already queued carrying its id. Stale work holding an expired exception is the failure this state exists to prevent - the override arrives long after the authority lapsed and looks identical to a valid one
EXPIRED; the rule applies normally again and the overrides already made stand
nodes.detail: a renewed exception is a new grant with its own scope and validity, assessed on current circumstances rather than extended from this one

nodes.headline: Record the exception REVOKED with its authority and its effective moment, and stop future override immediately. Revocation does not undo the overrides already validly applied - those happened under an authorization that existed at the time, and rewriting them removes the record of a decision that was correct when it was made
REVOKED; future override stopped, prior valid uses preserved
nodes.detail: whether the prior uses need correcting is a separate question with its own lifecycle, and revoking the exception does not answer it

edges.label: It defines one
edges.when: a valid-until, a period or a use limit was set when it was granted

edges.label: It does not
edges.when: no time limit was set

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the exception is invoked for an action, the exception is revoked

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: an exception that outlives its authority is a rule quietly disabled, and the disabling is invisible because every use looks like a valid one

edges.label: Invoked
edges.when: an action reached a policy decision point carrying this exception

edges.label: Revoked
edges.when: an authority withdrew it before it expired

edges.label: Valid
edges.when: the same rule, inside the granted scope, inside its validity, and not consumed

edges.label: Out of scope
edges.when: a different rule, a different entity or an action the grant did not name

edges.label: Already consumed
edges.when: a single-use exception that has been used

edges.label: Single-use
edges.when: the grant authorized one deviation

edges.label: Reusable within its validity
edges.when: the grant authorized deviations for a period or a scope rather than a count

distinctFrom.because: RSK-197 establishes that a deviation is authorized. This is the runtime question - is it valid for this action, this entity, right now, and has it already been used up. An exception granted correctly and applied wrongly is still an unauthorized deviation.

guardrails: An exception is not a policy disabled.
An exception for one action or entity never leaks to another.
An expired or revoked exception is never reused by stale work.
An expiration is never invented where none exists.
governance.reusableRule: Granted exceptions override only the policy decision explicitly authorized for their defined scope and validity.
governance.entityScope: the granted exception and each action it is invoked against
governance.entityNote: The exception is one record; each use is an event on it. Validity is asked at each use rather than set once when it was granted.

identity.title: Limit or quota reached → block, wait, increase or reset
identity.purpose: Treat a limit being reached as the limit working, and give the constrained action a real path forward.

entry.trigger: Limit threshold reached or would be exceeded
requires: a proposed action measured against a defined limit or quota

nodes.headline: Limit threshold reached or would be exceeded
Determine the limit type, the current usage, the limit amount, the measurement window, the reset semantics, the scope, and the authoritative source of the count
Is the usage figure authoritative?
external:external-status-reconciliation
nodes.detail: a limit decision resting on a usage figure that may be wrong

nodes.headline: Would the proposed action exceed the limit?

Record the usage against the limit atomically with the allowance, so two concurrent actions cannot each see room only one of them has. Checking and then applying separately is how a limit of ten becomes twelve under load, and the overage is discovered afterwards
within the limit; usage recorded atomically
nodes.detail: the next action is measured against the updated usage, which is why the record and the allowance happen together

nodes.headline: Block or hold the affected action only, and record LIMIT_REACHED with the limit, the window and the current usage. Reaching a limit is the limit working - it is not abuse, and a message that implies otherwise is read as an accusation by someone who did exactly what they were permitted to do
What path exists from here?
Is the reset point authoritatively defined?
until the authoritative reset occurs
nodes.detail: timeout after the expected reset point plus its tolerance

nodes.headline: Record the window reset from its authoritative source rather than from an assumed clock. A locally assumed reset grants capacity the authority has not granted, and the two drift apart quietly
window reset; capacity available again under the same limit
nodes.detail: the blocked action is re-attempted and measured against the new window like any other

nodes.headline: LIMIT_REACHED with no route to more capacity in this window
nodes.detail: an authorized change to the limit, or a new window, makes the same action possible. Nothing about this state is a finding against the entity

nodes.headline: Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a limit increase or override policy permits to be sought

nodes.headline: Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a limit with no authoritatively defined reset

edges.label: Authoritative
edges.when: the count comes from the source that owns it and is current

edges.label: Derived, stale or possibly incorrect
edges.when: the count is inferred, cached, or disagrees with the owning source
a limit decision resting on a usage figure that may be wrong

edges.label: Within the limit
edges.when: the action fits inside the remaining allowance

edges.label: Exceeds it
edges.when: the action would take usage past the limit

edges.label: The limit resets on its own
edges.when: the measurement window rolls and capacity returns

edges.label: An increase or override is permitted
edges.when: policy provides a route to more capacity

edges.label: Neither
edges.when: the limit is fixed for this entity and this window

edges.label: Defined
edges.when: the window's reset is stated and comes from the source that owns the count

edges.label: Not defined
edges.when: no authoritative reset point exists for this window

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the authoritative reset occurs

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a reset that does not arrive when it should means the count or the window is wrong, and waiting longer on a broken clock blocks an entity indefinitely
a limit increase or override policy permits to be sought
a limit with no authoritatively defined reset

distinctFrom.because: A limit is a constraint the entity was told about and is entitled to consume. Routing it into risk assessment puts ordinary heavy users in front of a fraud analyst, and produces a risk history for behaviour that was permitted.

guardrails: A limit reached is not abuse.
A reset period is never invented.
A limit is never silently increased.
Concurrent usage updates cannot permit unintended over-consumption.
governance.reusableRule: A limit should constrain only the measured activity governed by that limit until usage, time or authorized policy changes make additional capacity valid.
governance.entityScope: the entity and the specific limit or quota constraining it
governance.entityNote: One limit, one measurement window, one authoritative count. Reaching it is an operational fact about usage and nothing about the user.

identity.title: Policy or risk state changed → re-evaluate affected work → resume, restrict or preserve
identity.purpose: Apply a change where the new authority actually reaches, and leave the past alone.

requires: a material authoritative change - a policy version, a cleared risk case, a moved restriction threshold, a changed compliance requirement, a revoked exception, or a new authoritative classification

nodes.headline: Policy or risk state changed

Identify the active and future work the change actually touches. A policy update that restarts every journey in the system is indistinguishable from an outage, and it buries the handful of cases the change was genuinely about

Preserve completed actions exactly as they are. An action validly completed under the policy that governed it stays valid - a new rule does not make everybody retroactively non-compliant, and rewriting the record on a policy release destroys the evidence that anything ever complied
What are the change's effective-time semantics?

Apply the change to future relevant actions and leave pending work on the version that governed it when it started. Work in flight under an older version is not non-compliant - it is mid-process under the rule it began under
Has a newer evaluation already been applied to this work?

Suppress this evaluation. A queued policy job carrying an older version will otherwise overwrite a decision made under a newer one, and the regression is silent - the record shows a valid evaluation against a rule that has already been superseded
stale policy evaluation suppressed; the newer version's decision stands
nodes.detail: the newest authority governs. A further change is propagated on its own terms rather than by replaying this one

nodes.headline: Re-evaluate the pending work against the governing effective-time semantics, item by item. What is re-evaluated is the pending decision rather than the completed action behind it
What does the re-evaluation require now?

Record that the change was evaluated against this work and required nothing. Recording the non-change is what stops the same evaluation running again on the next release, and it is the evidence that the change was considered rather than missed
evaluated against the change and unchanged by it
nodes.detail: a later change is evaluated on its own terms. This record is what makes it cheap to see this one was already handled

nodes.headline: Capability restoration → revalidate → restore safely
nodes.detail: a restriction the change no longer justifies

nodes.headline: Risk threshold crossed → apply scoped restriction → review or release
nodes.detail: work the change now requires restricting

nodes.headline: Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a change with undefined effective-time semantics

edges.label: Prospective only
edges.when: the change governs actions from its effective time onward

edges.label: It reaches work already in flight
edges.when: the change explicitly applies to pending work started under the previous version

edges.label: The semantics are not defined
edges.when: nothing states whether the change reaches work in flight

edges.label: Nothing newer
edges.when: this is the most recent authority applied to it

edges.label: A newer version already governs it
edges.when: the work has already been evaluated under a later policy version than this job carries

edges.label: A current restriction is no longer justified
edges.when: the change removes the basis for something currently restricted

edges.label: A new restriction now applies
edges.when: the change creates a basis for restricting something currently permitted

edges.label: Nothing changes for existing work
edges.when: the change reaches this work and requires nothing different of it
a restriction the change no longer justifies
work the change now requires restricting
a change with undefined effective-time semantics

distinctFrom.because: RSK-191 evaluates one action at its decision point. This propagates a change across work already in flight, where the hard question is not what the rule says but which states the new rule is entitled to reach.

guardrails: A new policy does not mean a historical action was always invalid.
A cleared risk does not automatically restore an unrelated expired entitlement.
A policy update does not indiscriminately restart every existing journey.
A stale policy-evaluation job never overwrites a decision made under a newer version.
governance.reusableRule: Policy and risk changes should alter only the current or future states to which the new authority applies while preserving the historical context under which prior actions occurred.
governance.entityScope: the policy or risk state change and the work it actually touches
governance.entityNote: Completed actions are outside its reach by construction. What it re-evaluates is pending and future work, item by item.

identity.title: Availability query → evaluate capacity → offer valid options
identity.purpose: Produce the options that are genuinely bookable right now, and say plainly that nothing is being held.

requires: a request for bookable times against an identified resource, service or context

nodes.headline: Availability requested
Does an authoritative capacity model exist for this resource and service?

Record that this resource has no authoritative capacity model, and return no options rather than every option. An absent constraint is not an absence of constraint - a resource with nothing configured will otherwise appear infinitely bookable, and the overbooking is discovered by whoever turns up

Evaluate the authoritative constraints together - the resource's capacity, the service's duration, the location and context, eligibility constraints, existing reservations and holds, the operating window, lead-time rules and any defined buffers. Operating hours are not availability: a clinic open until six with every slot taken has nothing at five

Return only the options currently valid for the requested resource and context, labelled as what they are - what appeared bookable at this instant. Nothing here is held, and under contention any of it can be gone before the requester acts
Did any valid option survive the evaluation?
Record NO_AVAILABILITY for the requested window, with the constraint that closed it where that can be said without exposing anything it should not
What does policy offer when the requested window is empty?

Offer the nearest valid window, labelled as a different window rather than presented as the one that was asked for. Someone who wanted Tuesday and is shown Friday should be able to see that at a glance
Record the requester as waitlisted, which reserves nothing. Waitlisted is not reserved, and someone who believes they hold a place they do not hold will plan their day around it
valid options offered; no capacity is held by this query
nodes.detail: any option shown can be taken by someone else before it is requested. The reservation revalidates against current capacity rather than against what was displayed

nodes.headline: waitlisted; nothing is reserved and no time is committed
nodes.detail: capacity being released offers the waitlisted requester a chance to book, which is a new request that has to be confirmed like any other

nodes.headline: NO_AVAILABILITY for the requested resource and window
nodes.detail: availability changes constantly as holds expire and reservations cancel. A later query is answered on its own terms rather than from this result

edges.label: It exists
edges.when: capacity, duration, operating window and any lead-time or buffer rules are defined

edges.label: It does not
edges.when: no authoritative capacity model covers this resource

edges.label: Options exist
edges.when: at least one slot satisfies every constraint

edges.label: None
edges.when: no slot in the requested window satisfies the constraints

edges.label: A different window
edges.when: policy allows offering the nearest valid alternative

edges.label: A waitlist
edges.when: the resource operates a waitlist for released capacity

edges.label: Nothing further
edges.when: policy offers neither

distinctFrom.because: FUL-142 asks whether an accepted obligation can be resourced at all. This asks which specific times a resource can be committed to, for a requester who has not committed to anything yet.

guardrails: A displayed schedule is not guaranteed availability until a reservation or hold succeeds.
Availability is never inferred from generic operating hours.
Availability is evaluated for the requested resource and context rather than for the service in general.
governance.reusableRule: Availability represents capacity that appears bookable at query time; commitment begins only after that capacity is successfully reserved.
governance.entityScope: the availability request and the schedulable resource or service it asks about
governance.entityNote: The request is a question, not a claim on anything. Nothing it returns is protected between being shown and being requested.

identity.title: Slot hold → reserve temporarily → confirm, expire or release
identity.purpose: Protect specific capacity for a bounded moment while a booking is being completed, without pretending it is a booking.

requires: a hold granted against real, currently free capacity on an identified slot
insufficientAlone: a hold requested, which is not a hold granted - under contention two requests can both be made and only one can succeed, and treating the request as the grant overbooks by exactly the number of losers

nodes.headline: Temporary hold granted
Does a live hold by this requester already cover this slot?

Return the existing hold rather than creating a second. A retried booking step produces one hold, not two - two holds against one slot consume twice the capacity and expire at two different moments, so the slot is unbookable long after either of them mattered

Create the scoped hold with its id, the resource and slot, the capacity held, the owner, the creation time, the expiry and the booking intent it belongs to. Record HELD. The hold consumes capacity for its duration and creates no commitment - nobody has an appointment, and nothing here should be described to the requester as if they do
until the booking is confirmed against this hold, or the hold is explicitly released, or the booking intent is abandoned
nodes.detail: timeout after the hold's expiry

nodes.headline: What resolved the hold?
Is the held capacity still required by anything live?
Release the capacity and record the hold EXPIRED. An expired hold consumes nothing, and the release happens because the clock said so rather than because anyone remembered

Release the capacity and record the hold RELEASED. The release is idempotent - releasing an already-released hold changes nothing rather than returning capacity a second time, and the difference between those two behaviours is how many people can be booked into one slot

Consume the hold into the confirmed reservation, moving the capacity from held to reserved in one step. Releasing first and re-taking opens a window - short, and entirely long enough - in which someone else takes the slot the requester has just paid for
consumed into a confirmed reservation; capacity never passed back through free
nodes.detail: the reservation now owns the capacity. A cancellation releases it through the cancellation lifecycle rather than through this hold

nodes.headline: EXPIRED; capacity released and available again
nodes.detail: the same requester can take a new hold on the same slot if it is still free, which is a new hold rather than an extension of this one

nodes.headline: RELEASED; capacity available again
nodes.detail: a repeated release against this hold is a no-op rather than a second return of capacity

edges.label: One already exists
edges.when: an unexpired hold with the same owner and slot is live

edges.label: None
edges.when: no live hold covers it

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the booking is confirmed against this hold, the hold is explicitly released, the booking intent is abandoned

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the expiry is the entire point of a hold. Capacity still counted against a lapsed one is capacity nobody can book and nobody owns, and the resource reads as full while standing empty

edges.label: Confirmed
edges.when: a reservation was confirmed against this hold

edges.label: Explicitly released
edges.when: the owner or the booking flow released it

edges.label: The intent was abandoned
edges.when: the booking attempt that created it stopped

edges.label: No longer needed
edges.when: nothing else depends on this capacity being held

edges.label: Still needed
edges.when: another live booking step for the same requester still depends on it

distinctFrom.because: FUL-143 allocates a resource to an obligation that already exists. This protects capacity for a commitment that does not exist yet and may never - most holds end in expiry rather than in a booking.

guardrails: A hold is not a confirmed reservation.
An expired hold consumes no capacity.
Hold creation and release are both idempotent.
Concurrent holds respect real capacity rather than the capacity each of them assumed.
governance.reusableRule: A temporary hold protects capacity for a bounded period without creating the full commitment of a confirmed reservation.
governance.entityScope: the hold, the capacity it protects and the requester who owns it
governance.entityNote: One hold per requester per slot. A second hold by the same requester consumes the capacity twice and releases at two different times.

identity.title: Reservation request → validate → confirm, reject or pending
identity.purpose: Turn a request for a specific time into a commitment both sides can rely on, or say clearly that it did not.

requires: a request to reserve an identified slot on an identified resource or service
insufficientAlone: a payment attempt for the booking, which funds it without confirming it unless the booking semantics explicitly make payment the confirming act
a slot being held, which protects capacity without committing anyone to anything

nodes.headline: Reservation requested
Capture the requested slot, the resource or service, the requester, the details the booking requires and the intent behind it
Does a confirmed reservation already exist for this requester, resource and slot?
already confirmed; the existing reservation stands and no second one was created
nodes.detail: a genuinely different booking is a different request. A resubmitted one resolves here rather than consuming a second slot

nodes.headline: Re-read the slot's current state rather than trusting what the requester was shown. The availability they saw was true when it was rendered and may not be true now - under contention this is the single most common way two people end up holding one appointment, and only one of them finds out at the door
Is the capacity still available to this requester?

Record the request REJECTED with the reason. What is offered next is current availability rather than the set the requester was originally shown, which by definition contains at least one slot that no longer exists
Availability query → evaluate capacity → offer valid options
nodes.detail: a reservation that could not be made against the requested slot

nodes.headline: Validate the requester's eligibility, the details the booking requires and the dependencies its semantics define. Eligibility for a service and availability of a slot are different questions, and passing one says nothing about the other
What do the booking requirements say?

Record PENDING_CONFIRMATION with exactly what is outstanding, and keep the capacity protected for as long as the booking semantics allow. Pending is not confirmed and the requester is told which - an appointment someone believes they have and does not have is worse than being asked to wait
until the outstanding confirmation or dependency resolves, or the request is withdrawn
nodes.detail: timeout after the pending window the booking semantics allow

nodes.headline: How did the pending requirement resolve?
Record the request as lapsed and release any capacity protected for it. The slot returns to availability rather than staying reserved against a booking that never completed
request lapsed; capacity released and nothing committed
nodes.detail: a new request is evaluated against current availability, which may no longer include the slot that was being held

nodes.headline: Create the commitment explicitly. Record CONFIRMED_RESERVATION with the slot, the resource, the parties and the terms. This is the point at which two parties owe each other a specific time - the customer arranges their day around it and the provider stops selling the slot - and nothing before it was that
Reservation confirmed → prepare → upcoming or ready
nodes.detail: a confirmed reservation with time still to run before it

edges.label: It exists
edges.when: the same booking is already confirmed

edges.label: None
edges.when: no confirmed reservation covers it

edges.label: Available
edges.when: the slot is free, or is held by this requester

edges.label: Gone
edges.when: the capacity was taken between the query and the request
a reservation that could not be made against the requested slot

edges.label: All satisfied
edges.when: eligibility, details and dependencies are all in place

edges.label: A further confirmation or dependency is required
edges.when: the booking semantics require an approval, a prepayment or a verification before it can commit

edges.label: Not met
edges.when: a requirement fails and cannot be satisfied for this request

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the outstanding confirmation or dependency resolves, the request is withdrawn

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: capacity protected indefinitely for a booking that never completes is capacity taken from everyone who would have completed one

edges.label: Resolved
edges.when: the outstanding confirmation or dependency completed

edges.label: Withdrawn
edges.when: the requester withdrew before it resolved
a confirmed reservation with time still to run before it

distinctFrom.because: FUL-141 creates a generic fulfillment obligation. This creates a commitment to a specific time on both sides - which is why it revalidates capacity at the moment of confirming and why its failure mode is contention rather than eligibility.

guardrails: A request submitted is not a reservation confirmed.
Previously displayed availability may have changed and is revalidated rather than trusted.
A payment attempt alone does not confirm a reservation unless the authoritative booking semantics say so.
governance.reusableRule: A reservation becomes confirmed only when the requested capacity and all required booking conditions have been authoritatively committed.
governance.entityScope: the reservation request, the requester and the resource or service it names
governance.entityNote: One reservation per requester, resource and slot. A retried submission produces the same reservation rather than a second one against the same capacity.

identity.title: Reservation confirmed → prepare → upcoming or ready
identity.purpose: Get the conditions for a successful service in place, without letting them move the time that was promised.

requires: a reservation confirmed with a scheduled time still in the future

nodes.headline: Reservation confirmed

Determine the pre-event requirements this booking actually has - forms, documents, instructions, resource preparation, verification, prepayment, a check-in requirement, provider preparation. Which apply is a property of this service rather than a standard list, and running the standard list asks people for things their appointment does not need
Is each prerequisite already satisfied or already running?
Do not repeat it. A verification completed last month is completed, and re-running it opens a second journey against one requirement and asks the customer for something they have already given
Initiate each outstanding prerequisite on its own lifecycle. The reservation's time does not move while they run, and none of them owns the booking
until every prerequisite completes, or the booking materially changes
nodes.detail: timeout after the pre-service checkpoint policy defines ahead of the scheduled time

nodes.headline: What resolved the wait?
preparation superseded by a change to the booking
nodes.detail: the reschedule or cancellation owns what happens next. Preparation is re-derived against the new booking rather than carried across, because a different time can need different things

nodes.headline: Is an unresolved prerequisite critical to delivering the service?

Record AT_RISK or HOLD according to policy, naming the prerequisite. The confirmed time is not moved here - a preparation failing is a reason to escalate or to contact someone, and moving an appointment is a booking decision that belongs to the reschedule lifecycle
Responsibility escalation → higher authority → resolution or return
nodes.detail: a critical prerequisite unresolved at the pre-service checkpoint

nodes.headline: Record READY or UPCOMING with which prerequisites are complete and which are outstanding but not critical. A reminder having been sent is recorded separately from preparation being complete, because the first is something we did and the second is something that happened
READY or UPCOMING; the commitment stands and its conditions are in the state recorded
nodes.detail: the revalidation at service time reads the booking's current state rather than this readiness record, which was true when it was written

edges.label: Already handled
edges.when: the requirement is satisfied, or a journey against it is already live

edges.label: Outstanding
edges.when: the requirement is neither satisfied nor in progress

edges.label: on event
edges.when: every prerequisite completes, the booking materially changes

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the checkpoint is the last point at which an unresolved prerequisite can still be acted on. After it, the choice is to proceed unprepared or to disrupt someone's day at short notice

edges.label: Preparation complete
edges.when: every prerequisite finished before the checkpoint

edges.label: The booking changed
edges.when: the reservation was rescheduled, cancelled or materially altered

edges.label: Critical
edges.when: the service cannot be delivered properly without it

edges.label: Not critical
edges.when: the service can proceed and the requirement can follow
a critical prerequisite unresolved at the pre-service checkpoint

guardrails: A reminder sent is not preparation complete.
Duplicate prerequisite journeys are not created for a requirement already satisfied or running.
Preparation never alters the confirmed time unless the booking rules themselves require it.
governance.reusableRule: A confirmed reservation should preserve the time commitment while independently preparing the conditions required for successful service delivery.
governance.entityScope: the confirmed reservation and the preparation running against it
governance.entityNote: The preparation is subordinate to the booking. It can fail, and the booking stays confirmed while somebody decides what to do about it.

identity.title: Reschedule request → recheck availability → move, reject or preserve original
identity.purpose: Move a commitment to a new time without ever leaving the customer holding neither.

requires: an authorized request to move an existing confirmed reservation
insufficientAlone: someone viewing other times, which is looking rather than asking to move

nodes.headline: Reschedule requested

Keep the original reservation confirmed and intact while the replacement is evaluated. Releasing it first is the mistake this journey exists to prevent - the customer ends up with no appointment at all, and the slot they had is gone by the time anyone realises the replacement was not available
Search and validate the target availability against current authoritative capacity, for the resource and service the original booking actually requires
Is a valid replacement available?

Record the reschedule as not possible and leave the original reservation exactly as it was. The customer still has their appointment, which is the position they were in before they asked - and is a far better outcome than the alternative
original reservation preserved unchanged; no move took place
nodes.detail: the reschedule can be attempted again against different availability. Cancelling the original is a separate decision the customer makes explicitly

nodes.headline: Secure the new slot under the same scheduling semantics as an original booking - a hold and then a confirmation, or a direct commitment where the resource permits. The replacement has to be genuinely committed before anything is given up
Was the replacement actually secured?

Transfer the commitment to the new slot, recording the original time, the new one and the fact that this reservation moved. The original time stays readable - a reservation that only ever shows its current time cannot answer how many times it was moved, which is the first thing anyone investigating a service problem wants to know
Release the original slot, and only now. Capacity returns to availability at the point the replacement is real, which is the ordering the whole journey exists to enforce

Reconcile everything that pointed at the old time - the resource, the provider, the instructions, the prepayment, the preparation tasks and every queued notification. A reminder still aimed at the original time will fire, and the customer will arrive on the wrong day because of it
Does the new time or resource change what preparation is required?
Reservation confirmed → prepare → upcoming or ready
nodes.detail: a rescheduled booking whose preparation requirements have changed

nodes.headline: moved; the new time is committed and the original is preserved in the record
nodes.detail: a further move is a new reschedule against this reservation, and it joins the same history rather than replacing it

edges.label: One exists
edges.when: a slot satisfying the booking's requirements is currently free

edges.label: None
edges.when: nothing valid is available in the requested window

edges.label: Secured
edges.when: the new slot is committed to this reservation

edges.label: Lost to contention
edges.when: the slot was taken between finding it and securing it

edges.label: It changes
edges.when: a different provider, location or lead time alters the prerequisites

edges.label: Unchanged
edges.when: the same preparation applies and is already in the state it was
a rescheduled booking whose preparation requirements have changed

distinctFrom.because: SUB-166 changes the terms of a continuing relationship. This moves one specific occurrence to a different time or resource, and its whole difficulty is contention for the replacement - which terms changes never have.

guardrails: A reschedule requested is not a reschedule completed.
The original slot is never released before the replacement is secured unless policy explicitly requires it.
The historical original time remains auditable.
governance.reusableRule: Rescheduling should preserve the existing commitment until a valid replacement commitment has been successfully established.
governance.entityScope: the existing reservation and the reschedule request raised against it
governance.entityNote: One reservation throughout, carrying every time it has held. A reschedule is a move recorded on it rather than a cancellation followed by a new booking.

identity.title: Reservation cancellation → stop commitment → release capacity → reconcile
identity.purpose: End a future time commitment cleanly, returning the capacity and leaving the money to be decided elsewhere.

requires: an authorized cancellation of a confirmed reservation, taking effect
insufficientAlone: a cancellation requested, which is a request and may be blocked or may be for a later effective time
someone not responding to a reminder, which is silence rather than a cancellation

nodes.headline: Reservation cancellation effective

Record the actor and source, the reason, the effective time, the reservation's state at cancellation, and the timing relative to the scheduled service. The timing is what most cancellation policies turn on, and it has to be recorded at the moment rather than reconstructed afterwards from timestamps that mean something else
Which side cancelled?
Provider or resource cancellation → reallocate → reschedule, remedy or cancel
nodes.detail: a cancellation originating on the provider side

nodes.headline: Mark the reservation CANCELLED, preserving everything about it - the original booking, the times it held, the preparation that ran. The history is not deleted, because a released slot is capacity returning to the pool and says nothing about whether the appointment ever existed

Release the reserved capacity where the booking semantics permit it. The release is idempotent - an already-released reservation returns capacity once rather than once per attempt, and the difference shows up as two people booked into one room

Stop the obsolete preparation, reminders and check-in actions. A reminder for a cancelled appointment brings someone to a place where nobody is expecting them, which is the most avoidable failure in this whole category
Is an external provider or booking system holding this reservation?

Verify the cancellation actually took effect on the external side. A cancellation we recorded and they did not leaves them holding a slot we have released, and both sides discover it when someone arrives
Did the external side confirm the cancellation?
external:external-status-reconciliation
nodes.detail: a cancellation the external booking system has not confirmed

nodes.headline: Does the cancellation carry a financial consequence?
Refund request → eligibility → approve, reject or review
nodes.detail: a cancelled reservation that was paid for

nodes.headline: Financial obligation created → due → satisfied or outstanding
nodes.detail: a cancellation the terms attach a fee to

nodes.headline: CANCELLED; capacity released, history preserved, nothing owed
nodes.detail: a new booking is a new reservation rather than this one resuming, and this cancellation stays part of the record either way

edges.label: The customer or requester
edges.when: the cancellation originates from the party who booked

edges.label: The provider or resource side
edges.when: the cancellation originates because we cannot deliver
a cancellation originating on the provider side

edges.label: It is
edges.when: the slot exists in a system outside our own

edges.label: It is not
edges.when: the reservation is entirely internal

edges.label: Confirmed
edges.when: the external system authoritatively reports it cancelled

edges.label: Not confirmed
edges.when: the external side is unreachable, silent or still shows it booked
a cancellation the external booking system has not confirmed

edges.label: A refund or credit may be due
edges.when: the booking was paid for and the terms may return some or all of it

edges.label: A cancellation fee applies
edges.when: the terms create a charge given the timing of the cancellation

edges.label: Neither
edges.when: nothing was paid and the terms create no charge
a cancelled reservation that was paid for
a cancellation the terms attach a fee to

distinctFrom.because: FUL-150 cancels what remains of a generic fulfillment obligation. This ends a specific future time commitment, which releases capacity someone else can use and turns on timing relative to the appointment rather than on remaining scope.

guardrails: A cancellation requested is not a cancellation effective.
A cancellation is not a no-show.
Cancellation never deletes reservation history.
The refund or fee decision belongs to the financial lifecycle rather than to this one.
governance.reusableRule: Reservation cancellation ends the future time-bound commitment while independently reconciling released capacity and any resulting financial obligations.
governance.entityScope: the reservation and the cancellation acting on it
governance.entityNote: The reservation survives its own cancellation as a record. A released slot says something about capacity and nothing about whether the appointment existed.

identity.title: Scheduled time approaches → revalidate → check in, start or exception
identity.purpose: Start a service from what the booking is now, not from a confirmation issued weeks ago.

requires: the defined pre-start or start window for a scheduled occurrence being reached

nodes.headline: Pre start window reached

Re-read the booking from authoritative current state - is the reservation still confirmed, is the resource or provider available, are the required prerequisites met, does eligibility still hold where it is required, is there a material operational restriction. The confirmation from three weeks ago is not evidence about now, and this job is running because of a clock rather than because anything was checked
Is the reservation still valid?

Record the scheduled job as suppressed, naming what superseded it. A stale start job revives a cancelled booking, allocates a provider to it, and then produces a no-show for someone who cancelled correctly - three wrong outcomes from one unchecked assumption
stale start suppressed; no service was begun and no attendance state was written
nodes.detail: the booking's current version has its own scheduled occurrence, which revalidates on its own terms when it arrives

nodes.headline: Can the provider or resource actually deliver?
Provider or resource cancellation → reallocate → reschedule, remedy or cancel
nodes.detail: a booking that cannot be delivered by its assigned provider or resource

nodes.headline: Are the critical prerequisites met?

Record the occurrence as blocked at service time with the missing prerequisite, and do not start. Starting a service whose prerequisite is missing produces a partial or invalid delivery, which then needs a remedy - and the customer has spent the appointment either way
Responsibility escalation → higher authority → resolution or return
nodes.detail: a service blocked at its own start time

nodes.headline: Record READY_TO_START. The scheduled time arriving is not the service starting - the two are kept apart because everything between them can still fail, and most of what fails in this category fails exactly here
until attendance or check-in is authoritatively established, or the reservation is cancelled inside the window
nodes.detail: timeout after the arrival window policy defines

nodes.headline: What happened inside the arrival window?
Attendance or service start → complete, partial or interrupted
nodes.detail: attendance established for a revalidated booking

nodes.headline: Reservation cancellation → stop commitment → release capacity → reconcile
nodes.detail: a cancellation arriving inside the start window

nodes.headline: No-show or missed appointment → validate → rebook, close or consequence
nodes.detail: an arrival window closing with no attendance established

edges.label: Still confirmed
edges.when: the booking stands as scheduled

edges.label: Cancelled or rescheduled since
edges.when: the booking has moved or ended since the job was scheduled

edges.label: They can
edges.when: the assigned provider and resource are available and able

edges.label: They cannot
edges.when: the provider is unavailable, the resource failed, or the location cannot host it
a booking that cannot be delivered by its assigned provider or resource

edges.label: Met
edges.when: everything the service requires to start properly is in place

edges.label: Missing
edges.when: a prerequisite the service cannot proceed without is unresolved
a service blocked at its own start time

edges.label: on event
edges.when: attendance or check-in is authoritatively established, the reservation is cancelled inside the window

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the arrival window is what makes a missed appointment a fact rather than an assumption. Concluding before it closes records a no-show against someone who is running late and about to walk in

edges.label: Attended
edges.when: attendance or check-in was authoritatively established

edges.label: Cancelled inside the window
edges.when: the booking was cancelled after the start window opened
attendance established for a revalidated booking
a cancellation arriving inside the start window
an arrival window closing with no attendance established

guardrails: The scheduled time being reached is not the service having started.
Interaction with a reminder is not attendance.
A stale scheduled job never revives a cancelled or rescheduled reservation.
governance.reusableRule: A scheduled commitment should begin only after the reservation and its critical dependencies are revalidated at the time of service.
governance.entityScope: the confirmed reservation and the occurrence about to begin
governance.entityNote: The scheduled job carries the booking version it was created against. Everything it does begins with comparing that against the booking as it now stands.

identity.title: Attendance or service start → complete, partial or interrupted
identity.purpose: Separate the fact that someone turned up from the question of whether they got what they came for.

requires: attendance or service commencement established authoritatively
insufficientAlone: a reminder being opened or clicked, which is interest rather than attendance
arriving at a location, where the booking semantics require a check-in to establish attendance

nodes.headline: Service commencement established
Record IN_SERVICE or ATTENDED. The interaction is happening and nothing about its outcome is known yet
Track the scope actually delivered, where the service has a scope worth tracking. What is recorded is what was delivered rather than the fact that the appointment took place
until the service completes, or the service is interrupted
nodes.detail: timeout after the scheduled duration plus its tolerance

nodes.headline: Record the occurrence's outcome as unknown - someone attended and what happened afterwards was never recorded. This is not completion, and treating it as completion closes an obligation nobody confirmed was met
external:side-effect-reconciliation
nodes.detail: an occurrence that began and whose outcome was never established

nodes.headline: How did the service end?
Record COMPLETED. The scheduled obligation was met, which is a different claim from the appointment having happened
COMPLETED; attendance and delivery both established
nodes.detail: a problem raised afterwards about what was delivered is a post-completion issue and is assessed on its own terms

nodes.headline: Record PARTIALLY_COMPLETED with exactly what was delivered and what remains. Attendance is not a successful outcome, and a half-delivered service recorded as complete closes something the customer is still owed - they will find out, and they will find out later than we could have told them
Remedy selection → resolve obligation → financial handoff if needed
nodes.detail: a scheduled service delivered only in part

nodes.headline: Record the interruption with its cause and the point at which delivery stopped
What does the interruption allow?

Resume the same occurrence and continue tracking delivered scope. The wait's timeout is the scheduled duration and does not extend, so an occurrence that keeps stopping reaches its limit rather than running indefinitely
Reschedule request → recheck availability → move, reject or preserve original
nodes.detail: remaining scope needing a further scheduled occurrence

nodes.headline: Record that attendance happened and the service did not. This is a different fact from a no-show and from a cancellation - the customer did everything asked of them and left with nothing, which is the outcome most likely to be recorded wrongly and least likely to be forgotten by them
Why could it not proceed?
Provider or resource cancellation → reallocate → reschedule, remedy or cancel
nodes.detail: a service that could not proceed for provider-side reasons after the customer arrived

nodes.headline: Reschedule request → recheck availability → move, reject or preserve original
nodes.detail: a service that could not proceed because a customer-side requirement was absent

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the service completes, the service is interrupted

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: an occurrence that started and was never concluded is unknown rather than complete, and closing it as complete makes an unfulfilled service invisible to everyone downstream
an occurrence that began and whose outcome was never established

edges.label: Fully delivered
edges.when: the whole scheduled service was delivered

edges.label: Partly delivered
edges.when: some of the scheduled scope was delivered and some was not

edges.label: Interrupted
edges.when: delivery started and stopped before finishing

edges.label: Could not proceed after arrival
edges.when: the customer was present and the service never began
a scheduled service delivered only in part

edges.label: Resuming now
edges.when: the cause cleared and the remaining scope fits inside the occurrence

edges.label: Another appointment
edges.when: the remaining scope needs a separate scheduled occurrence

edges.label: A remedy
edges.when: the shortfall needs resolving rather than repeating
remaining scope needing a further scheduled occurrence

edges.label: The provider or resource side
edges.when: the provider, equipment, location or capacity failed at the point of delivery

edges.label: Something the customer had to bring
edges.when: a required document, condition or preparation the customer owns was absent
a service that could not proceed for provider-side reasons after the customer arrived
a service that could not proceed because a customer-side requirement was absent

guardrails: Check-in is not service completed.
Attendance is not a successful outcome.
Partial service is never represented as full completion.
governance.reusableRule: Attendance establishes that the scheduled interaction occurred; completion depends on the actual service obligation being delivered.
governance.entityScope: the reservation occurrence and the service delivered inside it
governance.entityNote: Attendance is about the occurrence. Completion is about the obligation. One appointment can end with the first true and the second false.

identity.title: No-show or missed appointment → validate → rebook, close or consequence
identity.purpose: Establish that one confirmed booking did not happen because the customer did not attend, having ruled out every other explanation.

requires: a confirmed occurrence whose service and arrival windows have both closed with no commencement established
insufficientAlone: the scheduled start time having passed, which does not close the arrival window and concludes nothing about someone who is running late

nodes.headline: Service window passed without commencement

Re-read the reservation's latest events before concluding anything. The missed-appointment job runs on a clock and the booking may have moved under it minutes earlier - this check is the difference between a fact and an accusation
Was the booking cancelled or rescheduled?

Suppress the no-show classification entirely. Recording one against someone who cancelled correctly, or who is booked for next Tuesday, attaches a penalty and a history to behaviour that was exactly right - and it is the kind of error people remember and repeat to others
no-show suppressed; the booking was cancelled or moved and nothing is attributed
nodes.detail: the rescheduled occurrence has its own window and is assessed on its own terms when it arrives

nodes.headline: Could the provider or resource actually have delivered?
Provider or resource cancellation → reallocate → reschedule, remedy or cancel
nodes.detail: a missed occurrence the provider side could not have delivered

nodes.headline: Do the booking's own semantics define what counts as failing to attend?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a missed occurrence with no defined attendance semantics

nodes.headline: Did the customer fail to attend under those semantics?
Attendance or service start → complete, partial or interrupted
nodes.detail: an arrival inside the grace period the semantics allow

nodes.headline: Record NO_SHOW with the semantics it was judged under and the window that closed. This is the non-occurrence of one confirmed booking and nothing more - it is not a statement about the customer's engagement, their loyalty or their relationship, and journeys reading it should not treat it as one
What does policy define as the next action?
Availability query → evaluate capacity → offer valid options
nodes.detail: a missed appointment policy allows to be rebooked

nodes.headline: Financial obligation created → due → satisfied or outstanding
nodes.detail: a no-show the terms attach a charge to

nodes.headline: NO_SHOW recorded; no consequence beyond the record
nodes.detail: an attendance event arriving after this reconciles against the recorded no-show rather than being ignored - a late system update is a reason to correct the record, not evidence that the record was right

edges.label: It was
edges.when: a cancellation or reschedule exists against this occurrence

edges.label: It stands
edges.when: the booking was confirmed and unchanged through its window

edges.label: They could
edges.when: the provider and resource were available and able throughout the window

edges.label: They could not
edges.when: the provider was unavailable, the resource failed or the location could not host it
a missed occurrence the provider side could not have delivered

edges.label: Defined
edges.when: a grace period, a late-arrival rule and any partial-attendance rule are stated

edges.label: Not defined
edges.when: nothing authoritative states what counts as a no-show for this service
a missed occurrence with no defined attendance semantics

edges.label: They did not attend
edges.when: no arrival occurred inside the grace the semantics allow

edges.label: They attended late, within the grace
edges.when: arrival happened inside the allowance the semantics define
an arrival inside the grace period the semantics allow

edges.label: Rebooking is offered
edges.when: the service is one where missing it means booking again

edges.label: A financial consequence applies
edges.when: the terms attach a fee or a forfeit to a missed appointment

edges.label: Closure
edges.when: policy defines no further action
a missed appointment policy allows to be rebooked
a no-show the terms attach a charge to

distinctFrom.because: RET-22 reads a pattern of expected usage not happening across a relationship. This is the non-occurrence of one specific confirmed booking at one specific time, and it is established by exclusion rather than by observing a trend.

guardrails: A no-show is never inferred before the relevant service and arrival windows close.
A no-show is not a cancellation.
Fees and penalties are never invented.
A late-arriving attendance event reconciles against the recorded no-show state.
governance.reusableRule: A no-show should be recorded only after excluding cancellation, rescheduling and provider-side failure as explanations for the missed scheduled service.
governance.entityScope: the single reservation occurrence that did not take place
governance.entityNote: One occurrence. Nothing here says anything about the customer's engagement, their history or their relationship - it is a fact about one appointment.

identity.title: Provider or resource cancellation → reallocate → reschedule, remedy or cancel
identity.purpose: Recover a commitment we cannot keep, without any of the cost landing on the person who was ready.

requires: a confirmed reservation that can no longer be fulfilled by its assigned provider or resource - unavailability, resource failure, location closure, withdrawn capacity or an operational incident

nodes.headline: Provider or resource cannot fulfil

Identify every reservation the failure affects, and its scope. A closed location is not one cancellation - treating it as one produces a correct outcome for the booking that raised the alarm and silence for the forty behind it, each of whom finds out at the door

Record that the failure is provider-side. Whatever follows, the customer is not marked as having cancelled and is never classified as a no-show - they were available and the service was not, and the record has to say so before anything else touches this booking
Is an equivalent replacement available for the same time?

Reallocate to the replacement, preserving the commitment and the time. The replacement has to actually satisfy the service's requirements - a different provider who cannot perform the booked service is not a replacement, and substituting one moves the failure from before the appointment to during it
Release the obsolete allocation, idempotently. The original resource returns to availability once, whatever number of times the release is attempted
Does the reallocation change anything the customer needs to know?

Tell them what changed, distinguished from a reschedule because the time did not move. Someone who reads 'your appointment has changed' and assumes the time moved will miss an appointment we successfully saved
reallocated; the time and the commitment both stand
nodes.detail: the booking continues to its scheduled occurrence and revalidates there like any other

nodes.headline: Do the applicable decision rules permit rescheduling this booking?
Reschedule request → recheck availability → move, reject or preserve original
nodes.detail: a provider-side failure that can be recovered at another time

nodes.headline: Cancel the affected reservation, recorded as provider-side. Provider cancellation and customer cancellation are different terminal states with different consequences, and collapsing them charges a cancellation fee to someone whose appointment we could not keep
Release the allocation and stop the obsolete preparation, reminders and check-in actions. A reminder for an appointment we cancelled brings the customer in for a service that has no provider waiting
What does the failure leave to answer for?
Remedy selection → resolve obligation → financial handoff if needed
nodes.detail: a service obligation left unresolved by a provider-side failure

nodes.headline: Refund request → eligibility → approve, reject or review
nodes.detail: a provider-cancelled booking that was paid for

nodes.headline: cancelled on the provider side; recorded as ours, with nothing attributed to the customer
nodes.detail: a new booking is a new commitment. This cancellation stays in the record as a provider failure, which is what any later question about the customer's booking history depends on

edges.label: Available and permitted
edges.when: another provider or resource can deliver the booked service at the booked time, and the rules allow substituting

edges.label: Not at this time
edges.when: nothing equivalent is free, or substitution is not permitted for this service

edges.label: It does
edges.when: the provider, the location or the preparation is different

edges.label: It does not
edges.when: nothing visible to the customer changed

edges.label: Permitted
edges.when: the service can be delivered at another time and the rules allow moving it

edges.label: Not permitted
edges.when: the service was time-specific, or the rules do not allow it to move
a provider-side failure that can be recovered at another time

edges.label: An unresolved service obligation
edges.when: the customer still needs the service and it has not been delivered

edges.label: Money to return
edges.when: the booking was paid for or a fee was taken

edges.label: Neither
edges.when: nothing was owed and nothing was paid
a service obligation left unresolved by a provider-side failure
a provider-cancelled booking that was paid for

distinctFrom.because: FUL-145 handles a generic fulfillment exception. This carries the scheduling-specific recovery: the same time with a different provider, a different time with the same commitment, and the rule that the customer is never recorded as the cause.

guardrails: A provider cancellation is not a customer cancellation.
An affected customer is never classified as a no-show.
A replacement must satisfy the service's actual requirements rather than merely being available.
Financial and remedy consequences remain separate lifecycle decisions.
governance.reusableRule: Provider-side inability should preserve the customer's underlying service obligation and attempt recovery before treating the reservation as simply cancelled.
governance.entityScope: the affected reservations and the provider or resource failure behind them
governance.entityNote: The scope is every booking the failure touches. A closed location is not one cancellation, and treating it as one leaves the rest to be discovered by the people who turn up.

identity.title: Continuing relationship created → validate → activate or pending
identity.purpose: Keep the existence of a continuing agreement apart from the moment it actually starts running.

requires: an authorised agreement to enter a continuing relationship, with parties, scope and a term
insufficientAlone: a payment succeeding, which funds a relationship without being what starts it - some contracts activate on signature, some on provisioning, some on a regulatory date
a plan being selected in an interface
a structural link being created between two entities, which connects them without agreeing a term

nodes.headline: Continuing relationship creation authorized

Create the relationship record. Capture the relationship id, the parties, the product or service scope, the start and effective date, the term, the renewal model, the reference to its financial terms, the basis on which it grants entitlements, and its status. Record CREATED - the agreement exists and nothing is running
Is it effective immediately?
Record PENDING_EFFECTIVE_DATE. Nothing is granted and nothing is billed against a relationship that has not started
Future effective start → wait → revalidate → activate or abort
nodes.detail: a relationship created with a future effective start

nodes.headline: Determine the activation requirements that actually govern this relationship - payment, verification, contract execution, a provisioning prerequisite, a regulatory condition. Which of them apply is a property of this agreement rather than a universal list, and assuming payment is the only one activates contracts that were never signed
Are the required dependencies satisfied?
Record PENDING_REQUIREMENT, naming which requirement is outstanding. A relationship stuck as pending with no stated reason is indistinguishable from one that is simply broken
until the outstanding requirements are satisfied, or the agreement is withdrawn before starting
nodes.detail: timeout after the window policy allows a created but unstarted relationship to remain open

nodes.headline: What resolved the wait?

Record the relationship as never activated, preserving the record and the reason. It existed and did not start, which is a different thing from never having been created and is worth being able to count
created and never activated; no entitlement was ever granted
nodes.detail: a new agreement between the same parties is a new relationship rather than this one resuming, and it starts from its own conditions

nodes.headline: Record ACTIVE with the effective date and what satisfied each requirement. Active describes the agreement running - it does not describe what the agreement grants. Every entitlement comes from the relationship's stated entitlement basis, so that a relationship being active is never mistaken for entitlement to everything
Entitlement qualification → grant, deny or pending
nodes.detail: an active continuing relationship whose entitlements now need qualifying

edges.label: Effective now
edges.when: the effective date is now or has passed

edges.label: Effective later
edges.when: the effective date is in the future
a relationship created with a future effective start

edges.label: All satisfied
edges.when: every governing activation condition is authoritatively met

edges.label: Something outstanding
edges.when: at least one governing condition is not met

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the outstanding requirements are satisfied, the agreement is withdrawn before starting

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a relationship that never activates is not a relationship, and leaving it pending indefinitely holds resources and reporting against something that will never begin

edges.label: Requirements met
edges.when: the outstanding conditions are now authoritatively satisfied

edges.label: Withdrawn
edges.when: the agreement was withdrawn before it started
an active continuing relationship whose entitlements now need qualifying

distinctFrom.because: REL-91 links two entities: a person to an organisation, a parent account to a child, a representative to the entity they act for. Such a link has no term, nothing to renew and nothing to lapse. What is created here has all three, and it is frequently attached to a link REL-91 created rather than replacing it.

guardrails: A record created is not a relationship active.
Payment success alone does not define every contract's activation.

A structural link is not an agreement. A person belonging to an organisation, or one account being the parent of another, is a relationship with no term to run, and it belongs to the entity-structure lifecycle rather than here.
No entitlement is granted before the authoritative effective conditions are met.
governance.reusableRule: A continuing relationship becomes active only when its effective date and required activation conditions have been satisfied.
governance.entityScope: the continuing relationship record - a subscription, contract, membership, policy, licence or service agreement
governance.entityNote: One record per relationship, carrying every term it has ever run under. Terms are versions inside it rather than replacements of it.
