This category owns continuing relationships governed by terms and effective periods, with the lifecycle semantics that follow from them. It does not own a structural link between entities merely because that link is long-lived - that is REL-91.

identity.title: Future effective start → wait → revalidate → activate or abort
identity.purpose: Activate a future-dated relationship from what is true at the effective time, not from what was true when it was scheduled.

requires: a created relationship whose effective start is in the future

nodes.headline: Relationship created with future start

Record SCHEDULED with the effective time and the prerequisites as they stand today. What is stored is a snapshot for comparison later - a future agreement is not a currently active relationship, and nothing it would grant exists yet
until the relationship is cancelled before it starts, or a material prerequisite changes
nodes.detail: timeout after the effective time

nodes.headline: What happened before the effective time?

Record the change against the scheduled activation and keep waiting, rather than acting on it now. A prerequisite that lapsed in March may be back in order by the June start date, and failing the activation three months early answers a question nobody has asked yet. The wait's timeout is a fixed calendar point, so returning to it cannot extend it

Record CANCELLED_BEFORE_START and suppress the scheduled activation. A pre-start cancellation that leaves the job in place activates something nobody has any more, bills for it, and is discovered by the person receiving the invoice
cancelled before it started; never active and never billed
nodes.detail: a new agreement is a new relationship. This one is closed at a state it never left

nodes.headline: Re-read the relationship's current state at the effective time - is the agreement still valid, is the financial state what activation requires, does eligibility still hold, is the verification still current, are the dependencies still in place. The decision is made from what is authoritative now, and the stored snapshot is used only to see what moved
Do the requirements still hold?

Record HOLD with exactly what is missing and what would clear it. The relationship has reached its start date without starting, which is a state worth naming rather than leaving as an activation that silently did not happen
until the missing prerequisite is satisfied
nodes.detail: timeout after the hold window the governing terms allow

nodes.headline: Record FAILED_ACTIVATION or CANCELLED, according to which the governing policy defines for this failure. The two mean different things to the counterparty and the policy chooses between them - the distinction is not invented here
reached its effective date and did not activate
nodes.detail: the prerequisites being satisfied later does not activate this relationship retroactively. A new agreement is created if the parties still want one

nodes.headline: Record ACTIVE from the effective date, with what was true at the moment of activation rather than at the moment of scheduling
Entitlement qualification → grant, deny or pending
nodes.detail: a future-dated relationship activating at its effective time

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the relationship is cancelled before it starts, a material prerequisite changes

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: reaching the effective time is what this wait exists for. It is the normal outcome rather than a failure, and it is the point at which everything is checked again

edges.label: Cancelled before start
edges.when: the agreement was cancelled while still scheduled

edges.label: A prerequisite changed
edges.when: something activation depends on moved, in either direction

edges.label: Still satisfied
edges.when: everything activation depends on is authoritatively in place

edges.label: Recoverable, and policy permits a hold
edges.when: something is missing that could still be supplied, and the governing terms allow a delayed start

edges.label: No longer satisfied
edges.when: a governing condition has failed and policy does not permit waiting

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the missing prerequisite is satisfied

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a relationship held past its own start date indefinitely has effectively failed to activate, and saying so is better than an open hold that ages quietly
a future-dated relationship activating at its effective time

guardrails: A future agreement is not a currently active relationship.
A scheduled activation never executes blindly if its prerequisites changed.
A pre-start cancellation suppresses the stale activation job.
governance.reusableRule: Future-dated relationships should activate from current valid state at the effective time rather than from assumptions made when they were scheduled.
governance.entityScope: the future-dated continuing relationship and its scheduled activation
governance.entityNote: The prerequisites recorded at scheduling are a snapshot kept for comparison. They are never the basis on which activation proceeds.

identity.title: Renewal window → eligibility → renew, non-renew or review
identity.purpose: Reach a decision about the next term, as a decision - separate from anything that makes the next term real.

requires: a relationship whose term end is inside the renewal decision window its governing terms define
insufficientAlone: a renewal reminder having been sent, which is a communication and not a decision window opening

nodes.headline: Renewal decision window opens

Evaluate renewal eligibility, the renewal model, the relationship's current state, the notice the terms require, the pricing and terms that would apply, any outstanding blockers, and whether the counterparty has to decide at all
Are the renewal terms and required notice period defined?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a renewal window with no defined notice period or renewing terms

nodes.headline: Does an outstanding blocker prevent the renewal from being decided?
What does the renewal model require?

Put the renewal decision to whoever holds it, with the terms that would apply. Asking is not deciding - a renewal notice sent is a communication, and treating the send as the answer renews relationships nobody agreed to
until an authorized renewal decision is recorded
nodes.detail: timeout after the last point at which the required notice period still allows a decision

nodes.headline: Apply what the governing terms define as the outcome when no decision is made - which for some renewal models is renewal and for others is non-renewal. Record that no decision was made rather than recording a decision, because someone who did not answer did not agree
What is the outcome for the next term?
Record RENEWAL_REVIEW with what has to be settled. The relationship stays active on its current term throughout - a renewal under review is not a relationship in trouble
until the review concludes with an authorized decision
nodes.detail: timeout after the notice deadline

nodes.headline: Responsibility escalation → higher authority → resolution or return
nodes.detail: a renewal review outliving the notice period

nodes.headline: Record the renewal as decided, with the new term's dates and the terms that would apply. Decided is not renewed - the new term does not exist until its own requirements have been met, and a relationship can sit here and still lapse
Renewal execution → financial and dependency check → new term active
nodes.detail: a renewal decided and ready for execution

nodes.headline: Record NON_RENEWING with the effective end being the current term's end. The relationship is still active and still governed by its current term - non-renewing is a decision about the next term and says nothing about this one
Scheduled cancellation → revalidate at effective time → end or preserve
nodes.detail: a non-renewal scheduling an end at the current term's end

edges.label: Defined
edges.when: the governing terms state the notice period, the renewal model and the terms that would apply

edges.label: Not defined
edges.when: the notice period or the renewing terms are not stated anywhere authoritative
a renewal window with no defined notice period or renewing terms

edges.label: Blocked
edges.when: an unresolved obligation, dispute or eligibility problem stands in the way

edges.label: Clear
edges.when: nothing outstanding prevents a decision

edges.label: Auto-renew, requirements met
edges.when: the terms renew automatically and every condition for that is satisfied

edges.label: An explicit decision
edges.when: the terms require the counterparty to choose

edges.label: Review first
edges.when: the terms require an internal decision before renewal can be offered

edges.label: on event
edges.when: an authorized renewal decision is recorded

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the notice period is what makes the deadline real - past it, the terms themselves determine what happens, and pretending the decision is still open misrepresents the relationship

edges.label: Renew
edges.when: the decision, or the terms' default, is to continue

edges.label: Do not renew
edges.when: the decision, or the terms' default, is to let the term end

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the review concludes with an authorized decision

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a review that outlives the notice period has removed the counterparty's ability to plan, whichever way it eventually goes
a renewal review outliving the notice period
a renewal decided and ready for execution
a non-renewal scheduling an end at the current term's end

distinctFrom.because: This produces a decision. SUB-164 makes the new term exist, which depends on payment, confirmation and eligibility that this journey does not touch. A relationship can be decided-to-renew and still not renew.

competition.precedence: below a cancellation in motion and below an active risk state on the same relationship

guardrails: Renewal eligible is not renewed.
A renewal communication is not a renewal decision.
Renewal notice periods and renewing terms are never invented.
A relationship under renewal review stays active on its current term.

A relationship with a cancellation already in motion, or with an active risk state, is not sent a routine renewal message. The lifecycle that already owns the person takes precedence, and a renewal reminder arriving during a cancellation reads as a system that is not paying attention.
governance.reusableRule: Renewal is a new term decision governed by the current relationship state and applicable renewal rules.
governance.entityScope: the continuing relationship and the renewal cycle currently open on it
governance.entityNote: One renewal cycle per term boundary. A relationship renewed eight times has eight cycles in its history, each with what was decided and why.

identity.title: Renewal execution → financial and dependency check → new term active
identity.purpose: Make the new term exist, once the things it depends on have actually happened.

requires: a renewal decided or scheduled, with the new term's dates and terms
insufficientAlone: a renewal being eligible, which permits the decision rather than being it

nodes.headline: Renewal authorized for execution

Determine what the new term actually requires - payment, contract confirmation, updated eligibility, required verification, resource availability. Which of these apply comes from the relationship's own terms, and assuming payment is the only one renews contracts whose eligibility has lapsed
Does the new term require a financial event?

Raise the renewal's financial obligation through the financial lifecycle, which owns whether it is created, due and satisfied. This journey keeps ownership of the new term and waits for that outcome rather than handing the term away - otherwise a failed payment leaves a renewal nobody is holding
until every renewal dependency resolves successfully, or a renewal dependency fails authoritatively
nodes.detail: timeout after the last point at which the new term could still start on time

nodes.headline: How did the dependencies resolve?
What is blocking the new term?
Renewal payment failure → grace or recover → renew or lapse
nodes.detail: a renewal blocked by an authoritative payment failure

nodes.headline: Record RENEWAL_PENDING with exactly which dependency is missing. Pending with a named cause can be acted on; pending with no cause becomes a relationship that quietly stops renewing
until the blocking dependency clears
nodes.detail: timeout after the recovery window the governing terms allow

nodes.headline: Create the new term as a new term, with its own dates, price and scope, and leave the previous term intact. Overwriting the old term's dates with the new ones erases that the relationship ran at a different price for a different period, which is the exact record anyone auditing a renewal is looking for
Record the new term ACTIVE from its start date. The relationship now has two terms in its history and one of them is running
Does the new term change the entitlement scope?
Entitlement change → recalculate scope → expand, reduce or preserve
nodes.detail: a new term whose scope differs from the previous one

nodes.headline: NEW_TERM_ACTIVE; the previous term is preserved in full
nodes.detail: the next renewal window opens against this term and is a new cycle with its own decision and its own record

nodes.headline: Record the renewal as failed, with what prevented it. The relationship reaches its term end without a new term, which is a non-renewal reached by failure rather than by decision - and the two are worth distinguishing when someone asks why a customer left
Relationship end → final reconciliation → former or expired state
nodes.detail: a term ending with no new term created

edges.label: It does
edges.when: the renewal carries a charge, a commitment or a financial obligation

edges.label: It does not
edges.when: the new term carries no financial requirement, or one already satisfied

edges.label: on event
edges.when: every renewal dependency resolves successfully, a renewal dependency fails authoritatively

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a renewal that has not completed by its own start date has left the relationship between terms, which is a state that has to be named rather than waited through

edges.label: All satisfied
edges.when: every authoritative requirement for the new term is met

edges.label: Something failed
edges.when: a dependency failed authoritatively

edges.label: The renewal payment failed
edges.when: the financial requirement failed authoritatively

edges.label: Recoverable, and not financial
edges.when: a non-financial dependency is missing and could still be supplied

edges.label: Cannot complete
edges.when: the new term cannot be created under any available resolution
a renewal blocked by an authoritative payment failure

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the blocking dependency clears

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the terms define how long a relationship may sit between terms, and exceeding it is a non-renewal whether or not anyone says so

edges.label: It changes
edges.when: the renewing terms grant more, less or different rights than the previous term

edges.label: Unchanged
edges.when: the new term grants exactly what the previous one did
a new term whose scope differs from the previous one
a term ending with no new term created

distinctFrom.because: SUB-163 decides. This executes, and it is where renewals actually fail - on payment, on eligibility that moved, on a resource that is no longer available. A decision is not a term.

guardrails: A renewal scheduled is not a renewal completed.
A payment attempt is not renewal completion.
The previous term is never overwritten with the new term's dates.
governance.reusableRule: A renewal becomes effective only after the requirements for the new term have actually been satisfied.
governance.entityScope: the renewal operation and the new term it would create
governance.entityNote: The new term is created as a new term. The previous one keeps its dates, its price and its scope, because that is what any later question about the relationship is asked against.

identity.title: Renewal payment failure → grace or recover → renew or lapse
identity.purpose: Decide what the relationship does while a failed renewal payment is being chased, without ending it by reflex.

requires: an authoritative failure of a payment a renewal depends on
insufficientAlone: a payment attempt erroring in transit, which is unknown rather than failed - and treating unknown as failed puts relationships into grace over payments that succeeded

nodes.headline: Renewal payment failed

Raise the failure into the payment recovery lifecycle, which owns classification and collection. This journey does not chase the money; it holds the relationship's state while that runs, which is why it does not hand the relationship away
Does governing policy define grace or lapse semantics for this relationship?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a failed renewal payment with no defined grace or lapse semantics

nodes.headline: Apply the relationship state policy defines during recovery - ACTIVE_IN_GRACE, RENEWAL_PENDING, RESTRICTED or LAPSE_PENDING. What the counterparty keeps access to follows from that state and from policy, never from a default of leaving everything running or switching everything off
Does the recovery state restrict capability?
Raise the restriction through the access lifecycle, with the scope policy defines. What is switched off and how is owned there; what the relationship's contractual state is remains owned here
until the payment is recovered, or an authorized alternate resolution is agreed
nodes.detail: timeout after the grace deadline policy defines

nodes.headline: How was the obligation resolved?

Record how the obligation was resolved other than by the original payment. The renewal proceeds on that basis and the record says which basis, because a term that renewed on a waiver is not the same fact as one that renewed on a payment
Are the remaining renewal requirements still valid?
Renewal execution → financial and dependency check → new term active
nodes.detail: a recovered renewal obligation with its other requirements intact

nodes.headline: Record the outcome this relationship's own semantics define - LAPSED, EXPIRED or NON_RENEWED. These are different words for genuinely different things, and which one applies changes what the counterparty is told and what they can do next
Relationship end → final reconciliation → former or expired state
nodes.detail: a renewal that lapsed after its recovery window closed

edges.label: Defined
edges.when: policy states what state the relationship takes during recovery, what access it keeps and how long

edges.label: Not defined
edges.when: no policy covers what happens between a failed renewal payment and a lapse
a failed renewal payment with no defined grace or lapse semantics

edges.label: It restricts
edges.when: policy limits what the relationship can be used for during recovery

edges.label: Full access continues
edges.when: policy keeps the relationship fully usable through the grace period

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the payment is recovered, an authorized alternate resolution is agreed

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the grace period is policy's own answer to how long this may run. Extending it is a decision nobody made, and shortening it takes back something the counterparty was granted

edges.label: The payment was recovered
edges.when: the original obligation was satisfied authoritatively

edges.label: An alternate resolution was authorized
edges.when: a different method, a partial arrangement or a waiver settled it

edges.label: Still valid
edges.when: eligibility, verification and the other new-term requirements still hold

edges.label: No longer valid
edges.when: something else the new term needed has lapsed while the payment was being recovered
a recovered renewal obligation with its other requirements intact
a renewal that lapsed after its recovery window closed

distinctFrom.because: FIN-134 classifies the payment failure and tries to collect. This decides what the relationship is while that happens - in grace, restricted, pending or lapsing - which is a question about the contract rather than about the money.

guardrails: A payment failure is not immediate termination.
Grace periods are never invented.
Access during grace follows governing policy rather than a default in either direction.
A late payment is reconciled against the current relationship state, never applied retroactively.
governance.reusableRule: Renewal payment failure creates a recovery problem while the continuing relationship follows its defined grace or lapse semantics.
governance.entityScope: the continuing relationship and the renewal obligation whose payment failed
governance.entityNote: Two lifecycles running at once. The financial one is chasing money; this one is deciding what the counterparty can do in the meantime.

identity.title: Plan or terms change request → validate → schedule, apply or reject
identity.purpose: Apply an authorized change to a running relationship at the right time, as a delta against whatever is actually there then.

requires: an authorized request to change a running term-bearing relationship's plan, tier, scope or terms
insufficientAlone: someone asking about a different plan, which is a question rather than an authorized change
a structural relationship between the entities changing type or state, which changes how they are related rather than what was agreed

nodes.headline: Relationship change requested

Capture the current terms, the requested terms, the requested effective time, the scope delta and the reference to its financial impact. What is stored is the delta and the relationship version it was authorized against
Do the governing terms permit this change?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a change request the governing terms do not address

nodes.headline: Record the change as rejected, naming the term that rules it out. The relationship continues unchanged on its current terms
change rejected; the current terms stand
nodes.detail: the same change may become permitted at a different point in the relationship - at a term boundary, or after a minimum period - and is requested again then

nodes.headline: When does the change take effect?

Record SCHEDULED_CHANGE with the delta, the effective time and the relationship version it was authorized against. The delta is stored rather than the resulting terms, because what those terms would be depends on the relationship as it stands when the change lands
until the relationship ends before the change lands, or the change is withdrawn
nodes.detail: timeout after the change's effective time

nodes.headline: Record the scheduled change as void, with why. A downgrade scheduled against a relationship that has since ended has nothing to apply to, and firing it anyway writes terms onto something that is no longer running
scheduled change voided before it took effect
nodes.detail: the change can be requested again against whatever relationship exists now, and is evaluated on those terms

nodes.headline: Re-read the relationship at the effective time and check the delta still makes sense against it. A downgrade authorized in March, applied to a relationship upgraded twice since, produces terms nobody chose and an invoice nobody expects
Does the delta still apply to the relationship as it now stands?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a scheduled change whose base terms no longer exist

nodes.headline: Validate what the change requires - availability, eligibility, financial capacity, provisioning capability. A tier the relationship is not eligible for and a resource that cannot be supplied both stop the change at the same point
Are the change's dependencies satisfied?
Record the change as not applied, naming the dependency that blocked it, and leave the current terms in force. A half-applied change - new price, old scope - is worse than no change at all
change not applied; the current terms remain in force unchanged
nodes.detail: the change can be requested again once the blocking dependency is available

nodes.headline: Apply the delta as a new terms version, dated from its effective time. The prior terms stay in the record with the period they governed - rewriting them means last month's invoice no longer matches any terms the system holds
What does the applied delta touch?
Entitlement change → recalculate scope → expand, reduce or preserve
nodes.detail: an applied change that alters entitlement scope

nodes.headline: Financial obligation created → due → satisfied or outstanding
nodes.detail: an applied change with a financial consequence

nodes.headline: change applied as a new terms version; prior terms preserved
nodes.detail: further changes are new requests evaluated against this version rather than against the original agreement

edges.label: Permitted
edges.when: the terms allow a change of this kind at this point in the relationship

edges.label: Not permitted
edges.when: the terms rule it out - a minimum term, a locked tier, a contractual restriction

edges.label: The terms do not say
edges.when: nothing authoritative states whether this change is permitted
a change request the governing terms do not address

edges.label: Immediately
edges.when: the terms allow it now and the request asks for now

edges.label: At a future effective time or the next cycle
edges.when: the terms defer it, or the request asks for a later date

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the relationship ends before the change lands, the change is withdrawn

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: reaching the effective time is what the wait exists for, and it is the point at which the delta is checked against the relationship rather than applied to it

edges.label: Still applies
edges.when: the relationship is on the version the change was authorized against, or the delta is unambiguous against the current one

edges.label: Superseded
edges.when: the relationship has changed in a way that makes the delta ambiguous or contradictory
a scheduled change whose base terms no longer exist

edges.label: Satisfied
edges.when: everything the new terms require is in place

edges.label: Not satisfied
edges.when: a dependency the change needs is missing

edges.label: The entitlement scope
edges.when: the change adds, removes or alters what the relationship grants

edges.label: Financial terms only
edges.when: the change alters price, billing or commitment without changing scope

edges.label: Neither
edges.when: the change alters administrative or contractual detail with no scope or financial effect
an applied change that alters entitlement scope
an applied change with a financial consequence

distinctFrom.because: This changes the commercial relationship - the plan, the tier, the scope, the contractual terms. ACC-73 applies whatever entitlement delta results. One is what was agreed; the other is what is switched on.

This changes the authorized terms a continuing relationship runs under. REL-92 changes what the structural relationship between the entities means. A tier change leaves the person exactly as related to the organisation as they were, and a membership type changing leaves the plan exactly as it was priced.

guardrails: A change requested is not a change applied.
Historical terms are never rewritten.
A structural link changing type or state is not a plan or terms change merely because the same entities are involved.
A scheduled upgrade or downgrade never executes against a relationship that has ended or materially changed without revalidation.
governance.reusableRule: Continuing relationship changes should apply an authorized delta at the correct effective time while preserving prior term history.
governance.entityScope: the continuing relationship and the change request raised against it
governance.entityNote: The request stores a delta and the relationship version it was authorized against. It never stores the resulting terms, because those depend on a relationship that will have moved. What changes here is what a term-bearing continuing relationship is authorized to run under. It does not own a change to the structural link between the entities merely because the same two parties are involved - that is REL-92.

identity.title: Cancellation request → determine effective end → schedule or cancel now
identity.purpose: Establish whether and when a relationship will end, while the current term keeps running until it does.

requires: an authorized request to end a continuing relationship
insufficientAlone: someone asking how to cancel, or viewing a cancellation page, which is intent rather than a request

nodes.headline: Cancellation requested

Determine who holds the authority, the current term and state, what the relationship's cancellation semantics actually say, the effective end those semantics produce, and the obligations that already exist and will outlive it
Does the requester hold the authority to cancel this relationship?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a cancellation requested by someone whose authority is not established

nodes.headline: Are the relationship's cancellation semantics defined?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a cancellation request against a relationship with no defined cancellation semantics

nodes.headline: Does a valid requirement block the cancellation?

Record the blocker explicitly, with what would clear it and when. A cancellation refused without a stated reason becomes a complaint, and then a dispute, over something that was usually a date the counterparty could have waited for
cancellation blocked; the relationship continues unchanged and the request stands
nodes.detail: the request proceeds once the blocker clears. Nothing about the relationship changed in the meantime, including its entitlements

nodes.headline: When does the relationship end?
Record the effective end as now, under the semantics that permit it, together with what remains owed on both sides
Relationship end → final reconciliation → former or expired state
nodes.detail: a cancellation taking effect immediately

nodes.headline: Record NON_RENEWING or CANCELLATION_SCHEDULED with the effective end, and leave the relationship ACTIVE. The current term keeps running and every entitlement it grants keeps working until that date - cutting access at the moment of request bills someone for a period they cannot use, and turns a clean exit into a refund claim
Scheduled cancellation → revalidate at effective time → end or preserve
nodes.detail: a cancellation scheduled for a future effective end

edges.label: Authorized
edges.when: the requester is a party or holds the delegated right to end it

edges.label: Not established
edges.when: the requester's authority over this relationship is unclear or absent
a cancellation requested by someone whose authority is not established

edges.label: Defined
edges.when: the terms state when cancellation takes effect, what notice applies and what survives it

edges.label: Not defined
edges.when: nothing authoritative states how this relationship ends
a cancellation request against a relationship with no defined cancellation semantics

edges.label: Blocked
edges.when: a minimum term, an outstanding obligation or a regulatory notice stands in the way

edges.label: Clear
edges.when: nothing valid prevents the relationship from ending

edges.label: Immediately
edges.when: the semantics permit an immediate end and that is what was requested

edges.label: At the end of the current term
edges.when: the semantics defer the end to the term boundary
a cancellation taking effect immediately
a cancellation scheduled for a future effective end

distinctFrom.because: This decides that the relationship will end and when. SUB-168 checks, at that date, whether the decision still applies to the relationship as it then is - which is a different question with a different failure mode.

competition.precedence: a cancellation in motion outranks a renewal decision on the same relationship

guardrails: A cancellation requested is not a relationship cancelled.
Non-renewing is not currently inactive.
Current entitlement is never ended early when the cancellation is end-of-term.
Cancellation semantics are never invented.
governance.reusableRule: Cancellation determines whether and when a continuing relationship will end; the relationship remains governed by its current term until that effective end occurs.
governance.entityScope: the continuing relationship and the cancellation request raised against it
governance.entityNote: The request produces an effective end date. It does not produce an ended relationship, and between the two the relationship is entirely normal.

identity.title: Scheduled cancellation → revalidate at effective time → end or preserve
identity.purpose: Stop a scheduled end from executing against a relationship the counterparty has since chosen to keep.

requires: a scheduled termination whose effective time has arrived

nodes.headline: Scheduled cancellation effective time reached

Re-read the relationship from its authoritative current state, including its version. What is compared is the relationship as it is now against the version the cancellation was authorized against - not against the copy the scheduled job is carrying
Is the cancellation still valid against the relationship's current version?

Record the scheduled termination as suppressed, naming what superseded it. Executing it would end a relationship the counterparty has since chosen to keep, and they would find out by losing access to something they had just paid for
stale termination suppressed; the relationship continues on its current version
nodes.detail: a fresh cancellation against the current relationship is a new decision with its own effective end. The suppressed one stays in the record as something that was decided and then overtaken

nodes.headline: Determine what remains owed at the end - open fulfillment, unbilled usage, outstanding payments, commitments made while the relationship was active. This is established before the end rather than discovered after it

Record the terminal state the relationship's semantics define - ENDED, CANCELLED or EXPIRED. The whole history stays: every term, every renewal, every suspension and every price it ran at. A termination that deletes the relationship removes the answer to every question anyone will later ask about it
Relationship end → final reconciliation → former or expired state
nodes.detail: a scheduled termination executing against a still-valid cancellation

edges.label: Still valid
edges.when: nothing since the scheduling has superseded the decision to end

edges.label: Superseded
edges.when: a reactivation, resubscription, plan change or later renewal decision has overtaken it
a scheduled termination executing against a still-valid cancellation

distinctFrom.because: SUB-167 decides the end. This is the guard between that decision and its execution, months later, against a relationship that may have been renewed, upgraded or resubscribed in between.

guardrails: A scheduled cancellation is version-aware.
A reactivation, resubscription or change after scheduling invalidates the old cancellation.
Termination never deletes relationship history.
governance.reusableRule: Scheduled termination should execute only if the cancellation remains valid against the relationship's current authoritative version.
governance.entityScope: the continuing relationship and the scheduled termination standing against it
governance.entityNote: The termination carries the relationship version it was authorized against. Comparing that version against the current one is the whole job.

identity.title: Suspension or hold → restrict relationship → restore or end
identity.purpose: Hold a relationship in a state where it cannot operate normally and has not ended.

requires: an authoritative suspension or hold condition - financial, administrative, security, eligibility, operational or otherwise policy-defined
insufficientAlone: a risk signal, which is a reason to look rather than a decision to suspend
a single failed payment, which has its own recovery lifecycle before it reaches this one

nodes.headline: Relationship suspension condition

Record the reason, the scope, the effective time, what behaviour remains allowed, and the condition that would restore it. A suspension with no stated restoration condition has no way out, and becomes a termination nobody decided and nobody can point to
Does governing policy move the renewal or end dates during suspension?

Apply the adjustment policy defines, recording it as an adjustment with its basis rather than silently editing the term. The dates moved because a rule moved them, and the record has to say which rule

Leave the renewal and end dates where they are. Silently pushing them out extends a relationship nobody agreed to extend, and it surfaces months later as a charge the counterparty did not expect on a date they did not know about

Record SUSPENDED and raise whatever capability restriction the suspension calls for through the access lifecycle, which owns what is switched off and how. This journey owns the relationship's contractual state; suspended is not cancelled, and the relationship survives this entirely
until the suspension reason is resolved, or a terminal decision is taken on the relationship
nodes.detail: timeout after the maximum suspension duration policy defines

nodes.headline: Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a suspension reaching its maximum duration undecided

nodes.headline: How did the suspension resolve?

Re-read the relationship's current terms and rebuild capability from them. Restoring from a snapshot taken at suspension gives back an entitlement the relationship may no longer include - the plan may have changed, the term may have renewed at a different scope, and a suspension lasting months usually spans at least one of those
Does the relationship still exist and still support restoration?
Record ACTIVE again and raise the capability restoration through the access lifecycle, built from the relationship's current terms rather than from what it held before
restored to ACTIVE on current terms
nodes.detail: a further suspension is a new suspension with its own reason and its own restoration condition. The previous one stays in the record

nodes.headline: Relationship end → final reconciliation → former or expired state
nodes.detail: a suspended relationship that will not resume

edges.label: Policy moves them
edges.when: the terms explicitly extend or pause the relationship's dates while suspended

edges.label: Policy leaves them
edges.when: the terms say nothing about pausing, or explicitly keep the dates fixed

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the suspension reason is resolved, a terminal decision is taken on the relationship

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: an indefinite suspension is a termination without a decision. Reaching the limit forces the question rather than letting the relationship sit unusable and un-ended
a suspension reaching its maximum duration undecided

edges.label: The reason was resolved
edges.when: the stated restoration condition is authoritatively met

edges.label: A terminal decision was taken
edges.when: the relationship is to end rather than resume

edges.label: It does
edges.when: the relationship is intact and its current terms support resuming

edges.label: It does not
edges.when: the relationship ended, lapsed or expired while suspended
a suspended relationship that will not resume

distinctFrom.because: This is the commercial relationship's suspension state. ACC-78 is what happens to capability and access as a result. A relationship can be suspended for reasons that restrict nothing, and access can be suspended without the contract changing at all.

guardrails: Suspended is not cancelled.
A suspension never silently resets renewal or end dates unless governing policy explicitly does so.
Restoration uses current terms rather than a historical snapshot.
A suspension always states the condition that would restore it.
governance.reusableRule: Suspension temporarily limits a continuing relationship without ending it, while restoration depends on current valid relationship state.
governance.entityScope: the continuing relationship and the suspension standing against it
governance.entityNote: The relationship keeps existing, keeps its term and, unless policy says otherwise, keeps counting toward its own renewal.

identity.title: Relationship end → final reconciliation → former or expired state
identity.purpose: Stop what the relationship was granting, while everything it created keeps its own lifecycle.

requires: an authoritative end of a term-bearing continuing relationship taking effect, by cancellation, non-renewal, expiry, termination or lapse
insufficientAlone: a cancellation requested, which sets a date rather than reaching one
a payment failing, which may or may not ever become an ending
a structural relationship between the parties ending, which removes a link rather than a term

nodes.headline: Relationship end effective

Record the end reason, the effective end, the final term and the authority that ended it. Which of the five causes it was is kept - cancelled, not renewed, expired, terminated and lapsed mean different things to whoever reads this afterwards, and to what the counterparty can do next

Stop future relationship-dependent activity - scheduled renewals, recurring deliveries, upcoming charges, queued relationship-scoped communications. What stops is the future. Nothing already delivered or already owed is touched

Raise the entitlement withdrawal through the entitlement lifecycle rather than switching anything off here. Which rights survive an ending and which do not is a property of the entitlements themselves, and a relationship record deciding it locally will eventually disagree with the entitlement lifecycle about who can do what

Raise the wind-down each dependent area needs - deprovisioning, final billing, any refund or credit due, open fulfillment, and data retention where it applies. Each runs on its own lifecycle and reaches its own conclusion; none of them is implemented here
Do valid obligations created while the relationship was active remain?

Preserve those obligations and let them resolve on their own lifecycles. An order placed while the subscription was live is still owed, a refund still due is still due, and a dispute still open is still open. Ending stops future rights, and does not cancel commitments already made in either direction
Are the relationship-specific operational obligations complete?
until the relationship-specific wind-down completes
nodes.detail: timeout after the wind-down window

nodes.headline: Responsibility escalation → higher authority → resolution or return
nodes.detail: a relationship wind-down outliving its window

nodes.headline: Record the terminal relationship state its own semantics define - FORMER, EXPIRED or TERMINATED. This is the relationship ending. It is not the account closing and it is not the data being deleted; both of those are separate decisions, with their own authority and their own lifecycles, and neither follows from this one
FORMER, EXPIRED or TERMINATED; the account, the history and the surviving obligations all stand
nodes.detail: a new subscription, contract or membership is a new relationship rather than this one resuming. Its history remains readable, and everything it legitimately created during its term remains owed until its own lifecycle resolves it

edges.label: They remain
edges.when: open orders, unpaid amounts, refunds due, disputes or remedies created during the term are still live

edges.label: Nothing remains
edges.when: everything created during the term has already resolved

edges.label: Complete
edges.when: the wind-down this relationship itself required has finished

edges.label: Still running
edges.when: deprovisioning, final billing or another relationship-scoped wind-down is still in progress

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the relationship-specific wind-down completes

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: a relationship stuck mid-wind-down is neither active nor former, and everything downstream that asks which one it is gets no answer
a relationship wind-down outliving its window

distinctFrom.because: A subscription, contract or membership ends here. TRM-106 closes the account relationship entirely. Most people who leave a plan keep their account, and chaining the two treats cancelling a subscription as asking to be removed.

REL-93 ends a structural link between two entities, and what stops is what depended on the link existing. This ends a term, and what stops is what the term was granting. Someone can leave an organisation while the subscription they paid for personally keeps running, and a policy can expire while the person stays exactly as related to the organisation as before.

guardrails: A relationship ending is not an account closure.
A relationship ending is not data deletion.
A relationship ending is not the removal of a structural link. The parties can stay exactly as connected as they were, and unlinking them is a decision nobody made here.
A relationship ending never erases historical entitlements, payments or fulfilled obligations.
Commitments created while active are reconciled separately and can outlive the relationship.
governance.reusableRule: Ending a continuing relationship stops future relationship-dependent rights and obligations while preserving and resolving commitments legitimately created during the active term.
governance.entityScope: the ended continuing relationship and the state that depended on it
governance.entityNote: The relationship record survives its own ending. The end is a state it reaches, not a deletion of what it was. What ends here is a term. The structural links between the same parties are untouched by it, and removing one of those is a separate decision owned by REL-93.

identity.title: Deadline created → track → complete, escalate or expire
identity.purpose: Let a deadline govern the state of one obligation, rather than schedule messages around a date.

requires: a deadline assigned to a specific obligation by a system or rule entitled to set one
insufficientAlone: a reminder date configured in a messaging tool, which schedules communication rather than governing an obligation
an internal target with no consequence attached to missing it

nodes.headline: Authoritative deadline assigned

Store the deadline with its timezone where that changes the answer, its source, the obligation it governs, its owner, and what would count as completion. The completion condition is the load-bearing part - a deadline that cannot say what would satisfy it can only ever measure elapsed time
until the obligation is completed, or a defined pre-deadline threshold is reached
nodes.detail: timeout after the deadline itself

nodes.headline: Which happened?

Mark the obligation satisfied and invalidate every reminder and escalation still queued against it. A completed obligation is never reopened by a stale deadline job, which is the specific way a finished thing comes back to life
obligation satisfied before its deadline
nodes.detail: a new obligation carries its own deadline; this one is closed

nodes.headline: Is a pre-deadline reminder useful here, and does policy define one?
Send the reminder defined for this threshold. The reminder schedule is not the deadline and does not move it - a deadline nobody was reminded about is still the deadline
The deadline passed with the obligation open - what does the governing rule say happens?
Due-state change → recalculate priority → resolve or escalate
nodes.detail: an obligation surviving its deadline

nodes.headline: Responsibility escalation → higher authority → resolution or return
nodes.detail: a deadline whose governing rule escalates rather than changing the obligation

nodes.headline: Expiry reached → validate current state → expire, extend or replace
nodes.detail: a deadline at which the obligation itself ceases to be valid

nodes.headline: obligation failed at its deadline, as the rule defines
nodes.detail: a new attempt is a new obligation with its own deadline; this one records that it was not met

nodes.headline: deadline passed, obligation unchanged
nodes.detail: the obligation continues under whatever governs it - time passing did not decide anything here, which is the ordinary case and not an omission

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the obligation is completed, a defined pre-deadline threshold is reached

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the deadline is an absolute point, so this wait is bounded by it however many thresholds sit inside

edges.label: Completed
edges.when: the completion condition recorded with the deadline is satisfied

edges.label: Pre-deadline threshold
edges.when: a defined point before the deadline was reached with the obligation still open

edges.label: Send it
edges.when: policy defines a reminder at this threshold and the recipient can still act on it

edges.label: Nothing to send
edges.when: no reminder is defined, or nobody can do anything differently on hearing it

edges.label: OVERDUE
edges.when: the obligation survives its deadline and changes operational state

edges.label: ESCALATED
edges.when: the rule raises it rather than changing the obligation itself

edges.label: EXPIRED
edges.when: the obligation itself ceases to be valid at the deadline

edges.label: FAILED
edges.when: the rule explicitly defines missing this deadline as failure

edges.label: STILL_VALID
edges.when: the deadline was a target and passing it changes nothing about the obligation
an obligation surviving its deadline
a deadline whose governing rule escalates rather than changing the obligation
a deadline at which the obligation itself ceases to be valid

distinctFrom.because: A deadline is a moment by which something must be done. An expiry is a moment at which something stops being valid. The first can pass with the obligation intact; the second cannot.

guardrails: A deadline being reached is not failure unless the governing rule says so. Five different outcomes are available and only one of them is failure.
The reminder schedule is not the deadline. Moving a reminder does not move the obligation.
A completed obligation is not reopened by a stale deadline job.
Timezone is recorded wherever it changes which day the deadline falls on.
governance.reusableRule: A deadline should govern the state of a specific obligation rather than merely schedule communication around a date.
governance.entityScope: the obligation the deadline is attached to - a task, request, case or application
governance.entityNote: The deadline belongs to the obligation. Two obligations sharing a date are two deadlines, and one being met says nothing about the other.

identity.title: Due-state change → recalculate priority → resolve or escalate
identity.purpose: Change what an unresolved obligation costs operationally when it becomes due or overdue, rather than only announcing that it has.

requires: an obligation entering DUE_SOON, DUE or OVERDUE against a real deadline
insufficientAlone: a report showing an item as old, with no deadline behind it

nodes.headline: Due state changed
Read the obligation's current authoritative state now, rather than trusting the state it held when the timer was set
Has the obligation already been satisfied?
Suppress the stale due-state action. Becoming overdue changes nothing about an obligation that no longer exists
stale due-state action suppressed
nodes.detail: a genuinely open obligation crossing a due threshold enters properly

nodes.headline: Does this obligation have an owner?
Work created → routing → assignment
nodes.detail: an overdue obligation with nobody responsible for it

nodes.headline: Recalculate the obligation's operational priority, and notify only where a notification would change what someone does. The original deadline history is appended to rather than overwritten - what it was due by and what it became are two facts
Is a consequence defined for this obligation being overdue?
Responsibility escalation → higher authority → resolution or return
nodes.detail: an overdue obligation whose policy escalates it

nodes.headline: external:overdue-consequence
nodes.detail: an overdue obligation carrying a defined operational consequence

nodes.headline: overdue and tracked; no consequence defined
nodes.detail: resolution closes it and a further due threshold re-opens it. An overdue item with no defined consequence is a reporting fact, and inventing a consequence to have something to do with it is the failure this branch prevents

edges.label: Already done
edges.when: it was completed between the timer being set and firing

edges.label: Still open
edges.when: the obligation genuinely remains unresolved

edges.label: Owned
edges.when: an active owner is responsible for it

edges.label: Unowned
edges.when: no active owner holds it - which is why it went overdue
an overdue obligation with nobody responsible for it

edges.label: Escalation
edges.when: policy raises it to a level able to resolve it

edges.label: Restriction or failure
edges.when: policy applies a defined operational consequence to the entity itself

edges.label: None defined
edges.when: the obligation is simply overdue and no consequence attaches to that
an overdue obligation whose policy escalates it
an overdue obligation carrying a defined operational consequence

guardrails: The overdue state and its consequences are business-defined. Where no consequence exists, the item is tracked rather than acted on.
Not every overdue item requires customer communication. Most overdue work is an internal problem.
Due-state changes append to the deadline history rather than overwriting the original deadline.
governance.reusableRule: Becoming overdue changes the operational state of an unresolved obligation only when the underlying obligation still exists.
governance.entityScope: the obligation or work item whose due state changed
governance.entityNote: Due state is a property of the obligation, not of the person waiting on it. Overdue work does not automatically mean overdue communication.

identity.title: Expiry approaching → eligibility check → renew, complete or let expire
identity.purpose: Use the window before an expiry only where acting inside it could actually change what happens.

requires: a time-bound entity entering a pre-expiry window whose length reflects how long acting on it actually takes
insufficientAlone: a fixed interval applied to every entity type regardless of what renewal involves

nodes.headline: Pre expiry window entered
Re-read the entity's current state. The window opened on a schedule, and the entity may have been renewed, replaced or completed since that schedule was written
Has it already been renewed, replaced or completed?
pre-expiry journey suppressed; nothing is expiring
nodes.detail: the replacement entity has its own expiry and its own window

nodes.headline: Is an action available that would materially change the outcome?
Establish who is responsible for acting and what the action actually is. A pre-expiry message addressed to someone who cannot perform the renewal is a notification pretending to be a call to action
Is telling anyone useful even though nothing can be done?
Say what will happen and when, with no call to action attached - because there is no action. A prompt to act where acting is impossible is worse than silence
expiring, nothing to do and nothing worth saying
nodes.detail: the expiry itself is handled at the moment it arrives

nodes.headline: until renewed, or completed, or replaced
nodes.detail: timeout after the expiry moment

nodes.headline: Invalidate the expiry actions queued against the old validity, so a renewal granted today is not undone by an expiry scheduled yesterday
external:renewal-lifecycle
nodes.detail: an entity resolved before its expiry

nodes.headline: Expiry reached → validate current state → expire, extend or replace
nodes.detail: the window closing without resolution

edges.label: Already resolved
edges.when: the entity is no longer heading toward this expiry

edges.label: Still expiring
edges.when: the expiry still applies

edges.label: Action available
edges.when: renewal, completion or replacement is possible and someone can carry it out

edges.label: Nothing can be done
edges.when: the expiry will happen regardless - no renewal exists, or the decision is not the holder's to make

edges.label: Worth saying
edges.when: the holder needs to plan around it, or would otherwise be surprised

edges.label: Not worth saying
edges.when: nobody gains anything from knowing earlier

edges.label: on event
edges.when: renewed, completed, replaced

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the window closes at the expiry by definition; what happens then belongs to the expiry journey rather than to this one
an entity resolved before its expiry
the window closing without resolution

distinctFrom.because: This runs while the outcome can still change. TIM-64 runs at the moment it stops being able to. Keeping them apart is what makes expiring and expired different states rather than the same one announced twice.

guardrails: Expiring is not expired. Nothing in this journey applies an expiry consequence.
No expiry reminder is sent where no action is possible or useful. A prompt to act on something nobody can act on teaches people to ignore the ones that matter.
The pre-expiry window reflects how long the action genuinely takes, not a shared default.
governance.reusableRule: Pre-expiry orchestration should exist only when action before expiry can materially change the outcome.
governance.entityScope: the time-bound entity approaching expiry - a subscription, document, entitlement, credential, approval, reservation, benefit or agreement
governance.entityNote: One window per entity. A person holding three expiring credentials has three windows, and renewing one closes only its own.

identity.title: Expiry reached → validate current state → expire, extend or replace
identity.purpose: Check what the entity actually is at the moment the expiry fires, before applying anything the timer was written to apply.

requires: an authoritative expiry moment arriving for a time-bound entity

nodes.headline: Expiry time reached
Re-read the entity's current authoritative version at this moment. The timer holds the expiry that was true when it was written, which is not necessarily the expiry that is true now
What does the entity's current version say?
stale expiry suppressed; the entity had already moved
nodes.detail: the entity's current expiry, whatever it now is, has its own execution

nodes.headline: Adopt the new authoritative expiry and invalidate this one. An older timer never overrides a later extension - the extension was a decision and the timer is only a memory of an earlier one
expiry superseded by an extension
nodes.detail: the new expiry executes on its own terms when it arrives

nodes.headline: Transition the entity to EXPIRED, keeping the record of the period during which it was valid. Expired is a new state on the same entity, not the erasure of the old one. The transition is applied idempotently, so a redelivered job cannot expire it twice

Apply the consequences defined for this entity type - access ending, a reservation released, a benefit becoming unavailable, a credential invalid, renewal no longer possible, requalification required. The consequence belongs to the entity rather than to expiry in general, and expiring is not the same as revoking
Expired state → re-entry eligibility → renew, requalify or remain expired
nodes.detail: an entity having expired

edges.label: Already renewed or replaced
edges.when: the entity moved on and this expiry no longer describes it

edges.label: A later extension exists
edges.when: an authoritative extension moved the expiry past this moment

edges.label: Still valid, expiry applies
edges.when: the current version still carries this expiry
an entity having expired

guardrails: An old scheduled expiry never overrides a later extension.
The expired state preserves the previous validity history rather than replacing it.
Expiry consequences are entity-specific. Expired is not revoked, and neither is a synonym for the other.
The transition is idempotent; a redelivered job applies it once or not at all.
governance.reusableRule: Expiry must be evaluated against the entity's current authoritative version at the moment the transition executes.
governance.entityScope: the time-bound entity and the specific version of it the timer was scheduled against
governance.entityNote: The version binding is the point. A timer scheduled against one version firing against another is the defining failure of scheduled work.

identity.title: Grace period entry → temporary continuity → recover or terminate
identity.purpose: Keep limited continuity while something recoverable is unresolved, without pretending the normal active state still exists.

entry.trigger: Primary validity ended with grace policy
requires: primary validity ending, and a grace policy that applies to this entity type
insufficientAlone: an informal tolerance nobody wrote down, which is not grace but inconsistency

nodes.headline: Primary validity ended with grace policy

Record the grace start, its end, the reason, the recovery condition, and explicitly which capabilities continue and which are restricted. A grace state that does not say what still works is indistinguishable from active, which removes the only reason to have named it
until the recovery condition is satisfied
nodes.detail: timeout after the grace end recorded at entry

nodes.headline: Is the entity still eligible for the active state it would return to?
Restore the active state and lift the grace restrictions, recording that recovery happened within the window
recovered within grace; active state restored
nodes.detail: a further lapse enters grace again, and the history of how often that happens is itself worth reading

nodes.headline: Dynamic eligibility → eligible or ineligible → consequence
nodes.detail: recovery arriving after eligibility may have changed

nodes.headline: Grace ended unresolved - what does policy do?
Expiry reached → validate current state → expire, extend or replace
nodes.detail: grace ending with the entity due to expire

nodes.headline: external:termination-lifecycle
nodes.detail: grace ending with access or the relationship ending

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the recovery condition is satisfied

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: grace is bounded at the moment it is granted and does not extend itself - a grace period that quietly lengthens is an active state nobody approved

edges.label: Still eligible
edges.when: the conditions for the active state hold as they did before

edges.label: Eligibility has moved
edges.when: something changed during grace - a rule, a limit, an entitlement, a status
recovery arriving after eligibility may have changed

edges.label: The entity expires
edges.when: the time-bound entity itself ceases to be valid

edges.label: Access or the relationship ends
edges.when: policy terminates or further restricts rather than expiring an entity
grace ending with the entity due to expire
grace ending with access or the relationship ending

distinctFrom.because: Grace is a specific degraded continuity after validity ends, with a recovery condition. TIM-67 is the generic mechanism for any temporary state, most of which are not degradations of anything.

guardrails: Grace is not fully active. Anything reading the entity can tell which state it is in.
Which capabilities continue during grace is recorded explicitly, not inferred.
A grace period does not extend itself. Its end is fixed when it is granted.
Recovery rechecks current eligibility rather than blindly restoring the previous state.
governance.reusableRule: Grace periods preserve limited continuity while a recoverable condition remains unresolved, without pretending the normal active state still exists.
governance.entityScope: the subscription, account, entitlement or obligation whose primary validity ended
governance.entityNote: Grace is a state on the entity, with its own capability set. Anything reading the entity has to be able to tell grace from active, which is why the capabilities are recorded rather than assumed.

identity.title: Temporary exception → validity window → revert or formalise
identity.purpose: Stop an exception granted for a reason from becoming a permanent state nobody remembers deciding on.

requires: an exception granted by someone with authority to grant it, against a standing policy or state
insufficientAlone: a setting that differs from policy with no recorded authority behind it, which is configuration drift rather than an exception

nodes.headline: Temporary exception granted
Record the exception type, who authorised it, the reason, its scope, when it starts, and when it expires or is reviewed. An exception with no end date is a policy change that nobody approved as one
until the condition that justified the exception is resolved, or a permanent decision is made about it
nodes.detail: timeout after the exception's recorded expiry or review date

nodes.headline: What resolved it?
Approval request → review → approve, reject or request changes
nodes.detail: an exception that should become the rule

nodes.headline: At the review point, does an authoritative extension exist?

Adopt the extension as its own record, appended to the extension history, and close this instance. Each extension is counted separately rather than absorbed into one long-running exception - the count is what makes a temporary state that has run for two years visible as one
exception extended; a new window opens as its own instance
nodes.detail: the extension is a new instance with a new review date, so the number of extensions is countable rather than hidden inside a single record

nodes.headline: Revert to the standard state and mark the exception as no longer usable, so a stale process cannot keep relying on an exception that has ended
exception ended; standard state restored
nodes.detail: a new exception is granted on its own authority and its own reason

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the condition that justified the exception is resolved, a permanent decision is made about it

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the review is the mechanism - an exception that is never revisited is the one that becomes permanent by default

edges.label: No longer required
edges.when: the condition that justified the exception has gone

edges.label: Should become permanent
edges.when: the exception turned out to describe how things should work
an exception that should become the rule

edges.label: Extended
edges.when: someone with authority extended it, on the record

edges.label: Not extended
edges.when: no extension exists

distinctFrom.because: An exception departs from a standing policy and carries an authority who granted it. A temporary state is a lifecycle position; it does not necessarily contradict anything.

guardrails: A temporary exception is not indefinite permission. Its end is recorded when it is granted.
Extension history is preserved and countable. An exception extended repeatedly is visible as one.
An expired exception cannot be relied on by a stale process.
Making an exception permanent goes through approval, not through another extension.
governance.reusableRule: Temporary exceptions require explicit scope and exit conditions so that exceptional access or policy does not silently become permanent.
governance.entityScope: the exception itself - its scope, the authority that granted it and the state it departs from
governance.entityNote: Each grant and each extension is its own record. An exception extended four times is a different fact from one granted once, and only separate records make that countable.

identity.title: Temporary state → explicit expiry → restore or transition
identity.purpose: Give any time-bound state a defined ending, and revalidate before returning anything to what it was.

requires: an entity entering a state that is intended to end

nodes.headline: Temporary state entered
Does the temporary state carry an explicit expiry or an explicit exit condition?
Decision request → validate → route, reject or hold
nodes.detail: a temporary state created with no ending

nodes.headline: Record the temporary state, when it took effect, when it expires or what ends it, and the state it would return to
until the exit condition is satisfied
nodes.detail: timeout after the recorded expiry

nodes.headline: Record that the state ended by its exit condition rather than by expiry. A temporary access revoked early and one that lapsed are different facts about the same entity
Record that the state ended by reaching its expiry with the exit condition unmet

Re-read the entity's current version before returning it anywhere. The state it was going to return to may no longer exist, the entity may no longer be eligible for it, and the authority that granted the original may have ended during the temporary period
Is the previous state still valid to return to?
Restore the previous state and clear the temporary one
temporary state ended; previous state restored
nodes.detail: a further temporary state carries its own ending

nodes.headline: Dynamic eligibility → eligible or ineligible → consequence
nodes.detail: a temporary state ending with no valid state to return to

edges.label: Bounded
edges.when: an expiry time or a condition that ends it is defined

edges.label: Unbounded
edges.when: nothing says how or when it ends
a temporary state created with no ending

edges.label: on event
edges.when: the exit condition is satisfied

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: expiry is the backstop for a condition that may never be met; without it the state has no ending at all

edges.label: Still valid
edges.when: the previous state exists and the entity is still eligible for it

edges.label: No longer valid
edges.when: the previous state is gone, or eligibility for it has changed
a temporary state ending with no valid state to return to

guardrails: A temporary state without an expiry or an exit condition is raised rather than created. That is the state this journey exists to prevent.
The previous state is not assumed safe to restore. Eligibility and authority can both change during the temporary period.
How the state ended - early or by expiry - is recorded, because the two mean different things about the entity.
governance.reusableRule: Temporary states must define how they end; time-bound state without an exit rule is an unmanaged permanent state.
governance.entityScope: the entity plus the temporary state placed on it
governance.entityNote: Temporary access, a temporary restriction, a temporary role, a temporary allocation or configuration all share this shape, and each carries its own exit rule.

identity.title: Reversible state → reversal window → confirm or restore
identity.purpose: Undo a transition within its window while restoring only what is independently still valid.

requires: a transition that policy defines as reversible, with a reversal window
insufficientAlone: a change someone regrets, where no reversal policy exists

nodes.headline: Reversible transition occurred

Record the previous state, the new state, whether reversal is eligible, its deadline, and which side effects have already executed. That last list is the one that matters - a reversal decided without it either restores too little or promises too much
until a reversal is requested
nodes.detail: timeout after the reversal deadline

nodes.headline: reversal window closed; the new state is now the normal state
nodes.detail: changing it now is a new transition with its own reversal window, not an undo of this one

nodes.headline: Have irreversible side effects already occurred?
Remedy selection → resolve obligation → financial handoff if needed
nodes.detail: a reversal request against a transition with irreversible effects

nodes.headline: Restore the previous state, and only the previous state. Consent that was withdrawn, credentials that were revoked, tokens that expired, integrations that were cancelled and journeys that were queued and are now obsolete are each judged on their own current validity. Reversing a transition does not rewind the world around it, and restoring an entity wholesale resurrects things that ended for reasons this reversal never addressed
Recalculate the dependent state against what is actually valid now, rather than replaying what was valid before the transition
Could every dependent state be restored?
transition reversed; previous state fully restored
nodes.detail: a further transition on this entity carries its own window

nodes.headline: partially restored; some dependent state did not validly return
nodes.detail: recorded as partial rather than presented as though nothing had happened - what did not come back is nameable, which is the only way anyone can ask for it

edges.label: on event
edges.when: a reversal is requested

edges.label: on timeout
edges.when: the window closing is the ordinary outcome, and after it the new state is simply the state

edges.label: Something cannot be undone
edges.when: money moved, a message went out, an external system was told, a physical action happened

edges.label: Nothing irreversible
edges.when: everything the transition did can be safely unwound
a reversal request against a transition with irreversible effects

edges.label: Fully restored
edges.when: the previous state and everything depending on it are valid again

edges.label: Partially restored
edges.when: the primary state is back and some dependent state could not validly return

guardrails: Restoring an entity does not automatically restore withdrawn consent, revoked credentials, expired tokens, cancelled integrations or obsolete queued journeys. Each is evaluated on its own current validity.
Where irreversible side effects have run, the route is forward correction or compensation rather than restoration.
A partial restoration is recorded as partial.
governance.reusableRule: State reversal restores only what remains valid and reversible; it does not rewind every side effect created by the original transition.
governance.entityScope: the transition itself - what changed, when, and which of its side effects have already run
governance.entityNote: The side-effect list is what makes a later reversal decidable. Without it, reversing is a guess about what the original transition set in motion.

identity.title: Expired state → re-entry eligibility → renew, requalify or remain expired
identity.purpose: Decide how something expired can become valid again, through the mechanism that actually restores validity rather than by editing the expiry away.

requires: an action attempted against an expired entity, or an opportunity to restore it arising

nodes.headline: Re entry attempted or available

Establish what expiry actually did to this entity. Some expiries suspend, some invalidate, some end a relationship outright, and the route back differs for each - reading them all as the same lapse is what produces a renewal flow that cannot renew anything
Which mechanism restores validity here?
external:renewal-lifecycle
nodes.detail: an expired entity the governing system can renew in place

nodes.headline: Qualification state change → route, re-route or exit
nodes.detail: validity depending on conditions that have to be demonstrated again

nodes.headline: Create the replacement entity and keep the expired one as a distinct historical record. The two stay separately addressable, because questions asked later are about one or the other and almost never about both
replacement issued; expired entity retained as history
nodes.detail: the replacement carries its own validity and its own expiry

nodes.headline: expired, no route back
nodes.detail: none - what would have to change is the rule or the entity's circumstances, and either produces a new entity rather than reviving this one

edges.label: Direct renewal
edges.when: the governing system supports renewing this entity in place

edges.label: Requalification
edges.when: validity depends on conditions that must be demonstrated again

edges.label: Replacement
edges.when: the expired entity cannot become valid and a new one has to be issued

edges.label: Prohibited
edges.when: nothing restores validity - the expiry was terminal by design
an expired entity the governing system can renew in place
validity depending on conditions that have to be demonstrated again

guardrails: An expired entity is not made active by editing its expiry timestamp, unless the governing system explicitly supports extension as a mechanism.
The expired entity and its replacement remain distinguishable.
The expired validity period is preserved. The gap during which nothing was valid is itself a fact.
governance.reusableRule: Re-entry after expiry should follow the business mechanism that restores validity rather than silently undoing the expiry.
governance.entityScope: the expired entity, kept distinct from any replacement created for it
governance.entityNote: The expired entity and its replacement are two objects. That a credential was valid until March and that a credential is valid now are different facts, and merging them destroys both.

identity.title: Scheduled future transition → validate at execution → apply, cancel or recalculate
identity.purpose: Treat a scheduled transition as an intention recorded in the past, and check it against the present before applying it.

requires: a state transition scheduled for a future moment against a specific entity

nodes.headline: Future transition scheduled

Persist the target entity, the state and version it is expected to be in, the target state, when it takes effect, and why it was scheduled. Recording the expected version is what makes execution-time validation possible at all - without it there is nothing to compare the present against
until the schedule is cancelled, or the schedule is replaced by a newer one
nodes.detail: timeout after the effective moment

nodes.headline: Invalidate this job. A cancelled or replaced schedule must not still fire - a replacement that leaves the original alive applies both, in whichever order the scheduler happens to run them
schedule cancelled or replaced before its effective moment
nodes.detail: the replacing schedule, if there is one, runs as its own instance

nodes.headline: Re-read the entity's authoritative current state and version. The schedule is an intention recorded in the past, and this is the only moment at which it can be checked against the present
Does the entity still match what the schedule expected?
stale transition suppressed; a newer change already applied
nodes.detail: an old schedule never overwrites a newer decision, whichever of the two the scheduler happens to reach first

nodes.headline: external:rescheduling-decision
nodes.detail: a schedule whose underlying assumptions no longer hold

nodes.headline: Has this transition already been applied?
duplicate execution absorbed
nodes.detail: schedulers retry by design, so absorbing a redelivery is the normal case rather than an error path
